label: lem:adelic-explicit-intertwiner
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every \(g\in G\), the normalized intertwiner is \[ D_g=\begin{pmatrix}\lambda_g&8\rho_2(g)\\0&1\end{pmatrix}. \] In particular \(D_g=I\) whenever \(\lambda_g=1\) and \(\rho_2(g)=0\).

label: lem:adelic-corrected-frames
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The formulas \begin{equation} T_g=q(A_g)^{-1}D_g,\qquad W_g=q(\beta_g)^{-1}D_g\qquad(g\in M_0) \label{eq:adelic-corrected-frames} \end{equation} define continuous homomorphisms $T:M_0\to N_3(4)$ and $W:M_0\to N_4(4)$.

label: lem:adelic-kernel-normality
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The joint kernel of $T,W$ in $M_0$ is normal in $\mathcal G$.

label: prop:adelic-cm-images
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The full division fields are \[ \mathbb Q(E_j[\mathrm{tors}])=K_j^{\mathrm{ab}}. \] On $H^{\mathrm{cyc}}$, one has \begin{equation} \rho_4(H^{\mathrm{cyc}})=N_4(4),\qquad \rho_3^{\circ}(H^{\mathrm{cyc}})=N_3(4),\qquad \rho_3^{\circ}=\kappa\rho_3. \label{eq:adelic-arithmetic-projections} \end{equation} The representations $\rho_3^{\circ}$ and $\rho_3$ have the same kernel on $H^{\mathrm{cyc}}$.

label: lem:adelic-cm-entanglement
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The intersection of the two full division fields is \begin{equation} K_3^{\mathrm{ab}}\cap K_4^{\mathrm{ab}} =\mathbb Q^{\mathrm{ab}}(3^{1/4}). \label{eq:adelic-cm-intersection} \end{equation} In the representations of Proposition~\ref{prop:adelic-cm-images}, the joint image of $H^{\mathrm{cyc}}$ is exactly $\mathcal E$.

label: prop:adelic-signed-path-comparison
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Choose the Tate-module bases by transport along paths to the harmonic and equianharmonic fibres of the Legendre family. For $\sigma\in H^{\mathrm{cyc}}$ one then has the exact integral identities \begin{equation} W_\sigma=\rho_4(\sigma),\qquad T_\sigma=\rho_3^{\circ}(\sigma) =\kappa(\sigma)\rho_3(\sigma). \label{eq:adelic-signed-path-comparison} \end{equation} In particular $(T,W)(H^{\mathrm{cyc}})=\mathcal E$.

label: thm:adelic-frame-elimination
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Put $G_1=G\cap M_0$. Then \begin{equation} (T,W)(G_1)=(T,W)(H^{\mathrm{cyc}})=\mathcal E. \label{eq:adelic-gt-arithmetic-image} \end{equation} In particular, the closed normal subgroup \begin{equation} C_{\mathrm{CM}}= \ker\bigl((T,W):G_1\longrightarrow N_3(4)\times N_4(4)\bigr) \label{eq:adelic-cm-kernel} \end{equation} satisfies \begin{equation} G=C_{\mathrm{CM}}H,\qquad C_{\mathrm{CM}}\cap H= G_{K_3^{\mathrm{ab}}K_4^{\mathrm{ab}}}. \label{eq:adelic-cm-normalization} \end{equation} The inclusion of $H$ induces the canonical isomorphism \begin{equation} G/C_{\mathrm{CM}}\simeq \operatorname{Gal}(K_3^{\mathrm{ab}}K_4^{\mathrm{ab}}/\mathbb Q). \label{eq:adelic-cm-arithmetic-quotient} \end{equation} Every continuous abelian character of $G$ that is zero on $H$ and whose restriction to $G_1$ factors through $(T,W)$ is zero.

label: thm:all-cm-original-restriction
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The original quadratic restriction maps satisfy \begin{equation} \ker\bigl(X_2\to H^1(R_{\rm all},\mathbb F_2)^G\bigr) =\ker\bigl(X_2\to H^1(V_{\rm all},\mathbb F_2)^G\bigr) =\mathcal S. \label{eq:all-cm-original-kernel} \end{equation} There are canonical maps \begin{equation} B(V_{\rm all})_{\max2} \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }B(R_{\rm all})_{\max2} \twoheadrightarrow B_{\max2}. \label{eq:all-cm-relative-surjection} \end{equation} The last map is a surjection; an isomorphism is not asserted. Moreover, \[ R_{\rm all}/V_{\rm all} \simeq R_{\rm quad}/V_{\rm quad}, \] and this isomorphism preserves the image of the arithmetic intersections.

label: prop:all-cm-intrinsic-extension
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let \(\kappa:R_{\rm all}\to\mathbb F_2\) be continuous, \(G\)-invariant, and zero on \(R_{\rm all}\cap H\). There is a central relative obstruction \[ o_2(\kappa)\in H^2(C,D_0;\mathbb F_2). \] If it vanishes, there is a conjugation obstruction \[ o_1(\kappa)\in H^1_{\rm cont}\!\left(G/R_0,\ \operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cont}(C/D_0,\mathbb F_2)\right). \] The character extends to a continuous character of \(G\) which is zero on \(H\) if and only if both obstructions vanish. When it exists, the extension is unique. Characters on \(V_{\rm all}\) satisfy the same criterion after their unique coprime extension to \(R_{\rm all}\).

label: thm:all-odd-cross-cup-lifts
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every distinct pair of odd primes \(\ell,q\), there is a continuous \(G_0\)-invariant homomorphism \[ \xi_{\ell,q}:M_0\to\mathbf F_2 \] whose transgression on \(\lambda(G_0)\), pulled back from the finite cyclotomic quotient, is \begin{equation} e_{c_\ell,c_q} =c_\ell c_q+ h_\ell(\ell^*,q^*)\delta_\ell+ h_q(\ell^*,q^*)\delta_q. \label{eq:all-odd-cross-cup-1} \end{equation} Thus every such class has zero inflation to full profinite GT. The restriction of \(\xi_{\ell,q}\) to \(G_K\), for \(K=\mathbf Q(\mu_\infty,2^{1/\infty})\), is exactly the arithmetic basis character \(\kappa_{\ell,q}\) transgressing to \eqref{eq:all-odd-cross-cup-1}. In particular all the odd-prime-pair axes of the complete arithmetic target lie in the image of \(X_2\). The characters indexed by \(\{a,c_p\}\) are not covered by this theorem.

label: lem:relative-proodd-restriction
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let \(G=QH\), where \(Q\) is a closed normal subgroup of the profinite group \(G\) and \(H\) is closed. Let \(E\subset Q\) be closed and normal in \(G\), and suppose that \(Q/E\) is pro-odd. For every finite abelian \(2\)-group \(A\), restriction induces a bijection \[ \begin{aligned} \{\chi\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cts}(G,A):\chi|_H=0\} &\longrightarrow\\ &\{\psi\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cts}(E,A)^G: \psi|_{E\cap H}=0\}. \end{aligned} \] All maps on the left are continuous homomorphisms. In particular there is a canonical isomorphism \[ \left(Q/\overline{[G,Q](Q\cap H)}\right)_{\max2} \ \simeq\ \left(E/\overline{[G,E](E\cap H)}\right)_{\max2}. \] No containment \(Q\cap H\subset E\) is required.

label: thm:all-prime-residual-quadratic-domain
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The subgroups \(P_D,T_D\) are closed and normal in \(G\). Both \(R_D/P_D\) and \(R_D/T_D\) are pro-odd. Consequently \[ \begin{aligned} B_{\max2}&\simeq \left(P_D/\overline{[G,P_D](P_D\cap H)}\right)_{\max2}\\ &\simeq \left(T_D/\overline{[G,T_D](T_D\cap H)}\right)_{\max2}. \end{aligned} \] Restriction from \(X_2(N)\) to either \(P_D\) or \(T_D\) has the same kernel as restriction to \(R_D\), namely \[ \left(\bigoplus_{q\ {\rm odd\ prime}}\mathbf F_2\psi_q\right) \oplus\mathbf F_2\eta_3. \] These assertions concern the maximal pro-two relative quotient; they do not assert \(G=P_DH\) or \(G=T_DH\).

label: prop:all-prime-residual-strictness
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Both \(P_D\) and \(T_D\) have infinite index in \(R_D\). Moreover \(T_D\) has infinite index in \(R_D\cap\ker d_{(3)}\).

label: prop:arithmetic-kummer-kernel-axes
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let \(G=\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}\), let \(H\) be its arithmetic subgroup, and put \[ M=\ker\lambda,\qquad N=\ker(\lambda,\rho_2^I). \] \[ D=\bigcap_{q\ {\rm prime}}\ker(\rho_q^I|_M), \] \[ R_M=\{g\in M:f_g=1\text{ in the free pro-two group}\}. \] For every odd rational prime \(q\), there is an element \(k_q\in R_M\cap N\cap H\) whose only nonzero rational Kummer coordinate is \[ \rho_{q,2}^I(k_q)=-2. \] In particular the tuple of dyadic odd-prime coordinates on the closed arithmetic subgroup of \(R_M\cap N\) killing every odd-primary Kummer coordinate has image exactly \begin{equation} \prod_{q\ {\rm odd}}2\mathbf Z_2. \label{eq:arithmetic-kernel-axes-1} \end{equation} If \(G=DH\), and \(R_D=R_M\cap D\), the natural map \[ (R_M\cap N)/R_D\longrightarrow N/D \] is an isomorphism. If, in addition, \(M=R_M(M\cap H)\), then \[ D=R_D(D\cap H),\qquad G=R_DH. \]

label: thm:main-full-quadratic-target
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: With \(A=G/N=H/(H\cap N)\), transgression is an isomorphism \[ \operatorname{tr}:Y_2\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \ker\bigl(H^2(A,\F_2)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Br}(\Q)[2]\bigr). \] There is a direct-sum decomposition \[ Y_2=\F_2\eta_3 \oplus\bigoplus_{p\text{ odd}}\F_2\psi_p \oplus\bigoplus_{p\text{ odd}}\F_2\kappa_{2,p} \oplus\bigoplus_{\substack{p<q\\p,q\text{ odd}}}\F_2\kappa_{p,q}, \] where \(\eta_3=m_3/8\bmod2\), with \(m_3(g)=[S^2T]f_g\) in the expansion \(x=1+S,y=1+T\), is the cubic character and the additional basis characters are uniquely specified by \begin{align*} \operatorname{tr}(\kappa_{2,p}) &=\operatorname{Inf}_U^A \bigl(ac_p+\varepsilon_p(\delta_2+\delta_p)\bigr),\\ \operatorname{tr}(\kappa_{p,q}) &=\operatorname{Inf}_U^A \bigl(c_pc_q+\ell_p(q^*)\delta_p+\ell_q(p^*)\delta_q\bigr). \end{align*} All products are cup products, and every character is a finite sum. The character \(\kappa_{5,29}\) is realized by the central quadratic layer of \[ \Q\bigl(\sqrt5,\sqrt{29},\sqrt{7+2\sqrt5}\bigr) /\Q(\sqrt5,\sqrt{29}), \] restricted to \(G_{K_2}\). It is nonzero and independent of \(\eta_3\) and the \(\psi_p\).

label: thm:main-full-odd-target
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every odd prime \(p\), inflation \(H^r(U,\F_p)\to H^r(A,\F_p)\) is an isomorphism in every degree. The arithmetic images of the \(\delta_\ell\) form a basis of \(H^2(H,\F_p)\). Put \(a_\ell=(\ell-1)/p^{v_p(\ell-1)}\bmod p\), and define \begin{align*} D_{\ell m}&=a_\ell^{-1}\gamma_m(\ell)\delta_\ell -a_m^{-1}\gamma_\ell(m)\delta_m\quad(\ell<m),\\ D_{0\ell}&=-a_\ell^{-1}\gamma_0(\ell)\delta_\ell. \end{align*} Here Frobenius acts by the positive power map. Transgression identifies \(Y_p\) with \[ \ker\bigl(H^2(A,\F_p)\longrightarrow H^2(H,\F_p)\bigr), \] and its inverse images of \(\gamma_i\smile\gamma_j-D_{ij}\), for \(i<j\) in \(\{0\}\cup\mathcal S_p\), form a basis of \(Y_p\). Every character is a finite sum of these basis elements.

label: prop:arithmetic-affine
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The subgroup $N$ is closed and normal in $G$, and $N\cap H=K$. The map $(\lambda,\rho _2)$ identifies $G/N$ with \[ A=\{(a,r)\in U\ltimes\widehat{\mathbb Z}: r\bmod 2=\epsilon _8(a)\}, \qquad (a,r)(b,s)=(ab,r+as). \] This identifies $G/N$ canonically with $\operatorname{Gal}(K_2/\mathbb Q)$. In particular $\rho _2\bmod 2=\epsilon _8\circ\lambda$ on $G$.

label: prop:arithmetic-commutators
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $T=\{(1,2t):t\in\widehat{\mathbb Z}\}\subset A$. Then \[ \overline{[A,A]}=T,\qquad \overline{[A,T]}=\{(1,4t):t\in\widehat{\mathbb Z}\}. \] Every finite $p$-group quotient of $A$ is abelian when $p$ is odd. Every finite quotient of $A$ which is a $2$-group of nilpotency class at most two has commutator subgroup of order at most two.

label: lem:character-gluing
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $G=NH$ be a profinite group with $N$ closed and normal and $H$ closed, and put $K=N\cap H$. Let $M$ be a finite abelian group with trivial action. An invariant character $\psi:N\to M$ and a character $\eta:H\to M$ extend to a character of $G$ if and only if $\psi|_K=\eta|_K$. The extension is unique and is given by \[ \chi(nh)=\psi(n)+\eta(h). \]

label: thm:abelian-splitting
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There is a canonical isomorphism of profinite abelian groups \[ G^{\mathrm{ab}}\simeq U\times B \] under which the multiplier is the first projection. Moreover \[ C_N=N\cap\overline{[G,G]},\qquad B\simeq\bigl(G/\overline{\langle\!\langle H\rangle\!\rangle}\bigr)^{\mathrm{ab}}. \] For every prime $p$, put \[ X_p=H^1(N,\mathbb F_p)^G, \qquad r_p:X_p\longrightarrow H^1(K,\mathbb F_p). \] Restriction gives canonical identifications \begin{align*} \ker r_p&\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cts}}(B,\mathbb F_p),\\ H^1(G,\mathbb F_p)&\simeq \lambda^*H^1(U,\mathbb F_p)\oplus\ker r_p. \end{align*} Consequently $\ker r_p=0$ if and only if every continuous $\mathbb F_p$-character of $G$ factors through the multiplier. The multiplier identifies $G^{\mathrm{ab}}$ with $U$ if and only if $N\subset\overline{[G,G]}$, and this holds if and only if $\ker r_p=0$ for every prime~$p$.

label: prop:transgression-comparison
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The transgression $d_H:Y_p\to H^2(A,\mathbb F_p)$ is injective and identifies $Y_p$ with \[ \ker\bigl(H^2(A,\mathbb F_p)\longrightarrow H^2(H,\mathbb F_p)\bigr). \] There is an exact sequence \[ 0\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cts}}(B,\mathbb F_p) \longrightarrow X_p \xrightarrow{\ d_Hr_p\ } \ker\bigl(H^2(A,\mathbb F_p)\longrightarrow H^2(G,\mathbb F_p)\bigr) \longrightarrow0. \] Thus, under the injection $d_H$, the image of restriction is precisely the inflation kernel for~$G$.

label: thm:arithmetic-target-dimension
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every prime $p$, \[ \dim_{\mathbb F_p}H^1(G_{K_2},\mathbb F_p)^{G_{\mathbb Q}}=\aleph_0. \] For $p=2$, an explicit independent family is given, for the odd rational primes $q$, by the quadratic extensions $K_2(q^{1/4})/K_2$. Equivalently these are the Kummer classes of $\sqrt q$ in $K_2^\times/(K_2^\times)^2$.

label: lem:ihara-cocycle
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For $g,g'\in\GTz$, \[ \rho_d^I(gg')=\rho_d^I(g)+\lambda(g)\rho_d^I(g'). \] If $n\in N$, then \[ \rho_d^I(gng^{-1})=\lambda(g)\rho_d^I(n). \]

label: lem:cyclic-cover-symmetry
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $F=\widehat F_2=\langle x,y\rangle$. Suppose a continuous automorphism $\phi$ satisfies \[ \phi(x)=x,\qquad \phi(y)=f^{-1}yf,\qquad f\in\overline{[F,F]}, \] and $\phi(xy)$ is conjugate to $xy$. For a positive integer $n$, use the free basis \[ X=x^n,\qquad Y_j=x^jyx^{-j}\quad(0\leq j<n) \] of $H_n$. If $[f]=a[X]+\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}c_j[Y_j]$ in $H_n^{\mathrm{ab}}$, then \[ a=0,\qquad \sum_{j=0}^{n-1}c_j=0,\qquad c_j=c_{-j\bmod n}\quad(0\leq j<n). \]

label: thm:all-kummer-parity
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every positive integer $d$, Ihara's integral Kummer cocycle is even on the multiplier-one subgroup of the gentle group: \[ \rho_d^I\bigl(\ker(\lambda:\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}_0\to U)\bigr) \subset2\widehat{\mathbb Z}. \] On the whole gentle group it satisfies \[ \rho_d^I\bmod2=\epsilon_d\circ\lambda, \] where $\epsilon_d:U\to\mathbb F_2$ is the additive quadratic Dirichlet character of $\mathbb Q(\sqrt d)$.

label: thm:quadratic-dimension
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The vector space of invariant continuous quadratic characters of the normalized subgroup has dimension \[ \dim_{\mathbb F_2}H^1(\Lambda_0,\mathbb F_2)^{\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}} =\aleph_0. \] For every positive integer $d$ the formula \[ \psi_d^N=\frac{\rho_d^I|_N}{2}\bmod2 \] defines a continuous invariant quadratic character. For the odd rational primes $q$, the characters $\psi_q^N$ are linearly independent and restrict to the characters of $K_2(q^{1/4})/K_2$. Thus \[ \dim_{\mathbb F_2}\operatorname{im}r_2=\aleph_0. \] More precisely, for distinct odd primes $q_1,\ldots,q_m$, let $R:N\to\mathbb Z_2^m$ be the vector of the $2$-adic components of $\rho_{q_1}^I,\ldots,\rho_{q_m}^I$. Then \[ R(K)=R(N)=2\mathbb Z_2^m, \] and restriction is injective on the $m$-dimensional character space obtained by pullback from this lattice.

label: prop:163-circular-unit-saturation
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There is an isomorphism \[ C/\{\pm1\}\simeq \mathbf Z^{81}/\mathbf Z(1,\ldots,1) \] which sends the \(k\)-th standard vector to \(\epsilon_k\). The classes of \(U_0,U_1,U_2\) in \(C/(\{\pm1\}C^2)\) span the irreducible two-dimensional \(\mathbf F_2[C_3]\)-module; their sole linear relation is \[ [U_0]+[U_1]+[U_2]=0. \] In particular none of the \(U_i\) is a square modulo sign of a circular unit. Let \(v_i=s^i(5+\theta_1)\), with the period notation of Lemma~\ref{lem:163-period-unit-square}. Then \(U_i=-v_i^2\), and \[ C^*=\langle C,v_0,v_1,v_2\rangle\subset\mathcal E, \qquad C^*/C\simeq\mathbf F_2^2. \] The quotient has the same nontrivial irreducible \(C_3\)-action. No assertion that \(C^*=\mathcal E\) is made.

label: lem:finite-cyclic-principal-gamma
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let \(p\) be odd and let \(b:\mathbf F_p\times\mathbf F_p\to1+2O\) be a normalized two-cocycle for the additive group \(\mathbf F_p\), with trivial action on the coefficient group. There is a unique function \(\gamma:\mathbf F_p\to1+2O\), with \(\gamma(0)=1\), such that \[ b(a,b)=\frac{\gamma(a)\gamma(b)}{\gamma(a+b)}. \] Explicitly, \[ \gamma(a)=\left(\prod_{c\in\mathbf F_p}b(a,c)\right)^{1/p}, \] where the \(p\)-th root is the unique root in the pro-two group \(1+2O\).

label: prop:163-mixed-beta-residual
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For \(r\in R_{\rm global}\), the principal ratio \(k_r^+\) belongs to \(P=P_{163}\), and \[ k_r^+\bmod QP=h_{163}(r)\bmod QP. \] Consequently the mixed ratio retains exactly the original degree--163 alternative. With \(n=2^{81}+1\) and the first-layer detector \(\Psi:P\to W\) of \eqref{eq:163-trace-detector}, \begin{equation} \Psi(k_r^n)=\Psi(h_{163}(r)). \label{eq:163-mixed-ratio-detector} \end{equation} The expression on the left is defined because \(k_r^n\) is principal and belongs to \(P\).

label: lem:163-mobius-period-fiber
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The three units satisfy \[ v_iv_{i+1}=v_i-1,\qquad v_{i+1}=1-v_i^{-1}\quad(i\bmod3), \] and are the roots of \[ X^3-14X^2+11X+1. \] In particular they lie in the fiber above \(14\) of the degree-three quotient map \[ J(v)=\frac{v^3-3v+1}{v^2-v} \] for the order-three transformation \(v\mapsto1-v^{-1}\). The discriminant of the polynomial is \(163^2\).

label: prop:163-binary-tetrahedral-lift
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The following conditions are equivalent. \begin{enumerate} \item Some continuous, \(G\)-invariant \(\kappa:J\to\mathbf F_2\), zero on \(J\cap H\), has nonzero central relative obstruction \(o_2(\kappa)\). \item There is a continuous homomorphism \(\widetilde\pi:G\to\widetilde A_4\) such that \(p\widetilde\pi=\pi\) and \(\widetilde\pi(H)\) lies in the displayed \(C_3\). \item The pullback of \(\widetilde A_4\to A_4\) by \(\pi\), equipped with its canonical splitting over \(H\), is split as a relative central extension of \((G,H)\). \end{enumerate} Every homomorphism in condition two is surjective and has \(\widetilde\pi(H)=C_3\). When such homomorphisms exist, their set is a torsor under the continuous quadratic characters of \(G\) which vanish on \(H\).

label: prop:cm163-full-image-dichotomy
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The full images \(h_{163}(\mathcal R)\) and \(h_{163}(\mathcal V)\) coincide. There are precisely two possibilities. \begin{enumerate} \item Their common image is \(A\). The groups \(\mathcal R'=\mathcal R\cap\ker h_{163}\) and \(\mathcal V'=\mathcal V\cap\ker h_{163}\) then give a further arithmetic normalization \(G=\mathcal R'H\). The full relative abelian quotient on \(\mathcal R'\), its maximal pro-\(2\) quotient on \(\mathcal V'\), and the exact original quadratic restriction kernel and image are unchanged. \item Their common image is \(P\). There is a continuous surjection \(G\longrightarrow A_4\) whose restriction to \(H\) has image a subgroup of order three. \end{enumerate} In the second case the displayed finite quotient has zero relative quadratic character space.

label: prop:163-finite-word-detector
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The elements \(X,Y\) generate \(\mathscr D\), so they define one finite quotient of \(\widehat F_2\), of order \(163\cdot4^{162}\). For every \(r\in R\), use the conjugator \(f_{r^n}\) of the group power \(r^n\), in the convention \[ \phi_f(x)=x,\qquad \phi_f(y)=f^{-1}yf,\qquad [x,y]=xyx^{-1}y^{-1}. \] Then \begin{equation} \prod_{j=0}^{26}f_{r^n}(X^{a_j},Y^{a_j}) =\bigl(2d^{-2}\Psi(h_{163}(r)),1\bigr) \quad\text{in }\mathscr D. \label{eq:163-exact-word-value} \end{equation} In particular, \begin{equation} \prod_{j=0}^{26}f_{r^n}(X^{a_j},Y^{a_j})=1 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad h_{163}(r)\in A. \label{eq:163-word-equivalence} \end{equation} The word value lies in \(2d^{-2}W\), a subgroup of order four.

label: prop:163-relative-cohomology
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There are natural identifications, relative to the displayed stable decomposition, \[ H^1(P,A;\mathbb F_2)=U, \] \begin{equation} H^2(P,A;\mathbb F_2) \simeq\operatorname{Quad}(E,\mathbb F_2) \oplus \operatorname{Bil}(E\times(L_{79}/2L_{79}),\mathbb F_2). \label{eq:163-relative-forms} \end{equation} The latter space has dimension \(161\). Inversion acts trivially on it, and \begin{equation} H^2(P,A;\mathbb F_2)^{C_{162}} =\mathbb F_2\,\mathfrak q. \label{eq:163-quaternion-line} \end{equation} Here \(\mathfrak q\) is the pullback of \(Q_8\to E\simeq\mathbb F_4\) along \(P\to E\), with its canonical splitting over \(A\). Its quadratic form is \(q(z)=z^3\). This class is fixed by every automorphism of the pair \((P,A)\).

label: prop:163-two-stage-extension
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For \(\kappa\in\mathscr X(J)\) there is a linear central obstruction \[ o_2(\kappa)\in H^2(P,A;\mathbb F_2)^{C_{162}} =\mathbb F_2\,\mathfrak q. \] If it vanishes, there is a second obstruction \[ o_1(\kappa)\in H^1_{\rm cont}(\Gamma,U), \qquad\Gamma=G/R,\quad U=(P/A)^\vee. \] A continuous character of \(G\), zero on \(H\), extends \(\kappa\) if and only if both obstructions vanish. When it exists, this extension is unique. Thus restriction from the original relative quadratic character space to \(\mathscr X(J)\) is injective, with image precisely the characters passing these two tests.

label: prop:163-central-obstruction-model
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The quaternion class can obstruct extension in a profinite group with the stated integral pair and cyclotomic action.

label: lem:163-period-unit-square
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let \(H_0=\langle8\rangle\subset(\mathbb Z/163)^\times\), and put \[ \theta_i=\sum_{a\in2^iH_0}\zeta_{163}^a,\qquad i=0,1,2. \] Then \begin{equation} \prod_{j=0}^{26} (\zeta_{163}^{8^j}+\zeta_{163}^{-8^j}) =-(5+\theta_1)^2. \label{eq:163-period-square} \end{equation} The element \(5+\theta_1\) is a real unit. The two conjugate identities hold for the other two cosets.

label: thm:163-exact-arithmetic-image
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: After imposing any collection of the scalar kernels \(h_q\) with \(q\ne163\), the degree-\(163\) arithmetic images of the resulting \(R\)- and \(V\)-groups are both exactly \[ Q_{163}P_{163},\qquad [P_{163}:Q_{163}P_{163}]=4. \] This is an unconditional integral image statement.

label: lem:163-integral-pair-decomposition
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There is a cyclotomic-stable decomposition \[ P=B_2\oplus L_{79},\qquad QP=2B_2\oplus L_{79}, \qquad \operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Z_2}B_2=2,\quad \operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Z_2}L_{79}=79. \] Moreover, if \(t=-s\) acts on the additive \(\mathbb Z_2\)-lattice \(P\), then \(P\) is a free rank-one \(\mathbb Z_2[C_{81}]\)-module.

label: prop:cm-class-number-determinant
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Multiplication by \(Q_p\) on \(R_p\) has positive determinant \[ \det(Q_p\mid R_p)=\frac{h_p^-}{p} \begin{cases} (2^{d/2}+1)^r,&d\ \text{even},\\ (2^d-1)^{r/2},&d\ \text{odd}. \end{cases} \] Consequently the determinant is nonzero for every \(p\), and \[ v_2\bigl(\det(Q_p\mid R_p)\bigr)=v_2(h_p^-). \] The operator \(Q_p\) is a unit in \(\mathbf Z_2[s]/(s^h+1)\) if and only if \(h_p^-\) is odd, equivalently if and only if the class number of \(\mathbf Q(\zeta_p)\) is odd.

label: thm:163-concrete-odd-inertia
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every \(j\ge0\), \begin{equation} H^j_{\rm cont}(\Gamma,U)=0. \label{eq:163-concrete-cohomology-vanishing} \end{equation}

label: cor:163-single-extension-obstruction
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Suppose \(h_{163}(R)=P\), and put \(J=\ker(h_{163}:R\to P)\). For \(\kappa\in\mathscr X(J)\), the second obstruction \(o_1(\kappa)\) of Proposition~\ref{prop:163-two-stage-extension} is always zero whenever it is defined. The character \(\kappa\) extends to a continuous character of \(G\) vanishing on \(H\) if and only if \[ o_2(\kappa)=0 \quad\text{in }\mathbb F_2\,\mathfrak q. \] When it exists, this extension is unique. Equivalently, restriction identifies \begin{equation} \operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cts}(B,\mathbb F_2) \simeq \ker\bigl(o_2:\mathscr X(J)\longrightarrow \mathbb F_2\,\mathfrak q\bigr). \label{eq:163-remaining-relative-obstruction} \end{equation}

label: prop:cm-relative-product-cohomology
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There is a natural isomorphism \begin{equation} H^2_{\rm cont}(C,D;k) \simeq \bigoplus_{i\in I}H^2_{\rm cont}(C_i,D_i;k) \ \oplus\!\!\bigoplus_{i<j}K_{ij}. \label{eq:cm-relative-product-cohomology} \end{equation} It is equivariant for every group acting continuously and coordinatewise on the pairs. The first coordinates are restrictions to individual pairs. The mixed coordinate of a relative central extension is the commutator pairing between its two indicated coordinate subgroups. All sums are algebraic direct sums, so a class has finite coordinate support.

label: thm:cm-cross-prime-central
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Under these hypotheses, \begin{equation} H^2_{\rm cont}(C,D;k)^{\mathcal G} \simeq \bigoplus_{i\in I} H^2_{\rm cont}(C_i,D_i;k)^{\mathcal G}. \label{eq:cm-prime-central-invariants} \end{equation} The isomorphism is restriction; its inverse is the finite sum of coordinate pullbacks. No assertion that the individual invariant groups vanish is part of the theorem.

label: cor:cm-individual-central-obstructions
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Restriction induces an isomorphism \[ H^2_{\rm cont}(C,D_0;\mathbf F_2)^G \simeq \bigoplus_{p\in\mathcal I} H^2_{\rm cont}(C_p,D_p;\mathbf F_2)^G. \] Every intrinsic relative central obstruction in Theorem~\ref{thm:all-cm-central-extension} has only finitely many nonzero individual-prime components and has no mixed component. The corresponding character extends to a continuous character of \(G\) vanishing on \(H\) if and only if all its individual-prime components vanish. Such an extension is unique.

label: prop:cm-exact-first-layer
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: With every finite sign subgroup included, \[ [P:QP]=[T:QT]=2^{v_2(D)+t},\qquad v_2(D)\ge b. \] The natural reduction \[ \alpha:T\longrightarrow \mathscr M,\qquad \alpha(u)=\frac{u-1}{2}\pmod{2O} \] induces a surjection \(T/QT\to \mathscr M/\overline QM\). It is an isomorphism if and only if \(t=0\) and \(v_2(D)=b\). The logarithmic convention \[ \alpha_{\log}(u)=\frac{\log u}{2}\pmod{2O} \] induces a map between the same quotients and has exactly the same isomorphism criterion.

label: thm:omitted-prime-vanishing
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Suppose \(G=R_\Lambda H\), and let \(p\ge5\) be a prime outside \(\Lambda\). Let \(W\) be a finite abelian \(2\)-primary \(G/R_\Lambda\)-module whose action factors through \[ G/R_\Lambda\xrightarrow{\lambda\bmod p} (\mathbb Z/p)^\times=\langle s_p\rangle. \] If \(s_p-1\) is bijective on \(W\), then \begin{equation} H^j_{\rm cont}(G/R_\Lambda,W)=0 \qquad(j\ge0). \label{eq:omitted-prime-cohomology} \end{equation}

label: lem:all-cm-isolated-axes
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: If \(i_p:P_p\to\prod_{q\in\mathcal I}P_q\) denotes inclusion in the \(p\)-coordinate, then \[ i_p(Q_pP_p)\subseteq D_0\subseteq C. \] In particular \(Q_pP_p\subseteq D_p\) and \(Q_pC_p\subseteq D_p\).

label: prop:all-cm-exact-products
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every set \(\mathcal I\) of primes at least five, \begin{equation} C=\prod_{p\in\mathcal I}C_p,\qquad D_0=\prod_{p\in\mathcal I}D_p. \label{eq:all-cm-exact-products} \end{equation} Consequently \[ C/D_0\simeq\prod_{p\in\mathcal I}C_p/D_p. \] These statements require no CM-unit or finite-index hypothesis.

label: lem:all-cm-coordinate-module
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Each \(U_p\) is finite, and \(s_p-1\) is bijective on it.

label: cor:all-cm-conjugation-vanishing
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: With its discrete conjugation action, \(U\) is a continuous \(\Gamma_0=G/R_0\)-module, and \begin{equation} H^j_{\rm cont}(\Gamma_0,U)=0 \qquad(j\ge0). \label{eq:all-cm-conjugation-cohomology} \end{equation}

label: thm:all-cm-central-extension
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For \(\kappa\in\mathscr X(J)\), the central extension \(R_0/\ker\kappa\to C\), with its prescribed arithmetic splitting over \(D_0\), defines a continuous relative class \[ o_2(\kappa)\in H^2_{\rm cont}(C,D_0;\mathbb F_2) \] when \(\kappa\ne0\); set \(o_2(0)=0\). The assignment \(o_2\) is \(\mathbb F_2\)-linear. The character \(\kappa\) extends to a continuous character of \(G\) vanishing on \(H\) if and only if \(o_2(\kappa)=0\). When it exists, this extension is unique. Equivalently, restriction identifies \begin{equation} \operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cont}(B,\mathbb F_2) \simeq \ker\bigl(o_2:\mathscr X(J)\longrightarrow H^2_{\rm cont}(C,D_0;\mathbb F_2)\bigr). \label{eq:all-cm-central-kernel-identification} \end{equation}

label: thm:113-global-saturation
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: After any collection of the other-prime scalar kernels, the degree-\(113\) images of \(R_{\rm quad}\), \(V_{\rm quad}\), and their arithmetic intersections are all \(P\). In particular degree \(113\) can be added to the previously normalized primes \(29\) and \(\Pi\), preserving the full relative quotient on the \(R\)-group, its maximal pro-\(2\) quotient on the \(V\)-group, and the original quadratic restriction kernel \(\mathcal S\) and full relative image. The new scalar kernel has infinite index on both groups.

label: thm:global-frobenius-29
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: All four images are the whole target: \[ \mathfrak h_{29}(\mathcal R_\Pi)=\mathfrak h_{29}(\mathcal R_\Pi\cap H) =\mathfrak h_{29}(\mathcal V_\Pi)=\mathfrak h_{29}(\mathcal V_\Pi\cap H)=P. \] In this inert case \(P\simeq\mathbf Z_2^{14}\). For \[ \mathcal R_{\Pi,29}=\mathcal R_\Pi\cap\ker\mathfrak h_{29},\qquad \mathcal V_{\Pi,29}=\mathcal V_\Pi\cap\ker\mathfrak h_{29}, \] one has \(G=\mathcal R_{\Pi,29}H\). Both new kernels have infinite index, with exact quotient \(P\), already on their arithmetic intersections. They preserve respectively the full relative quotient \(B\) and its maximal pro-two quotient. The original invariant quadratic-character restriction kernel remains exactly \(\mathcal S\), and its image on either new kernel is exactly the invariant quadratic characters killing the arithmetic intersection, canonically \(\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cts}(B,\mathbf F_2)\).

label: thm:simultaneous-global-cm-normalization
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let \(\Pi_{\rm global}\) be the set of primes \(p\geq5\) such that \(Q_p(1)\) is odd, the natural first-layer map \eqref{eq:uniform-natural-layer} is a finite isomorphism, and \(\mathscr K_p\) is injective. Define \[ R_{\rm global}=R_{\rm quad}\cap \bigcap_{p\in\Pi_{\rm global}}\ker h_p,\qquad V_{\rm global}=V_{\rm quad}\cap R_{\rm global}. \] Then the joint images of \(R_{\rm quad}\), \(V_{\rm quad}\), \(R_{\rm quad}\cap H\), and \(V_{\rm quad}\cap H\) are all \[ \mathcal P=\prod_{p\in\Pi_{\rm global}}P_p, \] including every finite sign subgroup. Consequently, \begin{equation} R_{\rm quad}/R_{\rm global}\simeq\mathcal P,\qquad V_{\rm quad}/V_{\rm global}\simeq\mathcal P,\qquad G=R_{\rm global}H, \label{eq:uniform-global-factorization} \end{equation} and inclusion induces an isomorphism \begin{equation} R_{\rm global}/V_{\rm global} \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }R_{\rm quad}/V_{\rm quad} \label{eq:uniform-proodd-identification} \end{equation} which preserves the image of the arithmetic intersections. In particular the quotient in \eqref{eq:uniform-proodd-identification} is pro-odd. The relative quotients satisfy \begin{equation} B(R_{\rm global})\simeq B,\qquad B(V_{\rm global})_{\max2}\simeq B_{\max2}. \label{eq:uniform-relative-quotients} \end{equation} The original restrictions of \(X_2\) to both new groups have kernel exactly \(\mathcal S\), and image all continuous \(G\)-invariant quadratic characters which vanish on the corresponding arithmetic intersection. The older unit set \(\Pi\) and the primes \(29,113\) belong to \(\Pi_{\rm global}\), whereas \(163\) does not. No infinitude assertion about \(\Pi_{\rm global}\) is needed.

label: lem:uniform-operator-inverses
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Under \eqref{eq:uniform-natural-layer}, inclusion identifies \(P/QP\) with \(T/QT\). On this quotient both \(s-1\) and \(1+[2]\) are automorphisms.

label: thm:uniform-arithmetic-cm-image
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let \(R_\Lambda\) and \(V_\Lambda\) be obtained from \(R_{\rm quad}\) and \(V_{\rm quad}\) by imposing any collection of the scalar kernels \(h_q\) with \(q\ne p\). Under \eqref{eq:uniform-natural-layer}, their arithmetic images are \begin{equation} h_p(R_\Lambda\cap H)=h_p(V_\Lambda\cap H) =\{v\in P:\ell(v\bmod QP)=0\text{ for every } \ell\in\ker\mathscr K\}. \label{eq:uniform-arithmetic-image} \end{equation} In particular, \[ [P:h_p(R_\Lambda\cap H)]=2^{\dim\ker\mathscr K},\qquad \dim_{\mathbb F_2}\bigl(h_p(R_\Lambda\cap H)/QP\bigr) =\dim\operatorname{im}\mathscr K. \] Every value in \eqref{eq:uniform-arithmetic-image} has a witness in \(V_{\rm quad}\cap H\) with all other prime scalar coordinates equal to \(1\).

label: prop:odd-inertia-vanishing
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let \(R\subseteq L\) be closed normal subgroups of a profinite group \(G\), and put \(\Gamma=G/R\). Assume \(C=L/R\) is a central pro-\(2\) subgroup of \(\Gamma\). Let \(a\in G\) have pro-odd procyclic closure, and assume its closed normal closure in \(G/L\) is pro-odd. If \(U\) is a finite continuous \(2\)-primary \(\Gamma\)-module with \(U^a=0\), then \[ H^j_{\rm cont}(\Gamma,U)=0\qquad\text{for every }j\ge0. \]

label: thm:coefficient-two-cross-cups
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every odd prime \(p\), there is a continuous \(G\)-invariant homomorphism \[ \xi_{2,p}:M\longrightarrow\mathbf F_2 \] whose restriction to \(N\) transgresses to \begin{equation} e_{a,c_p}=a c_p+A_p(\delta_2+\delta_p) \quad\hbox{in }H^2(A,\mathbf F_2). \label{eq:coefficient-two-cross-1} \end{equation} In particular \eqref{eq:coefficient-two-cross-1} has zero inflation to \(G\), and \begin{equation} \xi_{2,p}|_{G_{K_2}}=\kappa_{2,p}, \label{eq:coefficient-two-cross-2} \end{equation} where \(\kappa_{2,p}\) is the unique arithmetic target character transgressing to \eqref{eq:coefficient-two-cross-1}. The character is obtained from the action on compact homology, modulo eight, of the degree-\(p\) cyclic cover of the three-punctured sphere with monodromies \(1,1,-2\). The same construction is defined and invariant on the multiplier-one subgroup of any group of continuous positive peripheral automorphisms of \(\widehat F(x,y)\). The transgression assertion above concerns specifically the full quotient \(G/N=A\).

label: lem:two-norm-one-coinvariants
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let \(L/\mathbf Q_2\) be unramified of degree \(2s\), with integer ring \(O\), arithmetic Frobenius \(\sigma\), and involution \(\bar z=\sigma^s(z)\). Let \(O_0\) be the fixed integer ring, and put \[ T_s=\{z\in O^\times:z\bar z=1\}. \] There is a canonical isomorphism of finite groups \begin{equation} \mathcal D_s: \mathbf Z_2^\times/(\mathbf Z_2^\times)^2 \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } T_s/(\sigma-1)T_s, \qquad t\longmapsto\left[\frac{\sigma(v)}v\right], \qquad v\bar v=t. \label{eq:coefficient-two-cross-6} \end{equation} Here \((\sigma-1)T_s=\{\sigma(z)/z:z\in T_s\}\). Define \[ \alpha_s=a\circ\mathcal D_s^{-1},\qquad \beta_s=b\circ\mathcal D_s^{-1}. \] For \(z\in T_s\cap(1+4O)\), \begin{equation} \alpha_s(z)= \operatorname{Tr}_{\mathbf F_{2^s}/\mathbf F_2} \left(\frac{\log z}{4}\bmod2\right), \qquad \beta_s(z)=0. \label{eq:coefficient-two-cross-7} \end{equation} Moreover \begin{equation} \alpha_s(-1)=1, \qquad \beta_s(-1)=s\pmod2. \label{eq:coefficient-two-cross-8} \end{equation} If \(v\bar v=-1\), then \begin{equation} \alpha_s(v^2)=1, \qquad \beta_s(v^2)=0. \label{eq:coefficient-two-cross-9} \end{equation} In \eqref{eq:coefficient-two-cross-9}, the square belongs to \(T_s\); the values are independent of the choice of \(v\).

label: cor:all-arithmetic-quadratic-targets-lift
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The arithmetic restriction map is surjective: \[ X_2=H^1(N,\mathbf F_2)^G \longrightarrow Y_2=H^1(G_{K_2},\mathbf F_2)^H. \] Consequently the established structural sequence becomes \begin{equation} 0\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cont}} (B,\mathbf F_2) \longrightarrow X_2\longrightarrow Y_2\longrightarrow0. \label{eq:coefficient-two-cross-23} \end{equation} This does not determine the left-hand term.

label: prop:common-cover-homology-countermodel
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every odd prime \(p\), the degree-four cyclic cover with monodromies \((1,2)\) and the degree-\(p\) cyclic cover with monodromies \((1,1)\) have a common degree-\(4p\) cover. Its compact genus is \(2p-1\), and it has four punctures. There is an automorphism of its full profinite integral first homology which commutes with the deck group, preserves the intersection form, fixes every peripheral homology class, and is compatible with pushforward and transfer to both smaller covers. It induces the identity on the full integral homology of the degree-\(p\) cover, but has nontrivial harmonic quadratic sign at coefficient \(p\) on the degree-four cover. In particular it is the identity at coefficient two.

label: thm:companion-kummer-equality
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every odd prime \(p\), on the entire multiplier-one subgroup \(M\) of full profinite GT one has \begin{equation} \boxed{\quad \widetilde\psi_p(g)=\frac{\rho_p^I(g)}2\pmod2. \quad} \label{eq:companion-kummer-24} \end{equation} More generally, the equality holds for standard positive peripheral automorphisms \(x\mapsto x\), \(y\mapsto f^{-1}yf\), with \(f\in F'\), satisfying the two-cycle relation and the integral Anderson duplication identity. No duplication identity is assumed for a larger gentle group unless it has been separately established.

label: lem:companion-first-layer
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let \(O\) be unramified of degree \(2s\) over \(\mathbf Z_2\), with Frobenius \(\sigma\), involution \(\bar z=\sigma^s z\), and norm-one group \(T_s\). The companion character is \(\beta_s(z)=b(v\bar v)\) when \(z=\sigma(v)/v\); Hilbert 90 permits a unit \(v\), and its relative norm is rational. Another such unit differs by a rational unit, changing this norm by a square, so the value is well-defined. On the first principal-unit layer it is \begin{equation} \beta_s(z)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathbf F_{2^s}/\mathbf F_2} \left(\frac{z-1}{2}\bmod2\right) \qquad(z\in T_s\cap(1+2O)). \label{eq:companion-kummer-26} \end{equation} For an unramified extension of odd degree \(d\), \begin{equation} b(N_{O/\mathbf Z_2}z) =\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathbf F_{2^d}/\mathbf F_2} \left(\frac{z-1}{2}\bmod2\right) \qquad(z\in1+2O). \label{eq:companion-kummer-27} \end{equation}

label: lem:cyclic-kummer-fourier
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let \(g\in M\) be a standard positive peripheral automorphism as in Theorem~\ref{thm:companion-kummer-equality}. In \(\mathbf Z_2[C_p]=\mathbf Z_2[X]/(X^p-1)\), put \[ C_{p,g}(X)=(X-1)R_g(X,1)=\sum_{j=0}^{p-1}c_jX^j. \] Then \begin{equation} C_{p,g}(1)=0,\qquad C_{p,g}(X^{-1})=C_{p,g}(X), \qquad \rho_{p,2}^I(g)=-c_0. \label{eq:companion-kummer-28} \end{equation} If \(\mathcal S\) contains one representative from each reciprocal pair of nontrivial \(p\)-th roots of unity, then the sum \[ S_{p,g}=\sum_{\zeta\in\mathcal S}C_{p,g}(\zeta) \] belongs to \(\mathbf Z_2\), independently of those representatives, and \begin{equation} \frac{\rho_{p,2}^I(g)}2=-\frac{S_{p,g}}p. \label{eq:companion-kummer-29} \end{equation}

label: cor:cubic-two-lifts-equal
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let \(\tau\) be the earlier coefficient-two cubic frame character. Then on all of \(M\), \begin{equation} \xi_{2,3}=\tau+\psi_3. \label{eq:companion-kummer-33} \end{equation} Thus the difference between these two lifts of \(\kappa_{2,3}\) vanishes on full GT.

label: prop:harmonic-two-geometric-lifts
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The transgression of \(\vartheta_{p,4}\) on \(G/N=A\) is \begin{equation} e_{b,c_p}=b c_p+\frac{p-1}{2}\delta_p. \label{eq:companion-kummer-34} \end{equation} Thus the existing harmonic relative character is exactly \begin{equation} \Xi_{p,4} =\vartheta_{p,4}-\widetilde\psi_p \quad\hbox{on }N. \label{eq:companion-kummer-35} \end{equation} Its vanishing on full GT is equivalent to equality of these two geometric lifts of \eqref{eq:companion-kummer-34}. No vanishing or nonvanishing assertion for \eqref{eq:companion-kummer-35} is made here.

label: thm:main-complete-quadratic

statement:
For every odd prime \(p\), there is a continuous invariant character \(\xi_{2,p}:M	o\F_2\), determined by compact homology modulo eight of the degree-\(p\) cyclic cover with monodromies \(1,1,-2\), such that \(
u_p=\xi_{2,p}|_N\in X_2\) and \[ \operatorname{tr}(
u_p) =\operatorname{Inf}_U^A  igl(ac_p+\varepsilon_p(\delta_2+\delta_p) igr), \qquad 
u_p|_K=\kappa_{2,p}. \] The character is defined for every positive peripheral action with the hypotheses of Theorem~ef{thm:main-odd-pair-lifts}. Consequently the original quadratic restriction is surjective, with an explicit linear section: \[ 0\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{m cts}(B,\F_2) \longrightarrow X_2\xrightarrow{\ \mathrm{res}\ }Y_2 \longrightarrow0. \] One section sends the basis elements \(\eta_3,\psi_p,\kappa_{2,p}, \kappa_{\ell,q}\) to \(\eta_3,\psi_p,
u_p,\xi_{\ell,q}\), respectively, with \(\ell<q\). The companion character of the same integral homology construction satisfies \[ \widetilde\psi_p=ho_p^I/2\pmod2 \quad	ext{on }M	ext{ for every odd }p. \] At \(p=3\), the lift \(

label: thm:complete-quadratic-restriction
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Restriction \(X_2\to Y_2\) is surjective. The exact sequence \[ 0\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cts}(B,\F_2) \longrightarrow X_2\xrightarrow{\ \mathrm{res}\ }Y_2 \longrightarrow0 \] has an explicit \(\F_2\)-linear section \(s\), given on the arithmetic basis by \[ \begin{aligned} s(\eta_3)&=\eta_3,& s(\psi_p)&=\psi_p,\\ s(\kappa_{2,3})&=\tau|_N+\psi_3,& s(\kappa_{2,p})&=\nu_p\quad(p\ne3),\\ s(\kappa_{\ell,q})&=\xi_{\ell,q}\quad(\ell<q\text{ odd}). \end{aligned} \] Thus, putting \(\mathcal S=s(Y_2)\), \[ X_2=\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cts}(B,\F_2)\oplus\mathcal S, \qquad \mathcal S\xrightarrow{\ \mathrm{res}\ }Y_2 \text{ is an isomorphism}. \] This does not determine \(\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cts}(B,\F_2)\).

label: cor:full-quadratic-inflation-kernel
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The two quadratic inflation kernels on the arithmetic quotient agree: \[ \ker\bigl(H^2(A,\F_2)\to H^2(G,\F_2)\bigr) =\ker\bigl(H^2(A,\F_2)\to\operatorname{Br}(\Q)[2]\bigr). \]

label: thm:complete-quadratic-normalization
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The joint map \((\nu_p)_{p\in\mathcal J}:R^*\to\mathcal Q\) is onto already on \(R^*\cap H\), and also on \(V^*\cap H\). Its full and arithmetic kernels are the corresponding intersections with \(R_{\rm quad}\). In particular \[ R^*/R_{\rm quad}\simeq V^*/V_{\rm quad}\simeq\mathcal Q, \qquad G=R_{\rm quad}H. \] Moreover \[ \begin{aligned} B&\simeq R_{\rm quad}/ \overline{[G,R_{\rm quad}](R_{\rm quad}\cap H)},\\ B_{\max2}&\simeq \left(V_{\rm quad}/ \overline{[G,V_{\rm quad}](V_{\rm quad}\cap H)}\right)_{\max2}. \end{aligned} \] The full joint quotients, also on arithmetic intersections, are \[ R_D/R_{\rm quad}\simeq V_D/V_{\rm quad} \simeq\mathcal U\times\mathcal P\times\mathcal Q. \] The kernel of restriction from \(X_2\) to either residual subgroup is exactly \(\mathcal S=s(Y_2)\). Its image is exactly the space of invariant quadratic characters on that subgroup vanishing on its arithmetic intersection, canonically identified with \(\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cts}(B,\F_2)\).

label: thm:five-twenty-nine-cross-cup-lift
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There is a continuous \(G_0\)-invariant homomorphism \begin{equation} \xi_{5,29}:M_0\longrightarrow\mathbf F_2 \label{eq:cross-cup-5-29-2} \end{equation} whose restriction to \(G_K\), for \(K=\mathbf Q(\mu_\infty,2^{1/\infty})\), is precisely the central quadratic character \(\kappa_{5,29}\) of \[ \mathbf Q\!\left(\sqrt5,\sqrt{29},\sqrt{7+2\sqrt5}\right). \] In particular its restriction to \(N=\ker(\lambda,\rho_2)\subset G\) belongs to \(X_2=H^1(N,\mathbf F_2)^G\), and its arithmetic restriction is outside the span of the rational quartic Kummer characters and \(\eta_3\). Equivalently, the corrected cross-cup class \begin{equation} e_{c_5,c_{29}}=c_5\cup c_{29} \label{eq:cross-cup-5-29-3} \end{equation} has zero inflation to \(H^2(G,\mathbf F_2)\). The construction uses the homology modulo twenty-nine of a cyclic degree-five cover, and applies already to \(G_0\).

label: lem:five-cover-similitude
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The vector space \(V\) has dimension four and carries a nondegenerate alternating form. The induced representation \begin{equation} \rho:G_0\longrightarrow \operatorname{GSp}(V) \label{eq:cross-cup-5-29-6} \end{equation} has similitude multiplier \(\lambda_g\bmod29\). If \(D\) is the deck transformation induced by conjugation by \(x\), then \begin{equation} \rho(g)D\rho(g)^{-1}=D^{\lambda_g\bmod5}. \label{eq:cross-cup-5-29-7} \end{equation} The characteristic polynomial of \(D\) on \(V\) is \(1+X+X^2+X^3+X^4\).

label: lem:finite-cross-cup-extension
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The subgroup \(\ker\chi\) is normal in \(E\), and \begin{equation} 1\longrightarrow C_2\longrightarrow E/\ker\chi \longrightarrow C_4\times\mathbf F_{29}^\times \longrightarrow1 \label{eq:cross-cup-5-29-14} \end{equation} is a central extension with class \(x\cup y\). Here \(x\) is the nonzero quadratic character of \(C_4\), and \(y\) is the quadratic character of \(\mathbf F_{29}^\times\).

label: cor:cross-cup-strict-normalization
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The subgroups in \eqref{eq:cross-cup-5-29-19} are closed and \(G\)-normal, and \begin{equation} [R_D:R_D^\xi]=[V_D:V_D^\xi]=2,\qquad G=R_D^\xi H. \label{eq:cross-cup-5-29-20} \end{equation} The maximal pro-two relative quotient is unchanged on passage to \(V_D^\xi\): \begin{equation} B_{\max2}\simeq \left( V_D^\xi/ \overline{[G,V_D^\xi](V_D^\xi\cap H)} \right)_{\max2}. \label{eq:cross-cup-5-29-21} \end{equation} If the established kernel of restriction from \(X_2\) to \(H^1(V_D,\mathbf F_2)\) is the span of the rational Kummer characters and \(\eta_3\), then the kernel of restriction to \(H^1(V_D^\xi,\mathbf F_2)\) is exactly that span plus the independent character \(\xi_{5,29}|_N\). No factorization \(G=V_D^\xi H\) is asserted.

label: prop:cross-cup-residual-inertia
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Choose pro-two elements \(\tau_5\in I_5\) and \(\tau_{29}\in I_{29}\) of arithmetic inertia with \(c_5(\tau_5)=c_{29}(\tau_{29})=1\). Then \[ w=[\tau_5,\tau_{29}] \] belongs to \(V_D\cap H\). In fact every rational Kummer coordinate, every free pro-\(p\) action, and both complete corrected CM frames vanish on \(w\). The character \(\kappa_{5,29}\) of \[ \mathbf Q(\sqrt5,\sqrt{29},\sqrt{7+2\sqrt5}) \] has value one on \(w\).

label: lem:fr-cubic-two-character
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The logarithm identifies \(\mathcal U\) with \(4\delta\mathbf Z_2\). The formula \[ \tau(g)=\frac{\log\mathfrak t_2(g)}{4\delta}\pmod2 \qquad(g\in M) \] defines a continuous homomorphism \(M\to\mathbf F_2\), invariant under conjugation by all of \(G\). Equivalently, \[ \mathfrak t_2(g)\equiv(1+4\tau(g))I\pmod8. \] Its kernel in \(\mathcal U\) is \(\mathcal U^2\). An element of \(\mathcal U\) with \(\tau=1\) topologically generates \(\mathcal U\).

label: lem:fr-cubic-two-arithmetic-bit
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The restriction of \(\tau\) to \(D\cap H\) is nonzero. There is, on the other hand, an element \(k_0\in D\cap H\) with \[ \eta_3(k_0)=1,\qquad \tau(k_0)=0. \]

label: thm:fr-cubic-two-exact-image
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The full and arithmetic coefficient-two images are \[ \boxed{\quad \mathfrak t_2(R_D) =\mathfrak t_2(R_D\cap H) =\mathcal U. \quad} \] In particular the upper image is the entire level-four norm-one group, rather than just its square subgroup. For \[ R'=R_D\cap\ker\mathfrak t_2 \] one has \[ R_D/R'\simeq\mathcal U\simeq\mathbf Z_2,\qquad G=R'H,\qquad B\simeq R'/\overline{[G,R'](R'\cap H)}. \] Thus \(R'\) is a proper closed normal subgroup of infinite index in \(R_D\), and it preserves the full relative abelian obstruction.

label: cor:fr-cubic-two-joint-gate
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let \[ V_D= \bigl(D\cap\bigcap_p\ker\Phi_p\cap\ker d_{(3)}\bigr) \cap\ker W_{\mathrm{odd}}\cap\ker T_{\mathrm{odd}}, \qquad V'=V_D\cap\ker\mathfrak t_2. \] Then \[ \mathfrak t_2(V_D)=\mathfrak t_2(V_D\cap H)=\mathcal U, \qquad [V_D:V']=[V_D\cap H:V'\cap H]=\infty, \] and \[ B_{\max2}\simeq \left(V'/\overline{[G,V'](V'\cap H)}\right)_{\max2}. \] If \(X_2=H^1(N,\mathbf F_2)^G\), its exact restriction kernels to \(R'\) and to \(V'\) are both \[ \boxed{\quad \left(\bigoplus_{q\ \mathrm{odd}}\mathbf F_2\psi_q\right) \oplus\mathbf F_2\eta_3\oplus\mathbf F_2(\tau|_N). \quad} \] The last summand is independent of all preceding summands.

label: prop:fr-cubic-two-Y2-class
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: One has the exact equality of arithmetic characters \[ \tau|_{G_{K_2}}=\kappa_{2,3}+\psi_3. \] Consequently \[ \vartheta_{2,3}:=\tau|_N+\psi_3\in X_2 \] is an explicit invariant lift of the corrected cross-cup target \(\kappa_{2,3}\). The last summand in Corollary~\ref{cor:fr-cubic-two-joint-gate} can equivalently be written \(\mathbf F_2\vartheta_{2,3}\). Neither character is asserted to be arithmetic-trivial.

label: lem:integral-alternating-cubic
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $f$ be a pro-$2$ commutator word satisfying \[ f(y,x)f(x,y)=1,\qquad f(z,x)f(y,z)f(x,y)=1,\qquad z=(xy)^{-1}. \] Set $a=[S^2T]f$ and $A=[S^2T^2S]f$. Then \begin{equation}\label{eq:alternating-cubic-identity} [STS]f=-2a,\qquad [ST^2S]f=a,\qquad [STSTS]f=-2a-4A. \end{equation} In particular, $[STSTS]f\equiv2a\pmod4$.

label: prop:cubic-magnus-eight
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: One has \[ m_3(N)\subseteq8\mathbf Z_2. \] Consequently \[ \eta_3:N\longrightarrow\mathbf F_2, \qquad \eta_3(g)=m_3(g)/8\pmod2 \] is an ordinary continuous $G$-invariant quadratic character.

label: lem:rho2-cubic-modfour
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every multiplier-one gentle element, \[ \rho_2^I(g)\equiv-2m_3(g)\pmod4 \] in the $2$-adic coordinate.

label: prop:cubic-arithmetic-witness
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There exists $k\in K_{\mathrm{rad}}$ such that \[ m_3(k)\in8\mathbf Z_2^\times. \] In particular, $\eta_3|_{K_{\mathrm{rad}}}\ne0$, so $\eta_3$ is independent of every character generated by rational Kummer coordinates. Moreover, \[ m_3(D)=m_3(K_{\mathrm{rad}})=8\mathbf Z_2. \]

label: cor:cubic-radical-normalization
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Define \[ D_3=N_{\mathrm{rad},3}=D\cap\ker m_3, \qquad K_{\mathrm{rad},3}=K_{\mathrm{rad}}\cap\ker m_3. \] Then $D_3$ is a proper closed normal subgroup of $G$, and \[ D=D_3K_{\mathrm{rad}},\qquad G=D_3H,\qquad D_3\cap H=K_{\mathrm{rad},3}. \] Writing \[ B=N/\overline{[G,N]K},\qquad K=N\cap H, \] the previously obtained radical normalization refines canonically to \[ B\simeq D/\overline{[G,D]K_{\mathrm{rad}}} \simeq D_3/\overline{[G,D_3]K_{\mathrm{rad},3}}. \] If $L_3=\overline{\mathbf Q}^{\,K_{\mathrm{rad},3}}$, then $\operatorname{Gal}(L_3/L)\simeq\mathbf Z_2$. This defines the arithmetic extension by the explicit cubic monodromy coordinate; no radical formula for $L_3$ is asserted.

label: cor:cubic-radical-joint-image
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The map \[ N\longrightarrow \left(\prod_{q\text{ odd prime}}2\widehat{\mathbf Z}\right) \times8\mathbf Z_2, \qquad n\longmapsto((\rho_q^I(n))_q,m_3(n)) \] has kernel $D_3$ and is surjective; already its restriction to $K=N\cap H$ is surjective. Consequently the $G$-invariant continuous $\mathbf F_2$-characters of $N$ which vanish on $D_3$ form exactly \[ \left(\bigoplus_{q\text{ odd prime}}\mathbf F_2\psi_q\right) \oplus\mathbf F_2\eta_3. \] For an odd prime $p$, no nonzero $G$-invariant $\mathbf F_p$-character of $N$ vanishes on $D_3$.

label: lem:cubic-branch-filling
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $g=(1,f_g)\in\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$. Fill the punctures $0,\infty$ in the threefold cyclic cover $\mathbb P^1_t\setminus\{0,\infty,1,\omega,\omega^2\}$. The restriction of the standard action $\phi_g$ on the base group, followed by this filling, induces on $\pi_1(\mathbb P^1_t\setminus\{1,\omega,\omega^2\})$ the outer class of the same $g$.

label: prop:normalized-HF1-from-normalizer
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: If $g=(1,f_g)\in\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$ and $\rho_3^I(g)=0$, then its pure cubic conjugator satisfies \begin{equation}\label{eq:cubic-normalizer-13} \boxed{\quad A_g(u^2,v^2)^{-1}=f_g(u^2,uv)\quad} \end{equation} in the full signed profinite braid group.

label: cor:cubic-defect-zero-normalizer
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: On $D=\ker\lambda\cap\bigcap_q\ker\rho_q^I$ the finite cubic comparison defect $\epsilon_c=\tau+\eta$ vanishes. Together with the harmonic comparison, this gives $\chi_3=0$ on full GT.

label: prop:cubic-finite-relative-cocycle
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The map \(c_{\ell,3}:N\to\mathbf F_3(1)\) is a continuous homomorphism, independent of the choice of \(\omega\), and satisfies \[ c_{\ell,3}(aga^{-1})=\lambda_a c_{\ell,3}(g). \] The homomorphism \[ \Xi_{\ell,3}(g)=c_{\ell,3}(g)+ \ell\,\rho_\ell^I(g)\bmod3 \qquad(g\in N) \] vanishes on \(N\cap H\). It extends uniquely to a continuous crossed homomorphism \(G\to\mathbf F_3(1)\) that is zero on \(H\). On \(D\) its value is \(c_{\ell,3}\).

label: lem:pdl-reflex-and-local
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The CM type of \(J_p\) is \(\{[1],\ldots,[g]\}\). It is primitive, its reflex field is \(F_p\), and its reflex norm on coefficient-two units is the group-ring map \[ \Phi_p^*=\sum_{a=1}^{g}[a^{-1}]. \] For every prime \(v\mid2\) of \(F_p\), let \(\iota_v:O_{F_p,v}^\times\to\mathcal A_p^\times\) put a unit in the \(v\)-component and one in every other component. A corresponding inertia subgroup \(I_v\subset H\) satisfies the exact arithmetic identity \begin{equation}\label{eq:pdl-one-inertia} \rho_{J_p,2}(I_v) =\Phi_p^*(\iota_v O_{F_p,v}^\times). \end{equation} Consequently, products of elements of these conjugate inertia subgroups realize \(\Phi_p^*(u)\) for every \(u\in\mathcal U_p\).

label: prop:pdl-arithmetic-realization
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every \(u\in\mathcal U_p\), there is an element \(w_p(u)\in V_{\rm quad}\cap H\) such that \begin{equation}\label{eq:pdl-witness-values} \mathfrak h_p(w_p(u))=(s-1)^2\Phi_p^*(u),\qquad \mathfrak h_q(w_p(u))=1 \quad\text{for every odd prime }q\ne p. \end{equation} Every original \(\chi\in X_2\) vanishes on this entire family. In particular the image \((s-1)^2\Phi_p^*(\mathcal U_p)\) is realized arithmetically with all other prime-degree coordinates zero.

label: thm:simultaneous-cyclotomic-cm
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let \(\Pi\) be any set of primes at least five satisfying the equivalent unit conditions of Theorem~\ref{thm:cm-type-torus-unit}, and put \[ \mathcal R_\Pi=R_{\rm quad}\cap\bigcap_{p\in\Pi}\ker\mathfrak h_p, \qquad \mathcal V_\Pi=V_{\rm quad}\cap\mathcal R_\Pi. \] These subgroups are closed and normal in \(G\). The joint image of the old subgroups, and of either arithmetic intersection, is exactly \begin{equation}\label{eq:pdl-simultaneous} \prod_{p\in\Pi}\mathcal P_p. \end{equation} Both old-to-new quotients are this product, also on arithmetic intersections. Moreover \(G=\mathcal R_\Pi H\); full \(B\) is preserved on \(\mathcal R_\Pi\), and \(B_{\max2}\) is preserved on \(\mathcal V_\Pi\). The exact original restriction kernel on either subgroup is \(\mathcal S=s(Y_2)\). Its complete image is the invariant quadratic characters killing that subgroup's arithmetic intersection, canonically \(\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cts}(B,\mathbf F_2)\). No nonzero continuous quadratic character of the displayed product, pulled back to \(R_{\rm quad}\), extends to a member of \(X_2\).

label: prop:explicit-cm-type-factor
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: One has the exact identity \begin{equation} (s-1)\Phi^*=(c-1)Q_p \quad\text{in }\mathbf Z[G_p]. \label{eq:cm-type-3} \end{equation} The class of \(Q_p\) modulo \(1+c\) is uniquely determined by \eqref{eq:cm-type-3}. It is a unit of \(R_p\) if and only if \begin{equation} \gcd\bigl(\overline Q_p(X),X^h+1\bigr)=1 \quad\text{in }\mathbf F_2[X].\label{eq:cm-type-4} \end{equation} If \(h=2^v m\) with \(m\) odd, one may replace \(X^h+1\) in \eqref{eq:cm-type-4} by \(X^m-1\). Moreover \begin{equation} Q_p(1)=\pm1. \label{eq:cm-type-5} \end{equation} Consequently every prime with \(p-1\) a power of two satisfies \eqref{eq:cm-type-4}. The unit condition is independent of the choice of primitive generator of \(G_p\), of translation of the CM type, and of replacing the type by its complement.

label: thm:cm-type-torus-unit
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The action of \(\mathbf Z_2[G_p]\) on \(T\) factors through \(R_p\). The following conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item \(Q_p\) is a unit of \(R_p\); \item \(Q_p:T\longrightarrow T\) is an automorphism; \item \((s-1)\Phi^*(U)=T\). \end{enumerate} For every \(p\), without a unit hypothesis, the exact identity is \begin{equation} (s-1)\Phi^*(U)=Q_pT. \label{eq:cm-type-7} \end{equation} If \(\mathcal D_p\) is the determinant of multiplication by \(Q_p\) on the free rank-\(h\) module \(R_p\), then the unit criterion is equivalently \(\mathcal D_p\) odd. In particular it is an integral determinant criterion, with no class-number assumption.

label: thm:full-cyclotomic-torus-coinvariants
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There is a canonical isomorphism \begin{equation} \Delta_s:\mathbf Z_2^\times/(\mathbf Z_2^\times)^2 \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }T/(s-1)T, \qquad t\longmapsto[s(v)/v],\quad v\in U,\quad v\,c(v)=t. \label{eq:cm-type-10} \end{equation} In particular \begin{equation} T^{G_p}=\{1,-1\},\qquad T/(s-1)T\simeq C_2^2, \qquad [T:(s-1)T]=4. \label{eq:cm-type-11} \end{equation} Define \(\chi_a=a\circ\Delta_s^{-1}\) and \(\chi_b=b\circ\Delta_s^{-1}\) on \(T\). Then \begin{equation} (s-1)T=\ker\chi_a\cap\ker\chi_b. \label{eq:cm-type-12} \end{equation} They are exactly the two invariant torus characters of the coefficient-two cyclic-cover construction: \(\chi_a\) defines \(\xi_{2,p}\), and \(\chi_b\) defines its companion \(\widetilde\psi_p\). Thus the companion equality \(\widetilde\psi_p=\rho_p^I/2\bmod2\) identifies which known Kummer coordinate is removed in \eqref{eq:cm-type-12}.

label: prop:cm-commutator-torus-torsion
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: With the notation of Theorem \ref{thm:full-cyclotomic-torus-coinvariants}, let \(P=(s-1)T\) and let \(r\) be the number of orbits of complex conjugation on the primes above two. Then \[ P_{\mathrm{tors}}=(s-1)T_{\mathrm{tors}} \simeq C_2^{r-1}. \] In particular, as compact abelian groups, noncanonically, \[ T\simeq\mathbf Z_2^h\times C_2^r, \qquad P\simeq\mathbf Z_2^h\times C_2^{r-1}. \] For example, \(p=17\) has \(r=2\), so \(P\) has one nontrivial element of order two, even though the unit criterion holds.

statement: Among continuous invariant quadratic characters which factor through the dyadic beta multiplier, the space on $M$ is one-dimensional, generated by $\rho_{2,2}^I/2\pmod2$. On each of $N$ and $D$ it is one-dimensional, generated by $\eta_3=m_3/8\pmod2$.

label: cor:dyadic-metabelian-deep-gate
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Put \[ E=C_\infty\cap D_{10},\qquad J_E=E\cap H. \] Then $E$ is a proper closed normal subgroup of $D_{10}$ and of infinite index there, and \[ G=EH,\qquad B\simeq E/\overline{[G,E]J_E}. \] Every pro-$2$ Magnus word on $E$ starts in degree at least eleven, and its dyadic beta multiplier is identically one. The kernel of restriction from $H^1(N,\mathbf F_2)^G$ to $H^1(E,\mathbf F_2)$ is exactly \[ \left(\bigoplus_{q\text{ odd prime}}\mathbf F_2\psi_q\right) \oplus\mathbf F_2\eta_3. \]

label: lem:eighth-two-conductor
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For $n=2,4,8$, the field $L_n=\mathbb Q(i,2^{1/n})$ is cyclic of degree $n$ over $K_4$. Its conductor is respectively $\mathfrak p^4,\mathfrak p^6,\mathfrak p^8$. In particular \[ L_4\subset K_4(E_4[8]),\qquad L_8\subset K_4(E_4[16]). \]

label: prop:eighth-two-division-fields
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Over $k=\mathbb Q^{\mathrm{ab}}$ one has \[ k(E_4[8])=k(2^{1/4}),\qquad k(E_4[16])=k(2^{1/8}). \]

status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Modulo sixteen the commutator subgroup of $q(F)$ is the central cyclic group of order four generated by \[ C=[U^2,L^2] =\begin{pmatrix}13&8\\8&5\end{pmatrix}\pmod{16}. \] In particular $q_{16}(\gamma_3F)=1$.

statement: If $h=(1,f)$ is gentle and $\rho_2(h)=0$, then \[ \beta_h\in\gamma_3F,\qquad q_{16}(\beta_h)=D_h\bmod16=W_h\bmod16=I. \]

statement: For every $h\in M_0$, one has $A_h\in F'$.

statement: For every $h\in M_0$, \[ j_3(T_h)=\rho_2(h)\pmod3. \] On the arithmetic subgroup, this quotient is the Kummer action on $k(2^{1/3})/k$, with the indicated choice of exponent.

label: lem:kn-different-local-systems
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For $n=11$ and a primitive cube root $\omega$ in $\mathbb F_{17^2}$, consider characters over $\overline{\mathbb F}_{17}$. The character of $H_{11}$ obtained by pulling back $x\mapsto1,y\mapsto\omega$ along $d_{11}$ is different from the restriction of every character $x\mapsto\xi,y\mapsto\omega$ with $\xi^{11}=1$. Nor is either kind a deck translate of the other.

label: prop:kn-linear-sign-model
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There is an $\mathbb F_{17}$-linear automorphism of the space \eqref{eq:eleventh-local-system-H} that commutes with the whole deck group $A$, preserves its alternating intersection form, and has determinant $-1$ on the ten-dimensional $\omega$-eigenspace over $\mathbb F_{17^2}$. Its quadratic norm-one determinant sign is therefore $-1$. This is a linear model, not a GT element or a solution of the pentagon or of \eqref{eq:eleventh-local-system-K}.

label: prop:eta-ten-no-extension-d7
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The character $\eta_{10}$ on $D_9$ extends invariantly to $D_8$ by $\alpha_{10}$, but has no $G$-invariant extension to $D_7$. Consequently it has no such extension to $D_5$, $D_3$, $D$ or $N$.

label: cor:weight-ten-character-kernels
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The invariant quadratic-character kernels on restriction to $D_{10}$ are \[ \begin{array}{c|l} \text{domain}&\text{kernel}\\ \hline D_9&\mathbf F_2\eta_{10}\\ D_8&\mathbf F_2\eta_9\oplus\mathbf F_2\alpha_{10}\\ D_7&\mathbf F_2\eta_8\oplus\mathbf F_2\eta_9\\ D_5&\mathbf F_2\eta_7\oplus\mathbf F_2\alpha_8\\ D_3&\mathbf F_2\eta_5\\ N&\displaystyle\left(\bigoplus_{q\text{ odd prime}}\mathbf F_2\psi_q\right) \oplus\mathbf F_2\eta_3. \end{array} \]

label: prop:eta-eight-no-extension-d3
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The character $\eta_8$ on $D_7$ extends to the invariant character \[ \alpha_8:D_5\longrightarrow\mathbf F_2,\qquad \alpha_8(1,f)=[S^4TST^2]f\pmod2, \] but has no $G$-invariant extension to $D_3$. More precisely, no nonzero linear combination of $\eta_7$ and $\alpha_8$ on $D_5$ extends to a $G$-invariant character of $D_3$.

label: cor:d3-character-kernel-d8
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: One has \[ \ker\!\left(H^1(D_3,\mathbf F_2)^G \longrightarrow H^1(D_8,\mathbf F_2)\right) =\mathbf F_2\eta_5. \]

label: thm:exact-joint-odd-cm-image
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The full and arithmetic joint images on \(T_D\) agree: \begin{equation}\label{eq:exact-joint-odd-2} \begin{split} (T_{\rm odd},W_{\rm odd})(T_D) &=(T_{\rm odd},W_{\rm odd})(T_D\cap H)\\ &=\mathcal C_3\times\mathcal A_4. \end{split} \end{equation} Moreover \begin{equation}\label{eq:exact-joint-odd-3} T_{\rm odd}(U_D)=T_{\rm odd}(U_D\cap H)=\mathcal C_3. \end{equation} Consequently \begin{equation}\label{eq:exact-joint-odd-4} T_D/V_D\cong\mathcal C_3\times\mathcal A_4,\qquad U_D/V_D\cong\mathcal C_3, \end{equation} and \begin{equation}\label{eq:exact-joint-odd-5} T_D=V_D(T_D\cap H),\qquad U_D=V_D(U_D\cap H). \end{equation} These are internal factorizations of the indicated groups.

label: lem:wild-three-primary-kernel
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every \(g\in P_D\), the entire coefficient-three cubic frame is the identity: \[ T_{g,3}=1. \]

label: lem:local-cubic-cm-inertia
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let \(\ell\ge5\), let \(e_\ell=v_3(\ell-\chi_{-3}(\ell))\), and let \(Z_\ell\) be the cyclic three-Sylow subgroup of \(\mathcal N_{3,\ell}\), of order \(3^{e_\ell}\). There exists an arithmetic element \[ x_\ell\in M\cap H\cap\bigcap_p\ker\Phi_p \] whose uncorrected cubic Tate value is supported only at \(\ell\) and generates \(Z_\ell\).

label: prop:finite-interchange
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Put $X=U^2\bmod8$ and $P=\langle X,R\bmod8\rangle\subset\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z/8)$. There is a surjection \[ \kappa:P\longrightarrow\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb F_3) \] such that \[ \kappa(X)=-S\bmod3,\qquad \kappa(R)=U\bmod3,\qquad \kappa(5I)=-I. \] The group $P$ has order $192$ and the kernel has order eight. For every profinite commutator word $f\in\widehat F(x,y)'$, \[ \kappa\bigl(f(X,R)\bigr)=f(S,U)=f(U,S)^{-1} \] if $f$ satisfies the two-cycle relation.

label: lem:common-sign
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every $g\in D$ the matrix $f_g(U,S)\bmod3$ is central. Consequently \[ f_g(U,S)=(-I)^{\eta(g)}\quad\text{in }\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb F_3) \] defines a continuous homomorphism $\eta:D\to\mathbb F_2$.

label: prop:pair-of-gates
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For $g\in D$ define \[ \epsilon_h(g)=w(g)+\eta(g),\qquad \epsilon_c(g)=\tau(g)+\eta(g). \] These are continuous homomorphisms on $D$, and \[ \boxed{\quad \chi_3=\epsilon_h+\epsilon_c.\quad} \] More explicitly, the two signs are the following finite defects: \[ \begin{split} (-I)^{\epsilon_h(g)} &=q_3(\beta_g)^{-1}f_g(U,S)^{-1},\\ (-I)^{\epsilon_c(g)} &=\kappa\!\left(q_8(A_g)^{-1}f_g(X,R)^{-1}\right). \end{split} \] In particular the two finite comparisons \begin{equation} q_3(\beta_g)^{-1}=f_g(U,S),\qquad \kappa(q_8(A_g)^{-1})=\kappa(f_g(X,R)) \label{eq:finite-harmonic-cubic-comparisons} \end{equation} would imply $\chi_3(g)=0$. They are sufficient conditions; vanishing of $\chi_3$ requires only equality of their two defects. Both defects vanish on $D\cap G_{\mathbb Q}$.

label: lem:eta-quotient-invariant
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The kernel of the evaluation \[ e:\widehat F(x,y)\longrightarrow Q=\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb F_3), \qquad e(x)=U,\quad e(y)=S, \] is invariant under every gentle automorphism. Consequently $\eta$ is invariant under conjugation by all of $G$.

label: prop:two-relative-extensions
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Each of $\epsilon_h,\epsilon_c$ has a unique extension to a continuous homomorphism $G\to\mathbb F_2$ that is zero on $H$. Their sum is the established residual relative character $\chi_3$. The harmonic extension is proved to vanish in Section~\ref{sec:harmonic-dyadic-comparison}. The cubic extension and $\chi_3$ vanish by Section~\ref{sec:normalized-cubic-identity}.

label: prop:truncated-counterexample
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: In the mod-two Magnus ring $\mathcal R=\mathbb F_2\langle A,B\rangle/(\text{degree}\ge5)$, send $a$ to $1+A$ and $b$ to $1+B$. The word $\beta=a^3bab^3$ has exponent sums $(4,4)$ and satisfies \[ d\alpha(d)\alpha^2(d)=1\quad\text{in }\mathcal R. \] Nevertheless its image under $a\mapsto i,b\mapsto j$ in the quaternion group is $-1$. Thus this truncated norm equation and the two exponent sums modulo four do not determine the quaternion central sign.

label: prop:five-inertia-odd-cubic
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There is an element \(w\in U_D\cap H\) whose full harmonic frame is one and whose cubic frame at five is \[ T_5(w)=\left(\frac{1+5\omega}{1+5\omega^2}\right)^{-2}. \] This value has infinite pro-five order.

label: lem:frame-all-multipliers-congruence
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every $g\in\mathcal G$ and every prime $\ell$ there is a unique matrix \[ D_{g,\ell}=\begin{pmatrix}\lambda_{g,\ell}&b_{g,\ell}\\0&1\end{pmatrix} \] such that $\widetilde q_\ell\Phi_g=\operatorname{Ad}(D_{g,\ell})\widetilde q_\ell$. It depends continuously on $g$, and $D_{gh,\ell}=D_{g,\ell}D_{h,\ell}$. For $h\in N_0$, its reduction modulo twelve is the identity.

label: prop:frame-sign-conjugation
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The restrictions of $a_2,a_3$, and hence $\delta$, to $N_0$ are invariant under conjugation by $\mathcal G$.

label: thm:global-frame-character
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There is a unique continuous character \[ \Delta:\mathcal G\longrightarrow\mathbb F_2 \] which restricts to $\delta$ on $N_0$ and is zero on $G_{\mathbb Q}$. For any $g\in\mathcal G$, choose $\sigma\in G_{\mathbb Q}$ with $(\lambda,\rho_2)(\sigma)=(\lambda,\rho_2)(g)$. Then \[ \Delta(g)=\delta(g\sigma^{-1}). \] This character vanishes on the full pentagon group.

label: prop:full-cyclotomic-frattini-action
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Retain \(P=M/R_M\), \(V=P/\Phi(P)\), and the coordinate \(V=\mathbf F_2[[T]]\), where \(T=h_*-1\) and \(\lambda_2(h_*)=-3\). Put \[ U=G/M=\widehat{\mathbf Z}^{\,\times},\qquad \Gamma=1+4\mathbf Z_2,\qquad U_0=\{\pm1\}\times\prod_{q\ {\rm odd}}\mathbf Z_q^\times. \] Thus \(U=\Gamma\times U_0\). For \(u\in U\), let \(\langle u_2\rangle\) be the unique member of \(\{u_2,-u_2\}\) in \(\Gamma\). The complete action on \(V\) is \begin{equation} u\cdot F(T) =(1+T)^{\,\log\langle u_2\rangle/\log(-3)}F(T). \label{eq:cyclotomic-frattini-1} \end{equation} In particular \(U_0\) acts trivially.

label: prop:explicit-residual-extension-obstruction
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let \(W=H^1(P,\mathbf F_2)\), with its discrete continuous \(U\)-action. There is a natural isomorphism \begin{equation} H^1_{\rm cts}(U,W) \cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cts}(U_0,\mathbf F_2). \label{eq:cyclotomic-frattini-2} \end{equation} In particular the latter is a direct sum of one copy of \(\mathbf F_2\) for the dyadic sign factor and one for each odd rational prime. There is an exact segment \begin{equation} 0\longrightarrow\mathbf F_2(\mu\bmod2) \longrightarrow H^1(M,\mathbf F_2)^G \longrightarrow H^1(R_M,\mathbf F_2)^G \longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cts}(U_0,\mathbf F_2), \label{eq:cyclotomic-frattini-3} \end{equation} where \(\mu=\rho_{2,2}^I/2\). No surjectivity of the last map is asserted.

label: thm:full-dyadic-free-product
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The full dyadic image is the arithmetic image, and \[ Q_2\cong C_2*_{\mathrm{pro}\text{-}2}\mathbf Z_2. \] One may take complex conjugation as the generator of \(C_2\), and any arithmetic element with dyadic multiplier \(-3\) as the generator of the second factor. Under this presentation the multiplier is the abelianization map \[ Q_2\longrightarrow\mathbf Z_2^\times =\{\pm1\}\times(1+4\mathbf Z_2), \qquad c\longmapsto-1,\qquad h\longmapsto-3. \] Its kernel is the normalized image \(P=M/R_M\).

label: lem:free-product-cyclotomic-kernel
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
