statement: The group \(K_F\) is free pro-two on the convergent sequence \[ b_0=[s,t],\qquad b_{j+1}=[t,b_j]\quad(j\ge0). \]

label: prop:gaussian-division-norm
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: One has the exact identity \[ C_\ell^4=\frac{\chi}{\ell}. \] For the action of the residue norm-one torus \[ T_\ell= \{a\in(\mathbf F_\ell[i])^\times:a\overline a=1\} \] on the \(\ell\)-torsion points, the multiplier of \(C_\ell\) is its quadratic character: \[ \frac{a(C_\ell)}{C_\ell} =a^{(\ell-\chi)/2}\in\{1,-1\}. \] The notation on the left means the monomial action on the factors, using the second identity in \eqref{eq:gaussian-norm-function}; it does not presume an arithmetic realization of \(a\).

label: lem:gaussian-norm-v4-cover
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The morphism \(F:E\to\mathbf P^1\) is a Galois cover of degree four with deck group \[ \{1,\tau_{T_0},\tau_{T_+}[-1],\tau_{T_-}[-1]\} \simeq(\mathbf Z/2)^2. \] Its branch values are \(1,-1,i,-i\). It restricts to an unramified cover \[ E\setminus E[4]\longrightarrow \mathbf P^1\setminus\{0,\infty,1,-1,i,-i\}. \] For every odd prime \(\ell\), the values \(F(Q)^4\), with one \(Q\) in each order-four CM orbit on \(E[\ell]\setminus\{0\}\), form a configuration of \(M=(\ell^2-1)/4\) distinct points of \(\mathbf P^1\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}\).

label: prop:generic-elliptic-division-norm
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let \[ E_{A,B}:y^2=x^3+Ax^2+Bx,\qquad B(A^2-4B)\ne0, \] over a field of characteristic zero. Thus \((0,0)\) is a specified nonzero two-torsion point. For an odd prime \(\ell\), put \(M=(\ell^2-1)/4\), which is even, and choose one point in each pair \(\{Q,-Q\}\) of nonzero \(\ell\)-torsion points. Define \[ F_B(Q)=\frac{x(Q)^2-B}{2y(Q)},\qquad D_\ell=B^{-M/2}\prod_{Q\bmod\{\pm1\}}F_B(Q). \] Then \begin{equation}\label{eq:generic-elliptic-norm-square} D_\ell^2=\frac{\chi_{-4}(\ell)}{\ell}. \end{equation} Changing representatives changes \(D_\ell\) only by a sign. It is unchanged by the coordinate scaling \((x,y,A,B)\mapsto(u^2x,u^3y,u^2A,u^4B)\). For \(A=0,B=-1\), group the representatives in pairs \(Q,\iota Q\), one such pair for each order-four CM orbit, where \(\iota(x,y)=(-x,iy)\). Then the tensor \(C_\ell=\prod_{Q\bmod\langle\iota\rangle}F_{-1}(Q)\) satisfies, with those representative choices, \begin{equation}\label{eq:quadratic-norm-is-square-of-cm-norm} D_\ell=C_\ell^2. \end{equation}

label: prop:no-cm-preserving-tate-degeneration
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: A family of smooth elliptic curves in characteristic zero, equipped with an origin-preserving automorphism of exact order four, has constant \(j\)-invariant \(1728\). It cannot have a degeneration to a multiplicative Tate cusp while retaining that automorphism on the generic elliptic curve. If additional marked points are allowed to collide in a stable compactification, forgetting those points and stabilizing still has a smooth elliptic core of \(j\)-invariant \(1728\).

label: prop:gaussian-finite-peripheral-scope
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every odd prime \(\ell\), there is a finite quotient of the three-punctured sphere group with peripheral orders \(4,2,4\), and an automorphism that fixes its maximal pro-\(p\) quotient for every prime \(p\), preserves each positive peripheral conjugacy class, acts symplectically on its translation subgroup, and has nontrivial Gaussian square sign.

label: prop:genus-two-finite-quotient
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There is a surjection \[ \ell:G_8\longrightarrow\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb F_3),\qquad U\longmapsto A,\quad R\longmapsto T, \] whose kernel is the order-eight subgroup \[ K=\langle Z,X^2C,Y^2C\rangle. \] It kills $Z$, so the signed congruence representation induces \[ \bar\ell:\Gamma=C_2*C_3\longrightarrow \mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb F_3). \] For $s=uvu$, $r=uv$ and $u=r^{-1}s$, their images have orders $2,3,8$, respectively. On the subgroup $P$, this map agrees with the previous interchange map on all commutator prowords in $X,R$, although its value on $X$ is $S$ instead of $-S$.

label: cor:genus-two-sign-cover
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The discrete kernel of $\bar\ell$ is the fundamental group of a genus-two surface with six punctures. Its compactification carries a faithful deck action of $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb F_3)$ of signature $(2,3,8)$. The central involution is its hyperelliptic involution. On $D$ the induced action on this finite deck group is the identity. The pure harmonic conjugator maps to $I$, and the pure cubic conjugator maps to $(-I)^{\tau(g)}$.

label: thm:main-cyclotomic-cm-normalization
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every prime satisfying the first-layer condition, the exact arithmetic image of \(h_p\) on \(R_{\rm quad}\cap H\) or \(V_{\rm quad}\cap H\) is the preimage of \((\ker\mathscr K_p)^\perp\) in \(P_p\). This remains true after imposing any collection of the other-prime scalar kernels. For \(p\in\Pi_{\rm global}\), the joint images of \(R_{\rm quad}\), \(V_{\rm quad}\), and both arithmetic intersections are all \(\prod_pP_p\), with all finite signs included. Put \[ R_{\rm global}=R_{\rm quad}\cap \bigcap_{p\in\Pi_{\rm global}}\ker h_p,\qquad V_{\rm global}=V_{\rm quad}\cap R_{\rm global}. \] Then \[ \begin{gathered} G=R_{\rm global}H,\qquad R_{\rm global}/V_{\rm global}\simeq R_{\rm quad}/V_{\rm quad},\\ B\simeq R_{\rm global}/ \overline{[G,R_{\rm global}](R_{\rm global}\cap H)},\\ B_{\max2}\simeq \left(V_{\rm global}/ \overline{[G,V_{\rm global}](V_{\rm global}\cap H)}\right)_{\max2}. \end{gathered} \] The quotient in the first line is pro-odd, and its arithmetic image is preserved. Both original quadratic restriction kernels are exactly \(\mathcal S\), with image every invariant quadratic character vanishing on the arithmetic intersection. The set \(\Pi_{\rm global}\) contains every prime with odd cyclotomic class number, and also \(29\) and \(113\); it does not contain \(163\). At \(29\) and \(113\) the local index is eight but the full arithmetic image is \(P_p\). At \(163\) the arithmetic image is exactly \(Q_{163}P_{163}\), of index four.

label: thm:main-all-cm-restriction
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let \[ R_{\rm all}=R_{\rm quad}\cap\bigcap_{p\ge5}\ker h_p,\qquad V_{\rm all}=V_{\rm quad}\cap R_{\rm all}. \] Restriction from \(X_2\) to either group has kernel exactly \(\mathcal S\). There are canonical maps \[ B(V_{\rm all})_{\max2}\simeq B(R_{\rm all})_{\max2} \twoheadrightarrow B_{\max2}. \] Moreover \(R_{\rm all}/V_{\rm all}\simeq R_{\rm quad}/V_{\rm quad}\), preserving the arithmetic image. The last arrow is asserted to be surjective.

label: thm:main-all-cm-central-obstruction
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let \(\mathcal I\) be any set of primes at least five and put \[ R_0=R_{\rm quad},\qquad C_p=h_p(R_0),\qquad D_p=h_p(R_0\cap H),\qquad J=R_0\cap\bigcap_{p\in\mathcal I}\ker h_p. \] The joint full and arithmetic images are exactly \[ C=\prod_{p\in\mathcal I}C_p,\qquad D_0=\prod_{p\in\mathcal I}D_p. \] For the discrete conjugation module \(U=\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cont}(C/D_0,\mathbb F_2)\), \[ H^j_{\rm cont}(G/R_0,U)=0\qquad(j\ge0). \] Let \(\mathscr X(J)\) be the space of continuous \(G\)-invariant quadratic characters of \(J\) that vanish on \(J\cap H\). Restriction identifies \[ \operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cont}(B,\mathbb F_2) \simeq\ker\!\left( o_2:\mathscr X(J)\longrightarrow H^2_{\rm cont}(C,D_0;\mathbb F_2) \right). \] Here \(o_2\) is the relative central extension class, with the splitting over \(D_0\) specified by the arithmetic subgroup. Every character in this kernel has a unique extension to \(G\) which vanishes on \(H\).

label: thm:main-163-odd-inertia
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let \(R=R_{\rm global}\), \(P=P_{163}\), \(A=Q_{163}P\), and \(U=\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cts}(P/A,\mathbb F_2)\), with its cyclotomic conjugation action. Then \[ H^j_{\rm cont}(G/R,U)=0\qquad(j\ge0). \] If \(h_{163}(R)=P\) and \(J=\ker(h_{163}:R\to P)\), a continuous \(G\)-invariant quadratic character of \(J\) that is zero on \(J\cap H\) extends to \(G\), zero on \(H\), exactly when its relative central extension class is zero. The extension is unique. The possible invariant relative class is the one-dimensional quaternion line in \(H^2(P,A;\mathbb F_2)\).

label: thm:genus-two-exact-image
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The degree-five homology scalar has exact image \(P_5\) on \(R_{\rm quad}\), \(V_{\rm quad}\), and both arithmetic intersections. The four corresponding quotients by its kernel are \(\mathbf Z_2^2\). Moreover \(G=R_{{\rm quad},5}H\); the full relative quotient on \(R_{{\rm quad},5}\) is \(B\), and its maximal pro-two version on \(V_{{\rm quad},5}\) is \(B_{\max2}\). Both original restriction kernels are exactly \(\mathcal S\), and both images are the full relative invariant character space \(\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cts}(B,\F_2)\).

label: lem:genus-two-inertia-M
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Every \(v\in T_5^{(2)}\) is \(\mathfrak h_5(j)\) for a pro-two arithmetic element \(j\in I_2\cap M\).

label: thm:harmonic-beta-square-lattice
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There is one integral identification of the harmonic quadratic order with \(\widehat O_4\), valid for every \(g\in N\) and every coefficient prime, under which the corrected harmonic frame \(W_g\) is \(\nu_{4,g}\). Reversing the choice of primitive fourth root conjugates all these values simultaneously. Consequently, on \(D=N_{\rm rad}\), the tame harmonic square test at an odd prime \(\ell\) is equivalent to \[ B_{g,\ell}(i,-1)^{(\ell-\chi_{-4}(\ell))/2}=1 \] in the residue norm-one group. Either choice of the primitive fourth root gives the same test.

label: lem:dyadic-branch-word
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Put $h(a,b)=f^+(a,1,b)$. Then \[ f(a,b)=h(a,b)h(b,a)^{-1} \quad\text{in }\widehat F(a,b). \]

label: lem:unique-swap-frame
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The map $\gamma\mapsto\theta(\gamma)\gamma^{-1}$ on $\widehat F(a,b)$ is injective. In particular \[ \beta(a,b)=h(b,a). \]

label: prop:normalized-GF1-from-dyadic
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every $g$ as above, in the full signed profinite braid group on generators $u,v$, with $s=uvu$, one has \[ \beta_g(u^2,v^2)^{-1}=f_g(u^2,s). \tag{GF1$_0$} \]

label: cor:harmonic-defect-zero
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: On $D=\ker\lambda\cap\bigcap_q\ker\rho_q^I$, the finite harmonic frame sign satisfies $w=\eta$. Thus the previously constructed relative character $\epsilon_h=w+\eta$ is zero on the whole of full GT, and the remaining exceptional character is $\chi_3=\epsilon_c=\tau+\eta$. The cubic comparison in Section~\ref{sec:normalized-cubic-identity} will also make this character zero.

label: thm:individual-frame-kummer
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every $g\in N=\ker(\lambda,\rho_2)\subset\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$, \[ a_2(g)=a_3(g)=\frac{\rho_3^I(g)}2\pmod2. \] In particular the character $a_2+\rho_3^I/2\bmod2$ is zero on $N$. Both frame signs vanish on the simultaneous radical-normalized subgroup $N_{\mathrm{rad}}$.

label: prop:harmonic-finite-relative-character
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The map \(\vartheta_{\ell,4}:N\to\mathbf F_2\) is a continuous, \(G\)-invariant homomorphism. The difference \[ \Xi_{\ell,4}(g)=\vartheta_{\ell,4}(g) +\frac{\rho_\ell^I(g)}2\bmod2 \qquad(g\in N) \] vanishes on \(N\cap H\), and therefore extends uniquely to a continuous character \(G\to\mathbf F_2\) that is zero on \(H\). On \(D\) this character is \(\vartheta_{\ell,4}\). By Theorem~\ref{thm:harmonic-beta-square-lattice}, its vanishing there is exactly the tame harmonic square test at \(\ell\). No nonvanishing of \(\Xi_{\ell,4}\) on full GT is asserted.

label: prop:harmonic-formal-residue-gap
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Vanishing of the integral rational Kummer coordinates, beta associativity, unitarity, the dyadic Anderson formulas, and logarithmic Anderson identities do not by themselves force every harmonic square test as identities of formal integral Alexander data.

label: lem:iii-prime-two-dimensional
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $k$ be any field and let $\rho:B_4\to\mathrm{GL}_2(k)$ be a homomorphism. Then $\rho((ab)^3)$ and $\rho((bc)^3)$ commute. For a finite field $k$ and $g\in D$, it follows that \[ g_g\bigl(\rho((ab)^3),\rho((bc)^3)\bigr)=1. \] Thus such a direct matrix specialization of $(\mathrm{III}')$ does not retain its harmonic auxiliary-word term.

label: lem:integral-boundary-measure
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every $g\in N$ there is an integral $\mathbf Z_2$-valued measure $\nu_{g,+}$ on $1+4\mathbf Z_2$, of total mass zero, such that \begin{equation} \int t^{2k}\,d\nu_{g,+}(t) =(1-2^{2k})\tau_{2k+1}(g)\qquad(k\ge1), \label{eq:integral-boundary-moments} \end{equation} where the normalization is exactly \[ c_{2k+1}(g)=[u^{2k}]q_g(e^u),\qquad \tau_{2k+1}(g)=\frac{(2k)!}{2}c_{2k+1}(g). \] The same formula defines an integral continuous homomorphism $\tau_{2k+1}:M\to\mathbf Z_2$ with conjugation weight $\lambda_2^{2k+1}$. Its value modulo two is independent of $k$: \[ \tau_{2k+1}(g)\equiv\tau_3(g)=a_2(g)\pmod2 \qquad(g\in M). \]

label: lem:uniform-odd-coordinate-bound
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: If $g\in N$ and $a_2(g)=a_4(g)=\cdots=a_{2r-2}(g)=0$, then \[ a_{2r}(g)\in2^{2r+1}\mathbf Z_2. \]

label: thm:fr-Y2-complete
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There is a direct-sum decomposition \begin{equation}\label{eq:fr-Y2-basis} Y_2= \mathbf F_2\eta_3 \ \oplus\! \bigoplus_{p\ {\rm odd}}\mathbf F_2\psi_p \ \oplus\! \bigoplus_{p\ {\rm odd}}\mathbf F_2\kappa_{2,p} \ \oplus\! \bigoplus_{\substack{p<q\\p,q\ {\rm odd}}} \mathbf F_2\kappa_{p,q}. \end{equation} The additional characters are specified uniquely as follows. The transgression gives an isomorphism \begin{equation}\label{eq:fr-Y2-transgression} \operatorname{tr}:Y_2 \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \ker\!\left(H^2(A,\mathbf F_2) \longrightarrow\operatorname{Br}(\mathbf Q)[2]\right). \end{equation} Writing \(\operatorname{Inf}_U^A\) for inflation, one has \begin{align} \operatorname{tr}(\kappa_{2,p}) &=\operatorname{Inf}_U^A \left(a c_p+\varepsilon_p(\delta_2+\delta_p)\right), \label{eq:fr-Y2-k2p}\\ \operatorname{tr}(\kappa_{p,q}) &=\operatorname{Inf}_U^A \left(c_pc_q+\ell_p(q^*)\delta_p +\ell_q(p^*)\delta_q\right). \label{eq:fr-Y2-kpq} \end{align} All products in these formulas are cup products. Every sum in \eqref{eq:fr-Y2-basis} is finite. In particular the quotient of \(Y_2\) by the known span \(\mathbf F_2\eta_3+\bigoplus_p\mathbf F_2\psi_p\) has countably infinite dimension. These are statements about the arithmetic target only. They do not assert that any additional basis character extends to an invariant character of the corresponding full-GT subgroup.

label: thm:joint-odd-cm-gate
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let \(T_{\rm odd}\) be the maximal pro-odd projection of the corrected Eisenstein CM homomorphism, and put \[ V_D=U_D\cap\ker T_{\rm odd}. \] Then \(V_D\) is closed and \(G\)-normal, and \begin{equation} B_{\max2}\cong \left(V_D/\overline{[G,V_D](V_D\cap H)}\right)_{\max2}. \label{eq:joint-odd-cm-1} \end{equation} The original restriction kernel is \begin{equation} \ker\bigl(X_2\to H^1(V_D,\mathbf F_2)\bigr) =\bigoplus_{q\ {\rm odd}}\mathbf F_2\psi_q \oplus\mathbf F_2\eta_3. \label{eq:joint-odd-cm-2} \end{equation} Moreover \begin{equation} [U_D:V_D]=\infty,\qquad [U_D\cap H:V_D\cap H]=\infty. \label{eq:joint-odd-cm-3} \end{equation}

label: prop:kummer-multiplicativity
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For positive integers $a,b$ and every $g\in\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$, \[ \rho_{ab}^I(g)=\rho_a^I(g)+\rho_b^I(g). \] Consequently \[ \rho_n^I=\sum_{q\mid n}v_q(n)\rho_q^I, \qquad \frac{\rho_{ab}^I-\rho_a^I-\rho_b^I}{2}\bmod2=0. \] The last expression therefore supplies no nonzero character in the restriction kernel.

label: cor:dyadic-anderson
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Every element of $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$ satisfies all dyadic Anderson multiplication relations $(A_{2^j})$, $j\geq1$, in the notation of \cite[Definition 2.3]{Furusho2003}.

label: lem:level3-cusp-swap-gate
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There is an involution \(\vartheta_3\) of \(K_0\) with \[ \vartheta_3(u)=v^3,\qquad \vartheta_3(v^3)=u,\qquad \vartheta_3=\operatorname{Ad}(s)\circ d_3. \] For an element \(g=(1,f_g)\) of full profinite GT with \(\rho_2(g)=0\), put \(q=f_g(u^2,v^2)\). Then \[ d_3(q)=q\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \vartheta_3(q)=q^{-1}. \]

label: lem:level3-principal-image
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let \(P=\Gamma(3)\), the kernel of \(\mathcal M\to\operatorname{PSL}_2(\mathbf F_3)\). Then \[ d_3(P)=\Gamma^0(9),\qquad \vartheta_3(P)=\Gamma_0(9). \] In particular \(\vartheta_3\) does not preserve \(P\). The intersection \(P\cap\Gamma_0(9)\) has index \(36\) in \(\mathcal M\); its modular curve has genus one and six cusps, of widths \(3,3,3,9,9,9\).

label: lem:level3-cubic-frame-principal
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For the same normalized element \(g\), let \(A_g\) be the normalized pure cubic conjugator, so that \[ \Phi_g(uv)=A_g(uv)A_g^{-1},\qquad A_g\in\widehat F(u^2,v^2)'. \] Then \(A_g\in\overline{\Gamma(6)}\subseteq\overline{\Gamma(3)}\). If also \(\rho_3^I(g)=0\), the normalized cubic identity gives \[ f_g(u^2,uv)\in\overline{\Gamma(6)}. \]

label: lem:level3-marked-regular-closure
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let \(F=\Gamma(2)\) and \(J=F\cap\Gamma_0(3)\). The inclusion \(J\subset F\) has index four and its compactified modular curve has genus zero, with cusp widths \(2,2,2,6,6,6\). Its regular closure over \(F\) is \(\Gamma(6)\), with deck group \(A_4\). The latter group has index \(72\) in \(\operatorname{PSL}_2(\mathbf Z)\), twelve cusps of width six, and compactified genus one.

label: prop:level3-free-subgroup
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Put \(F=\langle a,b\rangle=\Gamma(2)\), where \(a=u^2,b=v^2\), and \(J=F\cap\Gamma_0(3)\). Then \(J\) has the free basis \[ a,\quad b^3,\quad b^2ab^{-1},\quad ba^2b^{-2}, \quad baba^{-1}b^{-1}. \] The restriction of the level-three degeneracy map is the homomorphism \(d:J\to F\) determined by \[ \begin{array}{c|c} \text{generator of }J&\text{image under }d\\ \hline a&a^3\\ b^3&b\\ b^2ab^{-1}&(ba)^3\\ ba^2b^{-2}&a^{-1}b^{-2}a^{-1}b^{-1}\\ baba^{-1}b^{-1}&a^{-1}b^3a \end{array} \] These formulas extend to full profinite completions. For \(g=(1,f_g)\) in full GT with \(\rho_2(g)=0\), the exact level-three gate is therefore the explicit equality \[ \widehat d(f_g(a,b))=f_g(a,b) \quad\text{in }\widehat F. \] No equality in this last display is asserted by this proposition.

label: thm:main-odd-pair-lifts
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every ordered pair of distinct odd primes \(\ell,q\), there is an invariant continuous homomorphism \(\xi_{\ell,q}:M\to\F_2\), where \(M=\ker\lambda\), whose restriction to \(N\) belongs to \(X_2\) and satisfies \[ \xi_{\ell,q}|_K=\kappa_{\ell,q}. \] Here \(\kappa_{\ell,q}=\kappa_{q,\ell}\) denotes the basis character indexed by the unordered pair. Its transgression is \[ c_\ell c_q+\ell_\ell(q^*)\delta_\ell +\ell_q(\ell^*)\delta_q. \] In particular this corrected class inflates to zero in \(H^2(G,\F_2)\). Explicitly, put \(d=\operatorname{ord}_\ell(q)\), and choose a primitive \(\ell\)-th root \(\zeta\in\F_{q^d}\). If \(d=2s\), choose representatives \(a_i\) of \((\Z/\ell)^\times/\langle q\rangle\); then \[ (-1)^{\xi_{\ell,q}(g)} =\prod_i B_g(\zeta^{a_i},\zeta^{a_i})^{(q^s+1)/2}. \] If \(d\) is odd, choose representatives of \((\Z/\ell)^\times/\langle q,-1\rangle\); then \[ (-1)^{\xi_{\ell,q}(g)} =\prod_i B_g(\zeta^{a_i},\zeta^{a_i})^{(q^d-1)/2}. \] The values are signs independent of these choices. The same construction works for any continuous positive peripheral action on \(\widehat F(x,y)\) of the form \(x\mapsto x^\lambda\), \(y\mapsto f^{-1}y^\lambda f\), with \(f\in\widehat F(x,y)'\) and \((xy)^{-1}\mapsto\text{a conjugate of }(xy)^{-\lambda}\). The two ordered constructions have the same arithmetic restriction. Their sum on \(N\) extends uniquely to a continuous character \(\varepsilon_{\ell,q}:G\to\F_2\) vanishing on \(H\). Whether these relative characters vanish is not determined here.

label: thm:main-structural
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Assume \eqref{eq:decomposition} and the preceding normalization of $\rho_2$. Then $N$ is closed and normal, $N\cap H=K$, and \[ \GT/N\simeq A:=\Gal(K_2/\Q). \] In the affine coordinates $(u,t)$, with product $(u,t)(v,s)=(uv,t+us)$, this quotient is \[ A=\{(u,t)\in\Zh^\times\ltimes\Zh: t\equiv\varepsilon_8(u)\pmod2\}, \] where $\varepsilon_8(u)=0$ for $u\equiv1,7\pmod8$ and $1$ for $u\equiv3,5\pmod8$. There is a canonical topological isomorphism \[ \GT^{\ab}\simeq\Zh^\times\times B,\qquad B=N/\overline{[\GT,N]K}. \] For every prime $p$, restriction identifies \[ \Hom(B,\F_p)\simeq\ker(X_p\longrightarrow Y_p). \] Consequently the relative kernel vanishes for every prime if and only if the multiplier identifies $\GT^{\ab}$ with $\Zh^\times$.

label: thm:main-dimension
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: With the same notation, \[ \dim_{\F_2} X_2=\dim_{\F_2}\operatorname{im}(X_2\longrightarrow Y_2)=\aleph_0. \] For every positive integer $d$, Ihara's integral cocycle $\rho_d^I$ is even on the multiplier-one subgroup of $\GTz$. For every odd prime $q$, \[ \psi_q=\frac{\rho_q^I|_N}{2}\pmod2 \] is an invariant continuous character of $N$. Its restriction is the character of $K_2(q^{1/4})/K_2$, and these restrictions are linearly independent as $q$ varies. For every prime $p$, including odd $p$, $\dim_{\F_p}Y_p=\aleph_0$.

label: thm:main-rational-normalization
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: With the preceding assumptions and notation, the joint map \[ N\longrightarrow\prod_{q\text{ odd prime}}2\Zh, \qquad n\longmapsto(\rho_q^I(n))_q \] is surjective already on $K$. Its kernel $N_{\mathrm{rad}}$ is a proper closed normal subgroup, and \[ \GT=N_{\mathrm{rad}}\GQ,\qquad N_{\mathrm{rad}}\cap\GQ=G_{L_{\mathrm{rad}}},\qquad \GT/N_{\mathrm{rad}}\simeq\Gal(L_{\mathrm{rad}}/\Q). \] The latter quotient consists of the affine coordinates $(u,(t_q)_{q\text{ prime}})$ satisfying $t_q\equiv\epsilon_q(u)\pmod2$, with multiplication $(u,t)(v,s)=(uv,t+us)$; here $\epsilon_q$ is the character of $\Q(\sqrt q)$. The relative abelian quotient is unchanged: \[ B\simeq N_{\mathrm{rad}}/ \overline{[\GT,N_{\mathrm{rad}}]G_{L_{\mathrm{rad}}}}. \] The invariant quadratic characters of $N$ that factor through all rational Kummer coordinates are exactly the finite linear combinations of the $\psi_q$ for odd primes $q$, and restriction is injective on this entire subspace. No nonzero invariant character with values in $\F_p$, for odd $p$, factors through these coordinates.

label: thm:main-all-degree-dyadic
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every $n\ge3$, the full and arithmetic leading images are \[ \operatorname{in}_n(F^nM) =\operatorname{in}_n(F^nM\cap H) =\mathfrak{grt}_1(\Q_2)_n \cap\operatorname{Lie}_{\Z_2}(S,T)_n. \] Arithmetic odd-degree elements freely generate this integral Lie algebra, and their reductions are Willwacher's characteristic-two generators. The full group $\GT$ and $H$ have the same image in $\operatorname{Aut}(\widehat F_2^{(2)})$. The subgroup $R_D$ is closed and normal, and \[ \GT=R_DH,\qquad B\simeq R_D/\overline{[\GT,R_D](R_D\cap H)}. \] Put $m_3(g)=[S^2T]f_g$ and $\eta_3=m_3/8\pmod2$ on $N$. Then $\eta_3\in X_2$, and \[ \ker\bigl(X_2\longrightarrow H^1(R_D,\F_2)\bigr) =\left(\bigoplus_{q\text{ odd prime}}\F_2\psi_q\right) \oplus\F_2\eta_3. \] Arithmetic restriction is injective on this kernel. Let $P$ be the image of $M$ in the dyadic action. It is the free pro-$2$ group on a convergent family with one arithmetic generator in each odd degree at least three. Its integral mass $\mu=\rho_{2,2}^I/2:P\to\Z_2$ is surjective. The images of $N$ and $D$ are both $P_0=\ker\mu$, and \[ H^1(P,\F_2)^G=\F_2(\mu\bmod2),\qquad H^1(P_0,\F_2)^G=\F_2\eta_3. \]

label: thm:main-full-dyadic-image
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Under the preceding hypotheses, the full dyadic action image is \[ \operatorname{im}\bigl(G\to\operatorname{Aut}(\widehat F_2^{(2)})\bigr) \cong C_2*_{\mathrm{pro}\text{-}2}\mathbf Z_2. \] The factors can be generated by complex conjugation and an arithmetic element of dyadic multiplier \(-3\). Its cyclotomic map is its abelianization, with kernel the free pro-two group \(P=M/R_M\).

label: thm:main-all-prime-quadratic-domain
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Both subgroups are closed and normal. Their quotients in $R_D$ are pro-odd, and \[ \begin{aligned} B_{\max2}&\simeq \left(P_D/\overline{[G,P_D](P_D\cap H)}\right)_{\max2}\\ &\simeq \left(T_D/\overline{[G,T_D](T_D\cap H)}\right)_{\max2}. \end{aligned} \] Restriction from $X_2$ to either subgroup has the same rational Kummer-plus-cubic kernel as restriction to $R_D$. The indices $[R_D:P_D]$ and $[R_D\cap\ker d_{(3)}:T_D]$ are infinite. No factorization $G=P_DH$ or $G=T_DH$ is asserted.

label: thm:main-odd-cm-domain
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The subgroup \(U_D=T_D\cap\ker W_{\rm odd}\) is closed and normal, and \[ B_{\max2}\cong \left(U_D/\overline{[G,U_D](U_D\cap H)}\right)_{\max2}. \] Restriction from \(X_2\) to \(U_D\) has the same kernel as restriction to \(R_D\). Moreover \[ W_{\rm odd}(T_D\cap H)=N_4(4)_{\rm odd},\qquad T_D=U_D(T_D\cap H), \] and \(U_D\) has infinite index in \(T_D\), already on the arithmetic intersection. No equality \(G=U_DH\) is asserted.

label: thm:main-exact-joint-odd-cm
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Put \[ \mathcal C_3=\prod_{\ell\ge5} (\mathcal N_{3,\ell,{\rm odd}})^3, \qquad \mathcal A_4=N_4(4)_{\rm odd}, \] with identity components at coefficient primes two and three in \(\mathcal C_3\). Then \[ (T_{\rm odd},W_{\rm odd})(T_D) =(T_{\rm odd},W_{\rm odd})(T_D\cap H) =\mathcal C_3\times\mathcal A_4. \] The cubic image on \(U_D\) is exactly \(\mathcal C_3\), already attained on \(U_D\cap H\). Hence \[ T_D/V_D\simeq\mathcal C_3\times\mathcal A_4, \qquad U_D/V_D\simeq\mathcal C_3, \] and \[ T_D=V_D(T_D\cap H),\qquad U_D=V_D(U_D\cap H). \] In addition, the full coefficient-three cubic frame is the identity on \(P_D\).

label: thm:main-primary-residual
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For a prime \(r\), let \(\Phi_p\) denote the free pro-\(p\) action and put \[ E_r=R_D\cap\bigcap_{p\ne r}\ker\Phi_p. \] This is a closed normal subgroup of infinite index in \(R_D\), and \[ B_{\max r}\cong \left(E_r/\overline{[G,E_r](E_r\cap H)}\right)_{\max r}. \] For odd \(r\), restriction from \(X_r\) to \(H^1(E_r,\mathbf F_r)\) is injective. For \(r=2\), one has \(E_2=P_D\), and the kernel is the rational Kummer span together with \(\mathbf F_2\eta_3\).

label: thm:main-odd-realization-obstruction
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let \(B_g(X,Y)\) be the full adelic Alexander multiplier, and put \[ J_B=D\cap\bigcap_r\ker\Phi_r\cap\ker T\cap\ker W\cap\ker B. \] Here \(T,W\) are the complete corrected cubic and harmonic CM homomorphisms, including every coefficient prime. For every odd prime \(p\), restriction \[ Y_p\longrightarrow H^1(J_B\cap H,\F_p) \] is injective. Its nonzero values can be witnessed by arithmetic elements acting trivially on the integral first homology of every finite abelian cover of the three-punctured projective line, at every coefficient prime. Consequently, if \(\chi\in X_p\) vanishes on \(J_B\), then \(\chi|_K=0\). In particular any original character that factors through the joint realizations defining \(J_B\) has zero arithmetic restriction.

label: thm:main-congruence-frames
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $g=(1,f)\in\GT$ satisfy $\rho_2(g)=0$, and put \[ U=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad V=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\-1&1\end{pmatrix}. \] In the signed adelic braid representation, \[ f(U^2,V^2)=I\quad\text{in }\operatorname{SL}_2(\Zh). \] For the signed cubic and harmonic frame bits $a_3(g),a_2(g)$ of \cite[Lemmas 12--15]{H17}, with the positive signed lifts specified in Section~\ref{sec:global-frame-character}, one has \[ a_2(g)=a_3(g)=\rho_3^I(g)/2\pmod2. \] In particular both signs vanish on $N_{\mathrm{rad}}$.

label: thm:main-finite-dyadic-examples
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Each coordinate is additive on its domain, has conjugation weight \(\lambda_2^j\), and has the displayed image both on that domain and on its intersection with \(H\). \begin{center} \begin{tabular}{@{}cccc@{}} \toprule Weight \(j\)&Domain&Exact image&First possible degree on \(D_j\)\\ \midrule 3&\(D\)&\(8\Z_2\)&5\\ 5&\(D_3\)&\(32\Z_2\)&7\\ 7&\(D_5\)&\(128\Z_2\)&8\\ 8&\(D_7\)&\(\Z_2\)&9\\ 9&\(D_8\)&\(512\Z_2\)&10\\ 10&\(D_9\)&\(\Z_2\)&11\\ \bottomrule \end{tabular} \end{center} Every \(D_j\) is proper in its preceding domain, closed and normal in \(G\), and \[ G=D_jH,\qquad B\simeq D_j/\overline{[G,D_j](D_j\cap H)}. \] For every displayed \(j\), the kernel of restriction from \(X_2\) to \(H^1(D_j,\F_2)\) is \[ \Sigma_0:=\F_2\eta_3\oplus \bigoplus_{q\text{ odd prime}}\F_2\psi_q. \] Moreover \(m_3(N)\subseteq8\Z_2\), and the joint map \[ N\longrightarrow \left(\prod_{q\text{ odd prime}}2\Zh\right)\times8\Z_2, \qquad n\longmapsto((\rho_q^I(n))_q,m_3(n)) \] is surjective already on \(K\). Divide each coordinate by the positive generator of its displayed image and reduce modulo two, obtaining \(\eta_j\). These characters have nonzero arithmetic restrictions. Their extension thresholds are as follows: \(\eta_3\) extends to \(N\); \(\eta_5\) on \(D_3\) does not extend invariantly to \(D\); \(\eta_7\) on \(D_5\) does not extend invariantly to \(D_3\); \(\eta_8\) extends to \(D_5\), but not to \(D_3\); \(\eta_9\) extends to \(D_7\), but not to \(D_5\); and \(\eta_{10}\) extends to \(D_8\), but not to \(D_7\). Each failure also excludes an invariant extension to any larger preceding domain. The joint map \((m_8,m_9):D_7\to\Z_2\times512\Z_2\) is surjective already on \(D_7\cap H\), with kernel \(D_9\). No nonzero combination of \(\eta_7\) and the extension of \(\eta_8\) on \(D_5\) extends invariantly to \(D_3\), and \[ \ker\bigl(H^1(D_3,\F_2)^G\longrightarrow H^1(D_8,\F_2)\bigr) =\F_2\eta_5. \]

label: thm:main-uniform-dyadic-normalization
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Put $C_0=D=N_{\mathrm{rad}}$ and \[ C_r=D\cap\bigcap_{j=1}^r\ker c_{2j+1},\qquad C_\infty=\bigcap_{r\ge0}C_r. \] For every $r\ge1$, the coefficient $m_{2r+1}=[S^{2r}T]f$ is additive on $C_{r-1}$, has conjugation weight $\lambda_2^{2r+1}$, and satisfies \[ m_{2r+1}(C_{r-1})=m_{2r+1}(C_{r-1}\cap H) =2^{2r+1}\Z_2,\qquad \ker(m_{2r+1}|_{C_{r-1}})=C_r. \] All these subgroups are closed and normal, and \[ G=C_rH=C_\infty H,\qquad B\simeq C_\infty/ \overline{[G,C_\infty](C_\infty\cap H)}. \] The subgroup $C_\infty$ is exactly the kernel in $D$ of the dyadic beta multiplier. The kernel of restriction from $X_2$ to $H^1(C_\infty,\F_2)$ is the rational Kummer span together with $\F_2\eta_3$. Finally, $E=C_\infty\cap D_{10}$ has infinite index in $D_{10}$, and \[ G=EH,\qquad B\simeq E/\overline{[G,E](E\cap H)}. \] Its elements have no pro-$2$ Magnus term below degree eleven and have trivial dyadic beta multiplier. The kernel of restriction from $X_2$ to $H^1(E,\F_2)$ is again exactly the rational Kummer span together with $\F_2\eta_3$. The mixed coordinate $b_{11}=[S^6TST^3]f$ on $E$ is additive, has conjugation weight $\lambda_2^{11}$, and has full and arithmetic image $\Z_2$. Its kernel $E'$ is a proper closed normal subgroup whose words start in degree at least twelve, $G=E'H$, and \[ B\simeq E'/\overline{[G,E'](E'\cap H)}. \] The kernel of restriction from $X_2$ to $H^1(E',\F_2)$ is the same rational Kummer span together with $\F_2\eta_3$. More precisely, if $F^n$ denotes the subgroup whose pro-$2$ Magnus words start in degree $n$, then $E'=C_\infty\cap F^{12}$. More generally put $E_n=C_\infty\cap F^n$ for $n=12,13,14,15$. The following leading layers have exact arithmetic images: \[ E_{12}/E_{13}\simeq\Z_2^2,\qquad E_{13}/E_{14}\simeq\Z_2^2,\qquad E_{14}/E_{15}\simeq\Z_2^3. \] For each $n=12,13,14,15$, one has \[ G=E_nH,\qquad B\simeq E_n/\overline{[G,E_n](E_n\cap H)}. \] The kernel of restriction from $X_2$ to $E_n$ is still the rational Kummer span together with $\F_2\eta_3$.

label: thm:main-cm-normalization
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The corrected pair $(T,W)$ has the same full adelic image on $G_1$ and on $G_{\Q^{\ab}}$. Its kernel $C_{\mathrm{CM}}$ in $G_1$ is closed and normal in $\GT$. If $K_3=\Q(\sqrt{-3})$ and $K_4=\Q(i)$, then \[ \GT=C_{\mathrm{CM}}\GQ,\qquad C_{\mathrm{CM}}\cap\GQ=G_{K_3^{\ab}K_4^{\ab}},\qquad \GT/C_{\mathrm{CM}}\simeq \Gal(K_3^{\ab}K_4^{\ab}/\Q). \] Every continuous abelian character of $\GT$ which is trivial on $\GQ$ and whose restriction to $G_1$ factors through $(T,W)$ is zero.

label: thm:main-harmonic-dyadic
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every $g=(1,f_g)\in\GT$ with $\rho_2(g)=0$, the pure harmonic frame satisfies \[ \beta_g(u^2,v^2)^{-1}=f_g(u^2,uvu) \quad\text{in }\widehat B_3. \] Consequently $w_3=\eta$ on $D$, the relative character $\epsilon_h$ is zero, and $\chi_3=\epsilon_c=\tau_3+\eta$.

label: thm:main-cubic-normalized
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every $g=(1,f_g)\in\GT$ with $\rho_3^I(g)=0$, the pure cubic frame satisfies \[ A_g(u^2,v^2)^{-1}=f_g(u^2,uv) \quad\text{in }\widehat B_3. \] Consequently $\epsilon_c=0$ and $\chi_3=0$ on full GT. The exceptional eighth-root-of-three compatibility is therefore satisfied. Joint radical--CM compatibility is equivalent to the remaining tame cubic and harmonic tests displayed above.

label: thm:main-harmonic-beta-residue
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There is one integral identification of the harmonic quadratic order with $\widehat{\Z[i]}$, valid for every $g\in N$ and every coefficient prime, under which $W_g=B_g^{\rm ad}(i,-1)$. Reversing the choice of primitive fourth root conjugates all these values simultaneously. For each odd prime $\ell$, reduce this value modulo $\ell$ and define \[ (-1)^{\vartheta_{\ell,4}(g)} =B_{g,\ell}^{\rm ad}(i,-1)^{(\ell-\chi_{-4}(\ell))/2}. \] Then $\vartheta_{\ell,4}\in X_2$, and \[ \Xi_{\ell,4}|_N=\vartheta_{\ell,4}+\rho_\ell^I/2\pmod2 \] extends uniquely to a continuous quadratic character of $\GT$ that is zero on $H$. On $D$, its vanishing is exactly the tame harmonic square condition. No vanishing or nonvanishing of these characters on full $\GT$ is concluded.

label: thm:main-163-finite-word
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The homomorphism $\Psi:P\to W$ has kernel $A$. The elements $X,Y$ generate $\mathscr D$, giving one finite quotient of $\widehat F_2$ of order $163\cdot4^{162}$. For every $r\in R$, use the conjugator $f_{r^n}$ of the group power $r^n$, with conventions \[ \phi_f(x)=x,\qquad \phi_f(y)=f^{-1}yf,\qquad [x,y]=xyx^{-1}y^{-1}. \] Then \[ \prod_{j=0}^{26}f_{r^n}(X^{a_j},Y^{a_j}) =\bigl(2d^{-2}\Psi(h_{163}(r)),1\bigr) \quad\text{in }\mathscr D. \] In particular, this word is the identity if and only if $h_{163}(r)\in A$. Its values lie in $2d^{-2}W$, an additive subgroup of order four.

label: prop:normalized-congruence-triviality
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $g=(1,f)\in\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$ satisfy $\rho_2(g)=0$. Then \[ f(U^2,V^2)=I \qquad\text{in }\operatorname{SL}_2(\widehat{\mathbb Z}). \] Consequently $\widetilde q\Phi_g=\widetilde q$ on $\widehat B_3$.

label: lem:parabolic-centralizer
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The centralizer of $v$ in $\widehat B$ is $\overline{\langle v\rangle}\simeq\widehat{\mathbb Z}$, and it has trivial intersection with $\mathcal C$.

label: cor:level-three-exact-gate
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For a normalized $g=(1,f)\in\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$, put $q=f(u^2,v^2)\in\widehat B$. The element $q$ lies in $\mathcal C$, hence in $\overline{\Gamma_0(3)}$. The automorphism $\Phi_g$ preserves that subgroup. For $d_3:\overline{\Gamma_0(3)}\to\widehat B$ induced by conjugation by $\operatorname{diag}(3,1)$, set \[ h_3=d_3(q)q^{-1}. \] Then $h_3\in\mathcal C$, and strict compatibility with both level-three degeneracy maps is equivalent to the exact identity \[ d_3(q)=q. \]

label: lem:all-finite-unitarity
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Suppose that $\lambda_g=1$. Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $a,b\in\overline{\mathbb F}_p^\times$ have finite orders prime to $p$. Then \[ B_g(a,b)B_g(a^{-1},b^{-1})=1. \] In fact $B_g(a,b)=1$ if $a=1$, $b=1$, or $ab=1$.

label: thm:odd-anderson-character
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $p\equiv5\pmod{12}$ be prime, and let $n\geq1$ satisfy $\gcd(n,3p)=1$. Choose a primitive cube root $\omega\in\mathbb F_{p^2}$. The expression \begin{equation} E_{p,n}(g)= \frac{\displaystyle\prod_{k=0}^{n-1}B_g(\omega,\omega^k)} {\displaystyle\prod_{\xi^n=1}B_g(\xi,\omega)} \label{eq:odd-anderson-defect} \end{equation} belongs to the norm-one subgroup of $\mathbb F_{p^2}^\times$. Here all evaluations are reduced modulo $p$, and the denominator ranges over all $n$th roots in $\overline{\mathbb F}_p$. The rule \begin{equation} (-1)^{\Theta_{p,n}(g)}=E_{p,n}(g)^{(p+1)/2} \label{eq:odd-anderson-sign} \end{equation} defines a continuous homomorphism $G_0\to\mathbb F_2$, independent of the choice between $\omega$ and $\omega^2$. It vanishes on $G_{\mathbb Q}$. In particular its restriction to $G$ is an explicit candidate for a nonzero element of $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cts}}(G/\langle\!\langle G_{\mathbb Q}\rangle\!\rangle,\mathbb F_2)$. The theorem does not assert that this restriction is nonzero.

label: cor:concrete-radical-anderson-character
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $H=G_{\mathbb Q}$ and let $N_{\mathrm{rad}}$ be the simultaneous kernel in $G$ of the multiplier and the rational-prime Kummer cocycles. Put \[ L_{\mathrm{rad}}=\mathbb Q(\mu_\infty,q^{1/m}: q\text{ prime},\ m\geq1), \qquad K_{\mathrm{rad}}=G_{L_{\mathrm{rad}}}. \] Assume the simultaneous normalization $G=N_{\mathrm{rad}}H$, with $N_{\mathrm{rad}}\cap H=K_{\mathrm{rad}}$, and identify the relative abelian quotient as \[ B=N_{\mathrm{rad}}/ \overline{[G,N_{\mathrm{rad}}]K_{\mathrm{rad}}}. \] For a primitive cube root $\omega\in\mathbb F_{289}$ the formula \begin{equation} (-1)^{\psi_{17,11}(u)}= \left(\prod_{\substack{\xi^{11}=1\\\xi\ne1}} B_u(\xi,\omega)\right)^9, \qquad u\in N_{\mathrm{rad}}, \label{eq:concrete-radical-anderson-sign} \end{equation} defines a continuous $G$-invariant quadratic character vanishing on $K_{\mathrm{rad}}$. It therefore gives a precisely specified element of $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cts}}(B,\mathbb F_2)$. Its unique extension to $G$ vanishing on $H$ is $\Theta_{17,11}$. In particular $\psi_{17,11}$ is nonzero if and only if $\Theta_{17,11}|_G$ is nonzero; neither nonvanishing assertion is proved here.

label: prop:formal-odd-sign
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There exists a Frobenius-equivariant sign-valued formal gamma function at the prime $17$ whose beta coboundary satisfies beta associativity, symmetry, the unitary relation, and the duplication formula, but for which the expression in \eqref{eq:odd-anderson-gamma} with $n=11$ equals $-1$. It may be taken constant in the pro-$17$ directions, so all its logarithmic derivatives vanish. This is a non-implication statement for the listed formal identities. It does not provide a solution of the full nonabelian relations $(K_n)$ or of the pentagon equation.

label: thm:odd-harmonic-cm-gate
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Put \[ P_D=D\cap\bigcap_p\ker\Phi_p,\qquad T_D=P_D\cap\ker d_{\eqref{eq:odd-cm-3}}, \] where \(d_{\eqref{eq:odd-cm-3}}\) is the cubic radical--CM defect. Let \(W_{\rm odd}\) be the projection of the harmonic CM homomorphism \(W:D\to N_4(4)\) onto the maximal pro-odd factor, and put \[ U_D=T_D\cap\ker W_{\rm odd}. \] Then \(U_D\) is closed and normal in \(G\), and \begin{equation} B_{\max2}\cong \left(U_D/\overline{[G,U_D](U_D\cap H)}\right)_{\max2}. \label{eq:odd-cm-1} \end{equation} The kernel of the original restriction map is \begin{equation} \ker\bigl(X_2\to H^1(U_D,\mathbf F_2)\bigr) =\bigoplus_{q\ {\rm odd}}\mathbf F_2\psi_q \oplus\mathbf F_2\eta_3. \label{eq:odd-cm-2} \end{equation} Moreover \begin{equation} [T_D:U_D]=\infty,\qquad [T_D\cap H:U_D\cap H]=\infty. \label{eq:odd-cm-3} \end{equation}

label: cor:full-odd-harmonic-arithmetic-image
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let \(A_{4,\rm odd}=N_4(4)_{\rm odd}\). Then \[ W_{\rm odd}(T_D\cap H)=W_{\rm odd}(T_D)=A_{4,\rm odd}, \qquad T_D/U_D\cong A_{4,\rm odd}. \] Moreover \(T_D=U_D(T_D\cap H)\). This factorization is internal to \(T_D\).

label: lem:odd-relative-kernel
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let \(G=DH\) be a profinite group with \(D\) closed and normal, and put \(K=D\cap H\). Suppose \(E\) is a closed normal subgroup of \(G\), with \(K\subset E\subset D\), such that \(D/E\) is pro-\(3\). For every finite abelian \(2\)-group \(A\), restriction is a canonical bijection \[ \begin{aligned} \{\chi\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cts}(G,A):\chi(H)=0\} &\longrightarrow\\ &\{\psi\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cts}(E,A)^G:\psi(K)=0\}. \end{aligned} \] Consequently the maximal pro-\(2\) quotient of the relative abelian group can be computed as the maximal pro-\(2\) quotient of \[ E/\overline{[G,E]K}. \] This does not assert \(G=EH\) or equality of the full relative abelian quotients before taking their pro-\(2\) parts.

label: thm:odd-full-galois-target
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Inflation gives an isomorphism \[ H^2(U,\mathbf F_p)\simeq H^2(A,\mathbf F_p). \] In fact the corresponding inflation is an isomorphism in every degree. The arithmetic inflation images of the \(\delta_\ell\), for \(\ell\in\mathcal S_p\), form a basis of \(H^2(G_{\mathbf Q},\mathbf F_p)\). Order \(\{0\}\cup\mathcal S_p\) with zero first. For each \(i<j\), there is a unique finite linear combination \(D_{ij}\) of the \(\delta_\ell\) having the same arithmetic image as \(\gamma_i\smile\gamma_j\). The transgression is an isomorphism \[ Y_p\simeq \ker\bigl(H^2(A,\mathbf F_p) \longrightarrow H^2(G_{\mathbf Q},\mathbf F_p)\bigr), \] and the inverse images of \(\gamma_i\smile\gamma_j-D_{ij}\), identified with classes of \(A\) by inflation, form a basis of \(Y_p\). Every linear combination here has finite support.

label: lem:full-integral-alexander-unitarity
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every \(g\in M\), \begin{equation}\label{eq:full-alexander-unitarity} B_g(X,Y)B_g(X^{-1},Y^{-1})=1 \end{equation} in the full completed adelic group algebra. Consequently, for complex conjugation \(c\) and any \(z\in M\), \begin{equation}\label{eq:full-alexander-symmetrization} B_{z c z c^{-1}}=1. \end{equation}

label: cor:odd-target-invisible-abelian-covers
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let \(J\) be the common radical, primewise-word, and signed-CM kernel from the preceding theorem, and put \[ J_B=J\cap\ker B. \] For every odd prime \(p\), restriction \[ Y_p\longrightarrow H^1(J_B\cap H,\mathbf F_p) \] is injective. Every witness \(w_{ij}\) from that theorem lies in \(J_B\cap H\), with the same diagonal evaluation \(\kappa_{ab}(w_{ij})=2\delta_{ai}\delta_{bj}\). Each witness acts trivially on the full adelic first homology of every finite abelian cover of the punctured line. In particular, Fermat-cover homology alone cannot provide a full GT lift of a nonzero odd target character.

label: thm:odd-target-survives-all-standard-kernels
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For each pair \(i<j\), there is an arithmetic element \(w_{ij}\in J_H\) such that, for every \(a<b\), \begin{equation}\label{eq:odd-mixed-evaluation} \kappa_{ab}(w_{ij})=2\,\delta_{ai}\delta_{bj}. \end{equation} Consequently restriction \[ Y_p\longrightarrow H^1(J_H,\mathbf F_p) \] is injective. In particular, if \(\chi\in H^1(N,\mathbf F_p)^G\) factors through the joint rational Kummer, primewise word, and two-frame realization of \(N\), then \(\chi|_K=0\). Thus no nonzero odd arithmetic target character can be obtained solely from those realizations. This conclusion does not assert that a target character fails to extend to full GT.

label: lem:coprime-relative-general
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let \(G=RH\), with \(R\) closed normal and \(H\) closed. Let \(E\triangleleft G\) be closed and contained in \(R\), and suppose every finite quotient of \(R/E\) has order prime to \(r\). For each finite abelian \(r\)-group \(A\), restriction gives a bijection between continuous characters \(G\to A\) killing \(H\) and continuous \(G\)-invariant characters \(E\to A\) killing \(E\cap H\).

label: thm:primary-residual-gate
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For a prime \(r\), put \[ E_r=R_D\cap\bigcap_{p\ne r}\ker\Phi_p, \qquad X_r=H^1(N,\mathbf F_r)^G, \] where \(\Phi_p\) is the action on the free pro-\(p\) group. Then \(E_r\) is closed and normal in \(G\), and \begin{equation} B_{\max r}\cong \left(E_r/\overline{[G,E_r](E_r\cap H)}\right)_{\max r}. \label{eq:primary-residual-1} \end{equation} For odd \(r\), restriction \[ X_r\longrightarrow H^1(E_r,\mathbf F_r) \] is injective. For \(r=2\), its kernel is \begin{equation} \bigoplus_{q\ {\rm odd}}\mathbf F_2\psi_q \oplus\mathbf F_2\eta_3. \label{eq:primary-residual-2} \end{equation} Moreover \(E_r\) has infinite index in \(R_D\).

label: thm:fr-uniform-dyadic-saturation
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every degree $n\ge3$, the full and arithmetic leading images are the entire integral Grothendieck--Teichm\"uller Lie lattice: \[ \operatorname{in}_n(F^nM) =\operatorname{in}_n(F^nM\cap H) =\mathcal L_n, \qquad \mathcal L_n= \mathfrak{grt}_1(\mathbf Q_2)_n \cap\operatorname{Lie}_{\mathbf Z_2}(S,T)_n. \] There are arithmetic elements $z_{2r+1}\in H_M\cap F^{2r+1}M$ whose reduced leading terms are precisely the characteristic-two free generators of Willwacher's Theorem~1.3. Their leading terms freely generate $\mathcal L=\bigoplus_n\mathcal L_n$ over $\mathbf Z_2$. One has \[ M=RH_M,\qquad G=RH,\qquad G=R_DH. \] In particular the full-GT and arithmetic images in $\operatorname{Aut}(\widehat F_2^{(2)})$ coincide. The normalized subgroup $R_D$ is closed and normal, and \[ B\simeq R_D/\overline{[G,R_D](R_D\cap H)}. \] The kernel of restriction from $X_2=H^1(N,\mathbf F_2)^G$ to $R_D$ is exactly \[ \left(\bigoplus_{q\ {\rm odd\ prime}}\mathbf F_2\psi_q\right) \oplus\mathbf F_2\eta_3. \] Moreover $R_D$ is a proper subgroup of infinite index in $E_{15}=C_\infty\cap F^{15}M$.

label: lem:fr-integral-leading-basis
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The finite-rank module $\mathcal L_n$ is saturated in $\operatorname{Lie}_{\mathbf Z_2}(S,T)_n$, and reduction gives an injection \[ \mathcal L_n/2\mathcal L_n \hookrightarrow\mathfrak{grt}_1(\mathbf F_2)_n. \] If a collection of elements of $\mathcal L_n$ reduces to a basis of the space on the right, it is a $\mathbf Z_2$-basis of $\mathcal L_n$.

label: lem:fr-minus-three-jet
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Choose $h\in H$ with $t=\lambda(h)$ and $t_2=-3$. Put $C=[S,T]$. For $z\in F^nM$, $n\ge3$, write $q=\operatorname{in}_n(z)$ and define, using the full profinite exponent, \[ \Delta_n(z)=hzh^{-1}z^{-t^n}. \] Then $\Delta_n(z)\in F^{n+1}M$, and its Magnus series satisfies \begin{equation}\label{eq:fr-minus-three-jet} f_{\Delta_n(z)} \equiv1+\{C,\overline q\} \pmod{\,2,\ (S,T)^{n+3}}. \end{equation} In particular every coefficient through degree $n+1$ is even, while its degree-$n+2$ term modulo two is the indicated Ihara bracket.

label: prop:fr-all-odd-arithmetic-generators
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There exist elements $z_{2r+1}\in H_M\cap F^{2r+1}M$ whose leading reductions are the generators \[ s_3=[S+T,[S,T]],\qquad s_{2r+3}=\{C,s_{2r+1}\} \] of $\mathfrak{grt}_1(\mathbf F_2)$. In each degree the leading terms of the corresponding arithmetic Hall commutator words form a $\mathbf Z_2$-basis of $\mathcal L_n$.

label: thm:normalized-protwo-free
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Put \(M=\ker\lambda\) and \[ R_M=\{g\in M:f_g=1\text{ in the free pro-two group}\}, \qquad P=M/R_M. \] Then \(P\) is free pro-two on a countable family converging to the identity. This family can be chosen arithmetically. More precisely, choose the square-corrected arithmetic family \(a_3=\sigma,a_5,a_7,\ldots\), whose leading reductions are the free generators of \(\mathfrak{grt}_1(\mathbf F_2)\), and for which \(a_{j+2}\) is \([h_*,a_j]\) followed by inverse-square corrections, where \(\lambda_2(h_*)=-3\). If \(F_r\) is the free pro-two group on \(z_3,\ldots,z_{2r+1}\), with transition maps killing the last generator, then \begin{equation} \varprojlim_r F_r \ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ P, \qquad z_j\longmapsto a_jR_M. \label{eq:normalized-protwo-1} \end{equation} In particular \(H^2_{\rm cts}(P,\mathbf F_2)=0\).

label: cor:protwo-image-invariant-characters
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For the family in Theorem~\ref{thm:normalized-protwo-free}, put \(V=P/\overline{P^2[P,P]}\) and \(T=h_*-1\). Then \begin{equation} V\simeq\mathbf F_2[[T]],\qquad [a_{3+2r}]=T^r[a_3],\qquad h_*=1+T. \label{eq:normalized-protwo-3} \end{equation} The dyadic mass \(\mu=\rho_{2,2}^I/2:P\to\mathbf Z_2\) is surjective. For \(P_0=\ker\mu\), \begin{equation} N/(N\cap R_M)\simeq D/R_D\simeq P_0, \label{eq:normalized-protwo-4} \end{equation} and \begin{equation} H^1(P,\mathbf F_2)^G=\mathbf F_2(\mu\bmod2), \qquad H^1(P_0,\mathbf F_2)^G=\mathbf F_2\eta_3. \label{eq:normalized-protwo-5} \end{equation} Thus every invariant quadratic character of \(M,N,\) or \(D\) that factors through its full pro-two parameter image already factors through the dyadic beta quotient.

label: lem:fr-pure-eleven-certificate
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every full-GT element whose dyadic word starts in degree eleven, with degree-eleven leading term $q$, one has \[ q=\frac{[S^{10}T]q}{8448}L_{11} +\frac{[S^6TST^3]q}{11}\{P_3,L_8\}. \] In particular $[S^{10}T]L_{11}=8448$, $[S^6TST^3]L_{11}=0$, and $L_{11}$ is primitive as an integral $2$-adic coefficient vector.

label: thm:radical-cm-intersection
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: One has \begin{align} L_{\mathrm{rad}}\cap L_{\mathrm{CM}} &=L_{\mathrm{rad}}\cap F_{12}^{\mathrm{ab}}\notag\\ &=k\bigl(q^{1/12}:q\in\mathcal P,\, 2^{1/8},3^{1/8}\bigr)=:I. \label{eq:radical-cm-intersection} \end{align} In particular \begin{equation} \operatorname{Gal}(I/k)\simeq (\mathbb Z/12)^2\times \prod_{q\in\mathcal P\setminus\{2,3\}}\mathbb Z/6. \label{eq:radical-cm-common-group} \end{equation} The first two factors are indexed by $2,3$. In these coordinates conjugation by an element of $G_{\mathbb Q}$ is multiplication by its cyclotomic character, reduced modulo the indicated orders.

label: prop:radical-cm-joint-gate
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $G=(N_{\mathrm{rad}}\cap C_{\mathrm{CM}})H$; \item the joint radical and CM image of $G$ equals that of $H$; \item $a=b$, or equivalently $d=0$. \end{enumerate} Thus the remaining compatibility has exponent dividing twelve over $k$: it consists of one cubic coordinate for every rational prime, one quadratic coordinate for each prime other than $2,3$, and one coordinate modulo four for each of $2,3$.

label: lem:simultaneous-kummer-image
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For distinct rational primes $q_1,\ldots,q_m$, the joint Kummer map \[ G_{\mathbb Q^{\mathrm{ab}}}\longrightarrow\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{\,m}, \qquad \sigma\longmapsto (\kappa_{q_1}(\sigma),\ldots,\kappa_{q_m}(\sigma)) \] has image exactly $2\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{\,m}$. Consequently, for distinct odd primes $q_1,\ldots,q_m$, its restriction to $K=G_{K_2}$ also has image $2\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{\,m}$.

label: thm:rational-radical-normalization
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The joint map \[ \mathcal R:N\longrightarrow \prod_{\substack{q\in\mathcal P\\q\ne2}}2\widehat{\mathbb Z}, \qquad n\longmapsto(\rho_q^I(n))_q \] is surjective already on $K$. Its kernel is $N_{\mathrm{rad}}$, and \[ N=N_{\mathrm{rad}}K,\qquad G=N_{\mathrm{rad}}H,\qquad N_{\mathrm{rad}}\cap H=K_{\mathrm{rad}}. \] In particular $N_{\mathrm{rad}}$ is a proper closed normal subgroup of $N$, and \[ N/N_{\mathrm{rad}}\simeq \prod_{\substack{q\in\mathcal P\\q\ne2}}2\widehat{\mathbb Z}. \] There are canonical topological isomorphisms \begin{align*} G/N_{\mathrm{rad}}&\simeq \operatorname{Gal}(L_{\mathrm{rad}}/\mathbb Q),\\ B&\simeq N_{\mathrm{rad}}/ \overline{[G,N_{\mathrm{rad}}]K_{\mathrm{rad}}}. \end{align*} The first quotient is explicitly \[ A_{\mathrm{rad}}= \left\{(u,(t_q)_{q\in\mathcal P}): \begin{array}{l} u\in\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{\times},\quad t_q\in\widehat{\mathbb Z},\\ t_q\equiv\epsilon_q(u)\pmod2\quad(q\in\mathcal P) \end{array}\right\}, \] with multiplication $(u,t)(v,s)=(uv,t+us)$, where $\epsilon_q$ is the quadratic character of $\mathbb Q(\sqrt q)$.

label: cor:rational-kummer-characters
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The invariant quadratic characters of $N$ that factor through all rational Kummer coordinates form exactly \[ X_2^{\mathrm{Kum}}= \bigoplus_{\substack{q\in\mathcal P\\q\ne2}} \mathbb F_2\,\psi_q^N. \] Restriction to $K$ is injective on this subspace. For an odd prime $p$, no nonzero invariant $\mathbb F_p$-character of $N$ factors through the rational Kummer coordinates. For every prime $p$, the unresolved relative kernel is equivalently \[ \operatorname{Hom}(B,\mathbb F_p)= \left\{\chi\in H^1(N_{\mathrm{rad}},\mathbb F_p)^G: \chi|_{K_{\mathrm{rad}}}=0\right\}. \]

label: prop:radical-character-pullback
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every prime $p$, put \[ X_p^{\mathrm{rad}}=H^1(N_{\mathrm{rad}},\mathbb F_p)^G, \qquad Y_p^{\mathrm{rad}}=H^1(K_{\mathrm{rad}},\mathbb F_p)^H. \] The restriction maps identify $X_p$ with the fiber product \[ X_p\simeq X_p^{\mathrm{rad}} \mathop{\times}_{Y_p^{\mathrm{rad}}}Y_p. \] The kernels of $X_p\to X_p^{\mathrm{rad}}$ and $Y_p\to Y_p^{\mathrm{rad}}$ are identified by restriction. They are zero for odd $p$, and for $p=2$ they are respectively $X_2^{\mathrm{Kum}}$ and its restriction to $K$.

label: prop:normalized-comparison
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There is a natural homeomorphism of right-coset spaces \[ N/K\longrightarrow G/H,\qquad nK\longmapsto nH. \] In particular $G=H$ if and only if $N=K$. Put $N_0=\ker(\lambda:\GTz\to U)\cap\ker\rho_2$. Then $\GTz=N_0H$. If a continuous homomorphism from $\GTz$ to any topological group is trivial on $H$, its restriction to $G$ is trivial if and only if its restriction to $N$ is trivial.

label: prop:lr-abstract-countermodel
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Separate arithmetic quotient identifications do not imply vanishing of a cyclotomically crossed defect. Even a trivial ordinary relative abelian quotient does not force its order-three component to vanish.

label: prop:lr-integral-cubic-beta
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For $g\in N$, an integral identification of the quadratic orders identifies $T_g$ with either $(-1)^{a_2(g)}\nu_g$ or $(-1)^{a_2(g)}\overline{\nu_g}$. For $g\in D$ the sign is one. No uniform orientation is needed for cube membership or for the scalar modulo-eight bit.

label: lem:lr-cubic-cm-quotient
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The maximal exponent-three subextension of $K_3^{\mathrm{ab}}/k$ is $k(q^{1/3}:q\text{ rational prime})$. The order-three part of $d$ is therefore zero if and only if $T_g\in N_3(4)^3$ for every $g\in D$.

label: lem:lr-wild-three-cube
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every $g\in D$, the three-adic component of $\nu_g$ is a cube in the norm-one units of $\mathbb Z_3[\omega]$.

label: thm:lr-tame-cubic-gate
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The order-three component of $d$ vanishes if and only if, for all $g\in D$ and primes $\ell\ge5$, \begin{equation} B_{g,\ell}(\omega,\omega)^{(\ell-\chi_{-3}(\ell))/3}=1 \quad\text{in the residue norm-one torus}. \label{eq:lr-tame-cubic-test} \end{equation} Use a primitive cube root in $\mathbb F_\ell$ in the split case and in $\mathbb F_{\ell^2}$ in the inert case.

label: prop:lr-formal-beta-obstruction
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Beta associativity, unitarity, all dyadic Anderson identities, vanishing integral Kummer coordinates, and the logarithmic derivatives of the Anderson identities do not, as formal integral Alexander identities, imply all tests \eqref{eq:lr-tame-cubic-test}.

label: lem:lr-quartic-cm-quotient
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The maximal elementary-two subextension of $K_4^{\mathrm{ab}}/k$ is \[k(q^{1/4}:q\text{ rational prime}).\]

label: lem:lr-cubic-eight-field
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: One has $k(E_3[8])=k(\alpha,v)$. The scalar automorphism $[-1]$ of this division field fixes $v$. On $H^{\mathrm{cyc}}$, if \[ T_{\sigma,2}\equiv(1+4\tau(\sigma))I\pmod8, \qquad \tau(\sigma)\in\mathbb F_2, \] then $\sigma(v)/v=(-1)^{\tau(\sigma)}$.

label: prop:lr-exceptional-three-character
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The character $\chi_3=w_3+\tau_3$ on $D$ is $G$-invariant and zero on $D\cap H$. It extends uniquely to an ordinary continuous quadratic character on $G$ that is zero on $H$. Its vanishing is exactly the remaining compatibility for $3^{1/8}$, once the known quartic coordinate of three is imposed. Moreover \[ \tau_3(g)=\frac{B_{g,2}(\omega,\omega)-1}{4}\pmod2, \] where the right side is scalar, in $\mathbb F_2\subset\mathbb F_4$.

label: prop:seven-inertia-mixed-prime-witness
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There is an arithmetic element \(w\in T_D\) for which every single-prime word action is trivial and \[ W_7(w)=\left(\frac{1+7i}{1-7i}\right)^{-2}. \] This value has infinite order.

label: lem:arithmetic-normalization-annihilator
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let \(G=NH\) be a profinite group, where \(N\) is closed and normal and \(H\) is closed. Put \(K=N\cap H\). Let \(R\subseteq N\) be closed and normal in \(G\), with \(G=RH\), and put \(J=R\cap H\). For any finite abelian group \(C\) with trivial action, restriction induces an isomorphism \[ \ker\bigl(\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cts}(N,C)^G \to\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cts}(R,C)\bigr) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \ker\bigl(\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cts}(K,C)^H \to\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cts}(J,C)\bigr). \]

label: thm:simultaneous-quadratic-normalization
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The joint homomorphism \[ (\mathfrak t_2,(\xi_{\ell,q})_{\mathcal I}) :R_D\longrightarrow\mathcal U\times\mathcal P \] is surjective already on \(R_D\cap H\), and remains surjective on \(V_D\cap H\). Consequently \[ R_D/R^*\simeq\mathcal U\times\mathcal P, \qquad V_D/V^*\simeq\mathcal U\times\mathcal P. \] Both quotient descriptions hold on the arithmetic intersections as well. Moreover \[ G=R^*H,\qquad B\simeq R^*/\overline{[G,R^*](R^*\cap H)}, \] and \[ B_{\max2}\simeq \left(V^*/\overline{[G,V^*](V^*\cap H)}\right)_{\max2}. \] Restriction from \(X_2\) to either \(R^*\) or \(V^*\) has kernel \[ \Sigma_0\oplus\F_2\tau\oplus \bigoplus_{(\ell,q)\in\mathcal I}\F_2\xi_{\ell,q}. \] Arithmetic restriction is injective on this kernel. In particular \(V^*\) is a proper subgroup of infinite index in \(V_D\), already on the arithmetic intersection.

label: thm:main-simultaneous-quadratic
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The integral logarithm defines an invariant character \[ \tau=\frac{\log\mathfrak t_2}{4\delta}\pmod2\in H^1(M,\F_2)^G, \qquad \tau|_K=\kappa_{2,3}+\psi_3. \] The joint map \[ (\mathfrak t_2,(\xi_{\ell,q})_{\mathcal I},(\nu_p)_{\mathcal J}):R_D \longrightarrow\mathcal U\times\prod_{\mathcal I}\F_2 \times\prod_{\mathcal J}\F_2 \] is surjective already on \(R_D\cap H\), and also on \(V_D\cap H\). Define \[ \begin{split} R_{\rm quad}&=R_D\cap\ker\mathfrak t_2 \cap\bigcap_{\mathcal I}\ker\xi_{\ell,q} \cap\bigcap_{\mathcal J}\ker\nu_p,\\ V_{\rm quad}&=V_D\cap R_{\rm quad}. \end{split} \] These subgroups are closed and normal in \(G\), and \[ \begin{gathered} R_D/R_{\rm quad}\simeq V_D/V_{\rm quad} \simeq\mathcal U\times\prod_{\mathcal I}\F_2 \times\prod_{\mathcal J}\F_2,\\ G=R_{\rm quad}H,\qquad B\simeq R_{\rm quad}/ \overline{[G,R_{\rm quad}](R_{\rm quad}\cap H)},\\ B_{\max2}\simeq \left(V_{\rm quad}/ \overline{[G,V_{\rm quad}](V_{\rm quad}\cap H)}\right)_{\max2}. \end{gathered} \] The two quotient descriptions also hold on arithmetic intersections. Restriction from \(X_2\) to either residual subgroup has kernel exactly \(\mathcal S=s(Y_2)\). Its image is precisely the space of invariant quadratic characters on that subgroup vanishing on its arithmetic intersection, canonically identified with \(\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cts}(B,\F_2)\).

label: prop:tame-harmonic-word-gate
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every $g\in D$ the corrected harmonic frame satisfies \begin{equation}\label{eq:tame-harmonic-1} W_g=f_g(U^2,S)\qquad\text{in }\mathrm{SL}_2(\widehat{\mathbb Z}). \end{equation} Consequently its residue belongs to the cyclic group \[ \mathcal T_\ell =\{aI+bS_\ell:a,b\in\mathbb F_\ell,\ a^2+b^2=1\}, \qquad |\mathcal T_\ell|=\ell-\chi_{-4}(\ell). \] The simultaneous compatibility of the radical and CM actions on every rational quartic root is equivalent to the following family of finite word identities: \begin{equation}\label{eq:tame-harmonic-2} \boxed{\quad f_g(U_\ell^2,S_\ell)^{m_\ell}=I \qquad(g\in D,\ \ell\ge5\text{ prime}).\quad} \end{equation} For a fixed $g$, the same equivalence holds pointwise. This is a reformulation of the remaining tame quartic gate; it does not assert the identities in \eqref{eq:tame-harmonic-2}.

label: prop:ns-lns-comparison
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Use the compatible standard markings of Nakamura--Schneps \cite[Theorem 11.2]{NS2000} and Lochak--Nakamura--Schneps \cite[Theorem 1.1]{LNS}. For $F=(\lambda,f)\in\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}$, write $\rho=\rho_2(F)$ and \[ w_1=1,\qquad w_j=(a_1\cdots a_{j-1})^j\quad(2\leq j\leq2g), \qquad K_F=\prod_{j=2}^{2g}w_j^{\,(-1)^{j+1}4\rho}. \] Let $A_F^{\mathrm{NS2000}}$ denote the standard quilt representative and $A_F^{\mathrm{LNS}}$ the representative given by the explicit chain formulas. On each of $\widehat\Gamma_{g,0}$ and $\widehat\Gamma_{g,1}$ one has \[ A_F^{\mathrm{NS2000}}=\operatorname{Ad}(K_F)\circ A_F^{\mathrm{LNS}}. \] In particular the two outer actions are equal. If $\rho_2(F)=0$, these standard representatives themselves are equal.

label: prop:nonunique-stabilizer-extension
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $\sigma=\{\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_{g-1}\}$ be a cut system with connected complement, and let $H$ be its oriented stabilizer in the full profinite pure mapping class group. Let $H_i$ be the oriented stabilizer of $\sigma\setminus\{\gamma_i\}$. The identity of $H$ has more than one inertia-preserving extension to $H_i$.

label: prop:degeneracy-two
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $F=(1,f)$ be a normalized element of $\widehat{\operatorname{GT}}$. Let $\Phi_F$ be its standard action on $\widehat B$, so that \[ \Phi_F(u)=u,\qquad \Phi_F(v)=q^{-1}vq,\qquad q=f(u^2,v^2). \] Then $\Phi_F$ preserves the closure of $\Gamma_0(2)$, and its restriction commutes with both degeneracy maps to $\widehat B$.

label: prop:local-brauer-frame
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let \[ \mathcal D=\{(T,W)\in\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb Z_3)^2: \operatorname{tr}(T)\operatorname{tr}(W^2)\in\mathbb Z_3^\times\}. \] On this domain define \[ \mathfrak b(T,W)= \big[(\operatorname{tr}(T)\operatorname{tr}(W^2),3)_{\mathbb Q_3}\big] \in\operatorname{Br}(\mathbb Q_3)[2]. \] Here brackets denote a quaternion algebra's Brauer class. This invariant is unchanged by independent conjugation of $T$ and $W$. Suppose their reductions have the form \[ \bar T\in(-I)^{\epsilon_3}\langle R_0\rangle, \qquad \bar W\in S_0^{\epsilon_2}\langle-I\rangle, \] where $R_0$ is the standard nonidentity unipotent matrix of order three in $\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb F_3)$ and $S_0^2=-I$. Then $(T,W)\in\mathcal D$ and \[ \mathfrak b(T,W)=(\epsilon_2+\epsilon_3) [(-1,-3)_{\mathbb Q_3}]. \] Its local Hilbert sign is $(-1)^{\epsilon_2+\epsilon_3}$.

label: prop:quartic-conductor
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The extension $L/K$ is cyclic of degree four. Its two faithful finite-order Hecke characters are $\psi,\psi^{-1}$ and \[ \mathfrak f(\psi)=\mathfrak f(\psi^{-1})=\mathfrak p^6, \qquad \mathfrak f(\psi^2)=\mathfrak p^4. \] All three characters have trivial infinity type. The absolute discriminant of $L$ is $2^{24}$. The representation $\operatorname{Ind}_{G_K}^{G_{\mathbb Q}}\psi$ is odd and irreducible of dimension two, has conductor $256$, and has determinant $\chi_{-4}$.

label: prop:twist-determinant-beta
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For the four block-substitution actions of an acyclotomic element \((1,f)\), the Fox determinants are respectively \[ B_f(X,Y),\qquad B_f(Y,Z),\qquad B_f(XY,Z),\qquad B_f(X,YZ) \] for \(F^{1,2},F^{2,3},F^{12,3},F^{1,23}\). The action on the rank-three fiber of the pure-braid proword \(f(x_{12},x_{23})\) has determinant one. Consequently, at the determinant level the twist relation gives exactly \begin{equation} B_f(X,Y)B_f(XY,Z)=B_f(X,YZ)B_f(Y,Z). \label{eq:twist-determinant-beta} \end{equation} This determinant operation supplies no scalar equation beyond the beta two-cocycle identity.

label: lem:twist-direct-pure-braid
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: On the fiber \(\widehat F_3=\langle x,y,z\rangle\), \begin{align*} \operatorname{Inn}(u)(x)&=(xy)^{-1}x(xy)=y^{-1}xy,\\ \operatorname{Inn}(u)(y)&=(xy)^{-1}y(xy)=y^{-1}x^{-1}yxy,\\ \operatorname{Inn}(u)(z)&=z, \end{align*} and \begin{align*} \operatorname{Inn}(v)(x)&=x,\\ \operatorname{Inn}(v)(y)&=(yz)^{-1}y(yz)=z^{-1}yz,\\ \operatorname{Inn}(v)(z)&=(yz)^{-1}z(yz)=z^{-1}y^{-1}zyz. \end{align*} In particular both base generators fix \(xyz\), and commute with \(w=(xyz)^{-1}\).

label: prop:twist-oriented-pentagon
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: With these conventions, \begin{equation} L=\operatorname{Inn}(f(v,u))R, \qquad \operatorname{Inn}(f(x_{23},x_{12})) =F^{1,2}F^{12,3}(F^{1,23})^{-1}(F^{2,3})^{-1}. \label{eq:twist-oriented} \end{equation} The equalities are automorphisms of the rank-three fiber.

label: cor:twist-finite-scalar-and-commutator
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For an acyclotomic full GT element, the finite matrices satisfy \eqref{eq:twist-finite-word}. For \(r\in R_{\rm global}\), the first layer after the GT group power \(2^{81}+1\) determines \(\Psi(h_{163}(r))\). For any two multiplier-one elements \(r_1,r_2\), one has \[ f_{[r_1,r_2]}(A_t,B_t)=1. \] Thus this specialization cannot detect the commutator value of the relative quaternion obstruction.

label: thm:uniform-odd-arithmetic-image
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every integer $r\ge1$, the coefficient \[ m_{2r+1}(g)=[S^{2r}T]f_g\qquad(g\in C_{r-1}) \] is a continuous homomorphism of conjugation weight $\lambda_2^{2r+1}$, with \[ m_{2r+1}(C_{r-1})=m_{2r+1}(J(C_{r-1})) =2^{2r+1}\mathbf Z_2. \] Its kernel is $C_r$. In particular each inclusion $C_r\subset C_{r-1}$ is proper, all these subgroups are closed and normal in $G$, and \[ G=C_rH\quad(r\ge0),\qquad G=C_\infty H. \] Moreover \[ C_\infty=\{g\in D:B_g(X,Y)=1\},\qquad B\simeq C_\infty/ \overline{[G,C_\infty](C_\infty\cap H)}. \] Here $B_g$ is its dyadic power-series component; no assertion about other components of the adelic beta function is made.

label: prop:uniform-odd-character-kernels
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For $s\ge0$, the kernel of restriction \[ H^1(C_s,\mathbf F_2)^G\longrightarrow H^1(C_\infty,\mathbf F_2)^G \] is the one-dimensional space generated by \[ \zeta_s(g)=m_{2s+3}(g)/2^{2s+3}\pmod2. \] For the original normalized group $N$, the kernel of restriction to $C_\infty$ is \[ \left(\bigoplus_{q\text{ odd prime}}\mathbf F_2\psi_q\right) \oplus\mathbf F_2\eta_3. \] Each of these kernels has injective restriction to the corresponding arithmetic subgroup.

label: thm:weight-eight-exact-image
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Every word belonging to $D_7$ starts in degree eight. Its homogeneous part of degree eight lies in a primitive rank-one integral Lie module, and \[ m_8(D_7)=m_8(J_7)=\mathbf Z_2. \] Set $D_8=D_7\cap\ker m_8$ and $J_8=D_8\cap H$. Then $D_8$ is a proper closed normal subgroup of $G$, \[ D_7=D_8J_7,\qquad G=D_8H,\qquad B\simeq D_8/\overline{[G,D_8]J_8}. \] Every word belonging to $D_8$ starts in degree at least nine. The continuous character $\eta_8=m_8\bmod2$ is $G$-invariant on $D_7$ and has nonzero arithmetic restriction. It has no $G$-invariant extension to $D$ or to $N=\ker(\lambda,\rho_2)$.

label: lem:weight-eight-leading-line
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Suppose $f\in\gamma_8$ satisfies the two-cycle and three-cycle relations \[ f(y,x)f(x,y)=1,\qquad f(z,x)f(y,z)f(x,y)=1,\qquad z=(xy)^{-1}. \] Then its homogeneous part of degree eight is \[ \operatorname{in}_8(f)=b\mathcal L_8\quad\text{for a unique }b\in\mathbf Z_2. \] If $h_w$ denotes a degree-eight Lyndon coordinate, then $b=-h_{SSSTSSTT}$ and $m_8(f)=7b$.

label: lem:weight-eight-arithmetic-commutator
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: One has $\overline{[M,M]}\subseteq D_7$. There are $\sigma\in H\cap M$ and $h\in H$ such that, with $s=h\sigma h^{-1}$, \[ w_8=[\sigma,s]\in J_7, \qquad m_8(w_8)=63\,m_3(\sigma)\,\tau_5(\sigma) \in\mathbf Z_2^\times. \] Moreover $w_8=[\sigma,k]$ for some $k\in D\cap H$.

label: cor:weight-eight-original-character-kernel
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $E$ be any closed $G$-stable subgroup containing $D$ and contained in $M$, and let $A$ be a finite abelian group with trivial $G$-action. Then \[ \{\chi\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cts}}(E,A)^G: \chi(D_8)=0\} = \{\chi\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cts}}(E,A)^G: \chi(D_7)=0\}. \] In particular, \[ \ker\!\left(H^1(N,\mathbf F_2)^G \longrightarrow H^1(D_8,\mathbf F_2)\right) =\left(\bigoplus_{q\text{ odd prime}}\mathbf F_2\psi_q\right) \oplus\mathbf F_2\eta_3. \]

label: lem:full-gt-leading-term
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: If $g$ is a full-GT element in $F^n$, with $n\ge3$, then \[ \operatorname{in}_n(g)\in \mathfrak{grt}_1(\mathbf Q_2)_n \cap\mathbf Z_2\langle S,T\rangle_n. \] Furthermore \[ \mathfrak{grt}_1(\mathbf Q_2)_n =\mathfrak{grt}_1(\mathbf Q)_n\otimes_{\mathbf Q}\mathbf Q_2. \]

label: prop:eleven-complete-leading-line
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $L_8$ and $P_3$ have the normalizations in Theorem~\ref{thm:eleven-mixed-mixed-reduction}, and put \[ V_{11}=\frac1{11}\{P_3,L_8\}. \] Then $V_{11}$ is an integral $2$-adic Lie polynomial with $[S^6TST^3]V_{11}=1$, and \[ \operatorname{in}_{11}(g)=b_{11}(g)V_{11}\quad(g\in E). \] In particular \[ \operatorname{in}_{11}(E) =\operatorname{in}_{11}(E\cap H)=\mathbf Z_2V_{11}, \qquad E'=E\cap F^{12}=C_\infty\cap F^{12}. \] Thus every dyadic word belonging to $E'$ starts in degree twelve. All arithmetic factorizations, relative quotient identifications, and character-kernel conclusions of the strict reduction remain valid for this deeper subgroup.

label: thm:eleven-mixed-mixed-reduction
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The coordinate \[ b_{11}(g)=[S^6TST^3]f_g\qquad(g\in E) \] is a continuous additive homomorphism satisfying \[ b_{11}(aga^{-1})=\lambda_2(a)^{11}b_{11}(g) \quad(a\in G,\ g\in E). \] Its full and arithmetic images are both saturated: \[ b_{11}(E)=b_{11}(J(E))=\mathbf Z_2. \] Consequently \[ E'=\ker(b_{11}|_E) \] is a proper closed normal subgroup of $G$, and \[ E/E'\simeq\mathbf Z_2,\qquad G=E'H, \qquad B\simeq E'/\overline{[G,E'](E'\cap H)}. \] For $X_2=H^1(N,\mathbf F_2)^G$, its restriction kernel remains \[ \ker\bigl(X_2\longrightarrow H^1(E',\mathbf F_2)\bigr) =\left(\bigoplus_{q\text{ odd prime}}\mathbf F_2\psi_q\right) \oplus\mathbf F_2\eta_3. \] The invariant character $b_{11}\bmod2$ on $E$ is nonzero on $J(E)$ and has no $G$-invariant extension to $N$.

label: thm:weight-five-exact-image
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The exact integral images are \[ m_5(D_3)=m_5(J_3)=32\mathbf Z_2. \] In particular, \[ \eta_5:D_3\longrightarrow\mathbf F_2, \qquad \eta_5(g)=m_5(g)/32\pmod2, \] is a continuous $G$-invariant character with nonzero arithmetic restriction.
