The kernel of $m_5$, \[ D_5=D_3\cap\ker m_5, \qquad J_5=D_5\cap H=J_3\cap\ker m_5, \] is a proper closed normal subgroup satisfying \[ D_3=D_5J_3,\qquad G=D_5H. \] The relative abelian quotient refines canonically to \[ B\simeq D_3/\overline{[G,D_3]J_3} \simeq D_5/\overline{[G,D_5]J_5}. \]

label: prop:weight-five-upper-bound
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For $g\in D_3$, one has $m_5(g)\in32\mathbf Z_2$.

label: lem:tau-five
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The map $\tau_5$ is a continuous homomorphism on $\ker\lambda$, and \[ \tau_5(hzh^{-1})=\lambda_2(h)^5\tau_5(z) \qquad(h\in G,\ z\in\ker\lambda). \] On $D_3$, it is equal to $12m_5$.

label: prop:weight-five-arithmetic-generator
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There exists $w\in J_3$ with $m_5(w)\in32\mathbf Z_2^\times$.

label: cor:weight-five-nonextension
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The character $\eta_5$ does not extend to a $G$-invariant continuous $\mathbf F_2$-character of $D=N_{\mathrm{rad}}$, and hence does not extend to one of $N$. Nevertheless $D_5$ is a strictly smaller normalization with the same relative abelian quotient. The kernel of restriction from $X_2$ to $H^1(D_5,\mathbf F_2)$ is exactly \[ \bigoplus_{q\text{ odd prime}}\mathbf F_2\psi_q \oplus\mathbf F_2\eta_3. \] The kernel of restriction from $H^1(D,\mathbf F_2)^G$ to $H^1(D_5,\mathbf F_2)$ is exactly $\mathbf F_2\eta_3|_D$. For every odd prime $p$, restriction from $H^1(N,\mathbf F_p)^G$ to $H^1(D_5,\mathbf F_p)$ is injective.

label: thm:fr-fourteen-normalization
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: On $E_{14}$ the coordinate map \[ b_{14}(g)=\bigl( [S^8TST^4]f_g,\ [S^7TST^5]f_g,\ [S^6TST^2ST^3]f_g \bigr) \] is continuous and additive with scalar conjugation weight $\lambda_2^{14}$, and \[ b_{14}(E_{14})=b_{14}(E_{14}\cap H)=\mathbf Z_2^3. \] Its kernel is $E_{15}=C_\infty\cap F^{15}$. Consequently \[ E_{14}/E_{15}\simeq\mathbf Z_2^3,\qquad G=E_{15}H,\qquad B\simeq E_{15}/\overline{[G,E_{15}](E_{15}\cap H)}. \] The original $X_2=H^1(N,\mathbf F_2)^G$ restriction kernel to $E_{15}$ remains the odd-prime rational Kummer span plus $\mathbf F_2\eta_3$. No nonzero linear combination of the three coordinates modulo two on $E_{14}$ extends invariantly to $N$.

label: prop:weight-nine-arithmetic-value
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There is $w_9\in J_8$ such that \[ m_9(w_9)=512\cdot12746612385\,\tau_9(\sigma), \qquad \tau_9(\sigma)\in\mathbf Z_2^\times, \] where $\sigma$ is the arithmetic element used in the preceding normalizations. Thus $512\mathbf Z_2\subseteq m_9(J_8)$.

label: thm:weight-nine-exact-image
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: One has \[ m_9(D_8)=m_9(J_8)=512\mathbf Z_2. \] The same equality holds with $D_8,J_8$ replaced by $D_7,J_7$. For $D_9=D_8\cap\ker m_9$ and $J_9=D_9\cap H$, \[ D_8=D_9J_8,\qquad G=D_9H,\qquad B\simeq D_9/\overline{[G,D_9]J_9}. \] The subgroup $D_9$ is proper, closed and normal in $G$, and every word belonging to it starts in degree at least ten. Moreover, \[ (m_8,m_9):D_7\longrightarrow\mathbf Z_2\times512\mathbf Z_2 \] is surjective already on $J_7$ and has kernel $D_9$.

label: prop:eta-nine-nonextension
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The character \[ \eta_9:D_7\longrightarrow\mathbf F_2,\qquad \eta_9(g)=m_9(g)/512\pmod2 \] is continuous and $G$-invariant. Its restriction to $D_8$ has nonzero arithmetic restriction and has no $G$-invariant extension to $D_5$.

label: cor:weight-nine-character-kernels
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The invariant quadratic-character kernels on restriction to $D_9$ are as follows: \[ \begin{array}{c|l} \text{domain}&\text{kernel}\\ \hline D_8&\mathbf F_2\eta_9\\ D_7&\mathbf F_2\eta_8\oplus\mathbf F_2\eta_9\\ D_5&\mathbf F_2\eta_7\oplus\mathbf F_2\alpha_8\\ D_3&\mathbf F_2\eta_5\\ N&\displaystyle\left(\bigoplus_{q\text{ odd prime}}\mathbf F_2\psi_q\right) \oplus\mathbf F_2\eta_3. \end{array} \]

label: thm:weight-seven-exact-image
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: One has \[ m_7(D_5)=m_7(J_5)=128\mathbf Z_2. \] Consequently, for $D_7=D_5\cap\ker m_7$ and $J_7=D_7\cap H$, \[ D_5=D_7J_5,\qquad G=D_7H,\qquad B\simeq D_7/\overline{[G,D_7]J_7}. \] The subgroup $D_7$ is proper, closed and normal in $G$, and \[ \eta_7:D_5\longrightarrow\mathbf F_2, \qquad \eta_7(g)=m_7(g)/128\pmod2 \] is a continuous $G$-invariant character with nonzero arithmetic restriction.

label: cor:weight-seven-nonextension
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The character $\eta_7$ has no $G$-invariant continuous extension to $D_3$, $N_{\mathrm{rad}}$ or $N$. Moreover, writing $\psi_q=\rho_q^I/2\pmod2$ for the divided odd-prime Kummer characters on $N$, one still has \[ \ker\bigl[H^1(N,\mathbf F_2)^G\longrightarrow H^1(D_7,\mathbf F_2)\bigr] =\left(\bigoplus_{q\text{ odd prime}}\mathbf F_2\psi_q\right) \oplus\mathbf F_2\eta_3. \] On $D_3$, the corresponding kernel is exactly $\mathbf F_2\eta_5$.

label: thm:weight-seven-bounds
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Every word belonging to $D_5$ has zero Magnus components below degree seven. The map $m_7:D_5\to\mathbf Z_2$ is a continuous homomorphism and \[ m_7(hgh^{-1})=\lambda_2(h)^7m_7(g) \qquad(h\in G,\ g\in D_5). \] Its arithmetic and full images are exactly \begin{equation}\label{eq:weight-seven-image-interval} m_7(J_5)=m_7(D_5)=128\mathbf Z_2. \end{equation} The corresponding degree-seven Hall images both equal $8\mathbf Z_2\mathbf L$, where $\mathbf L$ is the primitive integral vector specified below.

label: lem:weight-seven-leading-spaces
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Suppose that $f\in\gamma_5$ satisfies the two-cycle and three-cycle relations with multiplier one. Put $a=[S^4T]f$. Its Hall coordinates in degrees five and six are \begin{equation}\label{eq:weight-seven-lower-vector} a\left(1,-2,\tfrac32,2,\tfrac12,-1, -2,\tfrac72,-\tfrac32,-4,-\tfrac12,\tfrac32, \tfrac72,\tfrac32,-2\right). \end{equation} In particular, $a=0$ implies that $f$ starts in degree seven. If $f$ starts in degree seven and satisfies the same two relations, its degree-seven Hall vector has the form $a\mathbf v+b\mathbf w$, where $a=[S^6T]f$, $b$ is the sixth degree-seven Hall coordinate, and \begin{align} \mathbf v={}&\left(1,-3,5,5,-2,0,-12,-5,-2,\tfrac23, -5,5,8,3,-\tfrac{11}3,4,3,-1\right), \label{eq:weight-seven-v}\\ \mathbf w={}&\left(0,0,0,0,0,1,1,0,0,\tfrac13, -1,-1,-1,0,-\tfrac13,0,0,0\right). \label{eq:weight-seven-w} \end{align} These are necessary leading-term conditions; they assert no lifting of an arbitrary truncated solution to a profinite automorphism.

label: lem:weight-seven-integral-line
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For an element of $D_5$, the parameters in \eqref{eq:weight-seven-v}--\eqref{eq:weight-seven-w} satisfy \[ 16b=19a. \] Consequently $a\in16\mathbf Z_2$, and the integral leading line is generated by the primitive vector \begin{equation}\label{eq:weight-seven-primitive-vector} \mathbf L=(16,-48,80,80,-32,19,-173,-80,-32, 17,-99,61,109,48,-65,64,48,-16). \end{equation} The leading Hall vector of an element is $(a/16)\mathbf L$. Moreover, its leading alternating Magnus coefficient is $[STSTSTS]f=-2a$.

label: lem:weight-seven-beta
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The map $\tau_7$ is a continuous homomorphism on $\ker\lambda$, with conjugation weight $\lambda_2^7$. On $D_5$ it equals $360m_7$.

label: prop:weight-seven-arithmetic-value
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There is $z_5\in J_5$ with \[ m_7(z_5)\in128\mathbf Z_2^\times. \] More explicitly, it can be chosen so that $m_7(z_5)=128\cdot199017\,\tau_7(\sigma)$ for an arithmetic $\sigma$ with $\tau_7(\sigma)$ odd.

label: thm:weight-ten-exact-image
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The full and arithmetic images are \[ m_{10}(D_9)=m_{10}(J_9)=\mathbf Z_2. \] For $D_{10}=D_9\cap\ker m_{10}$ and $J_{10}=D_{10}\cap H$, \[ D_9=D_{10}J_9,\qquad G=D_{10}H,\qquad B\simeq D_{10}/\overline{[G,D_{10}]J_{10}}. \] The subgroup $D_{10}$ is proper, closed and normal, and its words start in degree at least eleven.

label: lem:weight-ten-leading-line
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every multiplier-one GT word starting in degree ten, the homogeneous term of degree ten is $A\mathcal L_{10}$ with $A\in\mathbf Z_2$. It vanishes exactly when $m_{10}$ vanishes.

label: lem:weight-ten-arithmetic-unit
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There is an arithmetic commutator $w_{10}\in J_9$ such that \[ m_{10}(w_{10})=-141\cdot729\,m_3(\sigma)\tau_7(\sigma) \in\mathbf Z_2^\times. \] Moreover $w_{10}=[\sigma,k]$ for some $k\in D\cap H$.

label: prop:eta-ten-extension-kernels
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The invariant character $\eta_{10}=m_{10}\pmod2$ on $D_9$ extends invariantly to $D_8$ by \[ \alpha_{10}(1,f)=[S^5TST^3]f\pmod2, \] but has no invariant extension to $D$ or $N$. The original kernel is \[ \ker\!\left(H^1(N,\mathbf F_2)^G \longrightarrow H^1(D_{10},\mathbf F_2)\right) =\left(\bigoplus_{q\text{ odd prime}}\mathbf F_2\psi_q\right) \oplus\mathbf F_2\eta_3. \] The joint raw-coefficient map $(m_9,m_{10})$ on $D_8$ has image $512\mathbf Z_2\times\mathbf Z_2$ already on $J_8$, with kernel $D_{10}$. Its invariant quadratic-character kernel on restriction to $D_{10}$ is $\mathbf F_2\eta_9\oplus\mathbf F_2\alpha_{10}$.

label: thm:thirteen-normalization
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The coordinate pair \[ b_{13}(g)= \bigl([S^7TST^4]f_g,\ [S^6TST^2ST^2]f_g\bigr) \qquad(g\in E_{13}) \] is continuous and additive, with scalar conjugation weight $\lambda_2^{13}$. Its full and arithmetic images are both $\mathbf Z_2^2$, and its kernel is \[ E_{14}=C_\infty\cap F^{14}. \] In particular $E_{13}/E_{14}\simeq\mathbf Z_2^2$, $G=E_{14}H$, and \[ B\simeq E_{14}/\overline{[G,E_{14}](E_{14}\cap H)}. \] The kernel of restriction of $X_2=H^1(N,\mathbf F_2)^G$ to $E_{14}$ is still the odd-prime rational Kummer span plus $\mathbf F_2\eta_3$. No nonzero linear combination of the two coordinates modulo two on $E_{13}$ extends invariantly to $N$.

label: thm:twelve-normalization
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: On $E_{12}$ put \[ \begin{split} b_{12,1}(g)&=[S^6TST^4]f_g,\\ b_{12,2}(g)&=[S^5TST^2ST^2]f_g, \end{split} \qquad b_{12}=(b_{12,1},b_{12,2}). \] This is a continuous additive map of scalar conjugation weight $\lambda_2^{12}$, and \[ b_{12}(E_{12})=b_{12}(E_{12}\cap H)=\mathbf Z_2^2. \] Its kernel is exactly \[ E_{13}=C_\infty\cap F^{13}. \] Consequently $E_{13}$ is a proper closed normal subgroup, with \[ E_{12}/E_{13}\simeq\mathbf Z_2^2,\qquad G=E_{13}H, \qquad B\simeq E_{13}/\overline{[G,E_{13}](E_{13}\cap H)}. \] The kernel of restriction of $X_2=H^1(N,\mathbf F_2)^G$ to $E_{13}$ is again the odd-prime rational Kummer span plus $\mathbf F_2\eta_3$. No nonzero linear combination of $b_{12,1}\bmod2$ and $b_{12,2}\bmod2$ on $E_{12}$ extends to a $G$-invariant character on $N$.

label: thm:even-characters
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $p\geq5$ be prime, let $m\geq2$ be even, and put $h_m=\dim_\Q(W/[W,W])_m$. For every $k\geq1$ such that $(p-1)p^{k-1}$ divides $m$, there is a continuous surjection \[ \GTz/\overline{\langle\!\langle\GT\rangle\!\rangle} \longrightarrow(\Z/p^k\Z)^{h_m}. \] The map is already onto on the global multiplier-one subgroup of $\GTz$. In particular weight sixteen gives a quotient $(\Z/17\Z)^{38}$.

label: lem:realization
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For $p\geq5$, let $\mathcal U$ be the multiplier-one subgroup in the image of $\GTz$ on the free pro-$p$ group $P$ on $X,Y$. Let $\mathcal U_n$ consist of pairs whose normalized conjugator belongs to $\gamma_nP$. Then \[ \mathcal U_2=\mathcal U_3=\mathcal U, \qquad \mathcal U_n/\mathcal U_{n+1}\simeq W_n(\Z_p), \qquad [\mathcal U_i,\mathcal U_j]\subset\mathcal U_{i+j}. \] Every element of the local multiplier-one group has a full gentle lift of global multiplier one.

label: lem:compact-log
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $U$ be a closed subgroup of a unipotent matrix group over $\Q_p$. Set $L=\operatorname{span}_{\Q_p}\log U$. Then $L$ is a nilpotent Lie algebra and $U$ contains $\exp(J)$ for some full $\Z_p$-lattice $J\subset L$. These statements apply to every closed subgroup of $U$.

label: cor:all-orders
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Put $Q=\GTz/\overline{\langle\!\langle\GT\rangle\!\rangle}$. There is a continuous surjection \[ Q^{\mathrm{ab}}\longrightarrow \prod_{\substack{p\geq5\\p\ \mathrm{prime}}} \prod_{k,j\geq1}\Z/p^k\Z. \] For every prime $p\geq5$, the vector space $\Hom_{\cts}(Q,\F_p)$ has dimension exactly $\aleph_0$.

label: lem:frame-all-multipliers-congruence
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every $g\in\mathcal G$ and every prime $\ell$ there is a unique matrix \[ D_{g,\ell}=\begin{pmatrix}\lambda_{g,\ell}&b_{g,\ell}\\0&1\end{pmatrix} \] such that $\widetilde q_\ell\Phi_g=\operatorname{Ad}(D_{g,\ell})\widetilde q_\ell$. It depends continuously on $g$, and $D_{gh,\ell}=D_{g,\ell}D_{h,\ell}$. For $h\in N_0$, its reduction modulo twelve is the identity.

label: prop:frame-sign-conjugation
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The restrictions of $a_2,a_3$, and hence $\delta$, to $N_0$ are invariant under conjugation by $\mathcal G$.

label: thm:global-frame-character
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There is a unique continuous character \[ \Delta:\mathcal G\longrightarrow\mathbb F_2 \] which restricts to $\delta$ on $N_0$ and is zero on $G_{\mathbb Q}$. For any $g\in\mathcal G$, choose $\sigma\in G_{\mathbb Q}$ with $(\lambda,\rho_2)(\sigma)=(\lambda,\rho_2)(g)$. Then \[ \Delta(g)=\delta(g\sigma^{-1}). \] This character vanishes on the full pentagon group.

label: thm:deep-frame-witness
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There is a multiplier-one gentle element $e=(1,f)$ such that \[ f\in F''',\qquad \rho_2(e)=0. \] Its modular automorphism $\Phi$ fixes $\tau$ and induces the identity under $q$. Its unique pure torsion frames, defined by \[ \Phi(s)=\beta s\beta^{-1},\qquad \Phi(r)=ArA^{-1}, \] satisfy \[ q(\beta)=1,\qquad q(A)=\zeta. \] In particular $e$ acts identically on $F/F'''$, and every character factoring through its metabelian action vanishes on $e$.

label: cor:frame-character-nonzero
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The character $\Delta$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:global-frame-character} is nonzero on $N_0$ and is outside the span of all continuous quadratic characters factoring through the metabelian action. In particular $\Delta$ and the characters $\vartheta_p$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:quadratic-beta-family} are linearly independent.

label: thm:peripheral-lifting
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $\alpha$ be a continuous automorphism of $\overline\Lambda$. Suppose that elements $\overline c_i\in\overline\Lambda$ satisfy \[ \alpha(\pi(x_i)) =\overline c_i\pi(x_i)\overline c_i^{-1} \qquad(1\leq i\leq3). \] There are a continuous automorphism $\Phi$ of $\Lambda$ and elements $c_i\in\Lambda$ such that \[ \pi\Phi=\alpha\pi, \qquad \pi(c_i)=\overline c_i, \qquad \Phi(x_i)=c_ix_ic_i^{-1} \qquad(1\leq i\leq3). \] If one specified conjugator $\overline c_i$ is the identity, the lift can be chosen so that the corresponding $c_i$ is the identity.

label: lem:finite-peripheral-refinement
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $q:\Lambda\twoheadrightarrow E$ be a finite quotient, let $A\triangleleft E$, and write $D=E/A$ and $q_D=q\bmod A$. There are a finite central extension $\beta:D^\dagger\twoheadrightarrow D$ and an epimorphism $q^\dagger:\Lambda\twoheadrightarrow D^\dagger$ such that $\beta q^\dagger=q_D$, with the following property. Suppose $q_1^\dagger:\Lambda\twoheadrightarrow D^\dagger$ is an epimorphism and $r_i\in D^\dagger$ satisfy \[ q_1^\dagger(x_i)=r_iq^\dagger(x_i)r_i^{-1} \qquad(1\leq i\leq3). \] There is an epimorphism $q_1:\Lambda\twoheadrightarrow E$ and elements $C_i\in E$ with \[ q_1(x_i)=C_iq(x_i)C_i^{-1},\qquad C_i\bmod A=\beta(r_i),\qquad q_1\bmod A=\beta q_1^\dagger. \]

label: thm:weight16
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For $k=\Q$ and for $k=\F_{17}$, \[ \dim_k W_{16}=75,\qquad \dim_k[W,W]_{16}=37,\qquad \dim_k(W/[W,W])_{16}=38. \] The bracket space has a basis consisting of thirty-seven brackets of homogeneous elements of weights less than sixteen.

label: thm:main-character-quotients
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Put $Q=\GTz/\overline{\langle\!\langle\GT\rangle\!\rangle}$. There is a continuous surjection \[ Q^{\mathrm{ab}}\longrightarrow (\Z/2\Z)^{\mathbb N}\times \prod_{\substack{p\geq5\\p\ \mathrm{prime}}}\prod_{k,j\geq1}\Z/p^k\Z, \] already onto on the global multiplier-one subgroup. For $p=2$ and for every prime $p\geq5$, the vector space $\Hom_{\cts}(Q,\F_p)$ has dimension $\aleph_0$.

label: thm:frame-overview
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There is a continuous character $\Delta:\GTz\to\F_2$ vanishing on $\GT$ and an element $e=(1,f)\in\GTz$ such that \[ \rho_2(e)=0,\qquad f\in\widehat F_2''',\qquad \Delta(e)=1. \] Consequently $\Delta$ is outside the span of the quadratic characters that factor through the metabelian action, including the beta characters constructed in this paper.

label: thm:main-pentagon17
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Over $\F_{17}$ the map $P_{16}$ has rank seventy and a five-dimensional kernel contained in $[W,W]_{16}$. Its restriction to that bracket space has rank thirty-two. Consequently \[ W_{16}/[W,W]_{16}\longrightarrow \mathfrak t_{4,16}/P_{16}([W,W]_{16}) \] is injective, of rank thirty-eight. Its dual injects linearly into the continuous $\F_{17}$-valued characters of the full gentle group which vanish on $\GT$, already after restriction to global multiplier one. Every nonzero functional gives a character of order seventeen.

label: prop:dual
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Put $B_n=[W,W]_n$ and $K_n=\ker P_n$. The linear functionals on $W_n$ that annihilate both brackets and linear pentagon solutions are \[ C_n=\Ann(B_n)\cap\im(P_n^*) =\bigl(W_n/(B_n+K_n)\bigr)^*. \] In particular $P_n$ is a map on $W_n/B_n$ only when $P_n(B_n)=0$.

label: prop:weight12
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: The space $W_{12}$ has dimension seven and its bracket subspace has dimension six. For the integral basis specified in Section~\ref{sec:cert}, the primitive functional \[ \ell=(-4,1,8,-4,-17,14,84) \] annihilates both $[W,W]_{12}$ and $\ker P_{12}$ over $\Q$. It has the same properties after reduction modulo thirteen and is nonzero there. Consequently $C_{12}$ is one-dimensional over $\Q$ and $\F_{13}$.

label: thm:main-topweight
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every prime $p\geq5$, set $m=p-1$ and form $W_m$, $B_m=[W,W]_m$ and $K_m=\ker P_m$ over $\F_p$. After a choice of tame splitting there is an injective linear map \[ (W_m/(B_m+K_m))^* \longrightarrow \Hom_{\cts}(Q,\F_p). \] The character associated with $\ell$ restricts to $\ell$ on the leading weight-$m$ subgroup, using its identification with $W_m$. These characters are independent already on the global multiplier-one subgroup. In particular there is a nonzero character of order thirteen from weight twelve, and thirty-eight independent characters of order seventeen from weight sixteen.

label: thm:main-peripheral-lifting
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $\alpha$ be a continuous automorphism of $\overline\Lambda$ and let $\overline c_i\in\overline\Lambda$ satisfy \[ \alpha(\pi(x_i))=\overline c_i\pi(x_i)\overline c_i^{-1} \qquad(1\leq i\leq3). \] There are a continuous automorphism $\Phi$ of $\Lambda$ and $c_i\in\Lambda$ such that \[ \pi\Phi=\alpha\pi,\qquad \pi(c_i)=\overline c_i,\qquad \Phi(x_i)=c_ix_ic_i^{-1}\quad(1\leq i\leq3). \] If one specified $\overline c_i$ is the identity, the lift can be chosen with that $c_i$ equal to the identity.

label: thm:peripheral-finite-obstruction
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There exist a finite group $G=\langle g_1,g_2\rangle$, a normal subgroup $N\trianglelefteq G$, and elements $a_1,a_2,a_3\in G$ with the following properties. Put $g_3=(g_1g_2)^{-1}$, $D=\gamma_{\infty}(N)$, and $h_i=a_ig_ia_i^{-1}$. Then \[ |G|=1440,\qquad |N|=480,\qquad |D|=120,\qquad G/D\cong A_4, \] and \[ h_iD=g_iD\quad(1\leq i\leq3),\qquad G=\langle h_1,h_2\rangle,\qquad 1\notin h_1^D h_2^D h_3^D. \] One may take $a_2=a_3=1$. In particular, the finite quotient datum is an identity automorphism with specified peripheral conjugators, but those conjugator cosets cannot be corrected by $D$.

label: lem:peripheral-central-sign
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: In $S=\operatorname{SL}_2(\F_5)$, put \[ A=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\4&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad B=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\4&3\end{pmatrix},\qquad C=\begin{pmatrix}2&2\\1&4\end{pmatrix}. \] Then $S=\langle A,B\rangle$, $ABC=I$, and \[ I\in A^S B^S C^S,\qquad -I\notin A^S B^S C^S. \]

label: prop:peripheral-full-quotient-excludes
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $\Lambda=\widehat F_2=\langle x_1,x_2\rangle$, put $x_3=(x_1x_2)^{-1}$, and let $q:\Lambda\twoheadrightarrow G$ send $x_1,x_2$ to $g_1,g_2$. Set $U=q^{-1}(N)$, $R=\gamma_{\infty}(U)$, and $\bar\Lambda=\Lambda/R$, and write $\bar x_i$ for the image of $x_i$. There is no homomorphism $\alpha:\bar\Lambda\to\bar\Lambda$ and conjugators $\bar c_i$ such that \[ \alpha(\bar x_i)=\bar c_i\bar x_i\bar c_i^{-1} \] and the images of the $\bar c_i$ in $G/D$ are $a_1D,1,1$.

label: lem:cover-sign-homology
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $\mathcal P$ be a finite set of primes congruent to five modulo twelve, and let \[ Q=\Gamma\Big/ \bigcap_{p\in\mathcal P}\overline{U_6'U_6^p}. \] Then $Q$ fits into a split exact sequence \[ 1\longrightarrow\prod_{p\in\mathcal P}M_p \longrightarrow Q\longrightarrow\Gamma_6\longrightarrow1, \] and $Q^{\mathrm{ab}}=C_6$. Choose a complement to its kernel. For $p\in\mathcal P$, let $\alpha_p$ act as $-1$ on $V_p$, and as the identity on $W_p$, on all $M_q$ with $q\ne p$, and on this complement. Then $\alpha_p$ is an involutive automorphism of $Q$. It acts trivially on $H_2(Q,\mathbb Z)$.

label: lem:sign-central-extensions
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $Q$ and $\alpha_p$ be as in Lemma~\ref{lem:cover-sign-homology}, and let $q:\Gamma\to Q$ be the natural quotient. Every finite central extension \[ 1\longrightarrow Z\longrightarrow D\longrightarrow Q \longrightarrow1 \] admits an involutive automorphism $\widetilde\alpha_p$ which lifts $\alpha_p$ and fixes $Z$ pointwise. For each $t\in\{s,r,\tau\}$, choose $b_t\in V_p$ such that \[ \alpha_p(q(t))=b_tq(t)b_t^{-1}. \] Such an element exists. For every lift $\widetilde t\in D$ of $q(t)$, there is a lift $\widetilde b_t\in D$ of $b_t$ with \[ \widetilde\alpha_p(\widetilde t) =\widetilde b_t\widetilde t\widetilde b_t^{-1}. \] The same assertions hold with $\tau^{-1}$ as the third peripheral.

label: thm:quadratic-sign-lifts
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every finite set $\mathcal P$ of primes congruent to five modulo twelve and each $p\in\mathcal P$, there is a full multiplier-one gentle element whose action on the sixth-root homology characters modulo each $q\in\mathcal P$ is $-1$ on $(\omega,\omega),(\omega^2,\omega^2)$ when $q=p$, and is the identity on all other nontrivial characters. One may at the same time prescribe identity conjugator values in any fixed finite quotient of $\Gamma$ of order divisible only by two and three.

label: lem:cover-unitarity
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement:
Let $\phi$ be a continuous automorphism of $F$ inducing the identity on $F^{\mathrm{ab}}$ and preserving the three positive peripheral classes. On a nontrivial sixth-root character $(a,b)$ with \[ a
e1,\qquad b
e1,\qquad ab
e1, \] let $B_\phi(a,b)$ be the scalar by which it acts on the corresponding one-dimensional summand of $H_1(U_6,\overline{\mathbb F}_p)$, where $p\geq5$. Then \[ B_\phi(a,b)B_\phi(a^{-1},b^{-1})=1. \]

label: thm:quadratic-beta-family
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every prime $p\equiv5\pmod{12}$ there is a continuous character \[ \vartheta_p:\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}_0\longrightarrow\mathbb F_2 \] which vanishes on $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$. Their joint map is surjective, already on the multiplier-one subgroup: \[ (\vartheta_p)_p: \widehat{\mathrm{GT}}_{0,1} \twoheadrightarrow\prod_{p\equiv5\ (12)}\mathbb F_2. \] Consequently the continuous quadratic character space of the gentle group vanishing on the pentagon group, and also the one vanishing on $G_{\mathbb Q}$, has dimension $\aleph_0$.

label: cor:simultaneous-quotient
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: There is a continuous surjection, already onto on global multiplier one, \[ \left(\GTz/\overline{\langle\!\langle\GT\rangle\!\rangle}\right)^{\mathrm{ab}} \longrightarrow (\Z/2\Z)^{\mathbb N}\times \prod_{\substack{p\geq5\\p\ \mathrm{prime}}} \prod_{k,j\geq1}\Z/p^k\Z. \] Consequently its continuous character group with values in $\Q/\Z$ contains the direct sum of the dual finite cyclic groups displayed here.

label: thm:pentagon17
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Over $\F_{17}$ the pentagon map in weight sixteen has the following ranks: \[ \operatorname{rank}P_{16}=70,\qquad \dim\ker P_{16}=5,\qquad \operatorname{rank}(P_{16}|_{[W,W]_{16}})=32. \] Its kernel is contained in $[W,W]_{16}$. Consequently the induced map \[ W_{16}/[W,W]_{16}\longrightarrow \mathfrak t_{4,16}/P_{16}([W,W]_{16}) \] is injective and has rank thirty-eight. Every functional on $(W/[W,W])_{16}$ annihilates the linear pentagon kernel.

label: thm:topweight
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: For every prime $p\geq5$, put $m=p-1$. After a choice of tame splitting, there is an injective linear map \[ \bigl(W_m(\F_p)/([W,W]_m(\F_p)+\ker P_m)\bigr)^* \longrightarrow \Hom_{\cts}\bigl(\GTz/\overline{\langle\!\langle\GT\rangle\!\rangle}, \F_p\bigr). \] The character associated with $\ell$ restricts to $\ell$ on the leading weight-$m$ subgroup. The characters are independent already on the global multiplier-one subgroup. In particular the integral certificate in weight twelve gives a nonzero character of order thirteen without using the Deligne--Drinfeld theorem; Theorem~\ref{thm:pentagon17} realizes all thirty-eight weight-sixteen functionals as characters of order seventeen.

label: cor:quadratic-kernel
status: Proved in the paper; CHECK_EVENTS records the independent and targeted check scopes
statement: Let $\delta:\GTz\to\F_2$ be a continuous character. Its kernel contains a global multiplier-one element outside $\GT$. If $\delta$ is nonzero and vanishes on $\GT$, then \[ \GT\varsubsetneqq\ker\delta\varsubsetneqq\GTz. \] This conclusion does not use the Deligne--Drinfeld theorem.

label: thm:harmonic-beta-square-lattice
status: Superseded by AQ.323; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: For \(g\in N\), the corrected harmonic frame \(W_g\), under an integral identification of its quadratic order with \(\widehat O_4\), is \(\nu_{4,g}\) or its conjugate. Consequently, on \(D=N_{\rm rad}\), the tame harmonic square test at an odd prime \(\ell\) is equivalent to \[ B_{g,\ell}(i,-1)^{(\ell-\chi_{-4}(\ell))/2}=1 \] in the residue norm-one group. Either choice of the primitive fourth root gives the same test.

label: thm:main-harmonic-beta-residue
status: Superseded by AQ.324; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: Under an integral identification with $\widehat{\Z[i]}$, the corrected harmonic frame $W_g$ equals $B_g^{\rm ad}(i,-1)$ or its complex conjugate. For each odd prime $\ell$, reduce this value modulo $\ell$ and define \[ (-1)^{\vartheta_{\ell,4}(g)} =B_{g,\ell}^{\rm ad}(i,-1)^{(\ell-\chi_{-4}(\ell))/2}. \] Then $\vartheta_{\ell,4}\in X_2$, and \[ \Xi_{\ell,4}|_N=\vartheta_{\ell,4}+\rho_\ell^I/2\pmod2 \] extends uniquely to a continuous quadratic character of $\GT$ that is zero on $H$. On $D$, its vanishing is exactly the tame harmonic square condition. No vanishing or nonvanishing of these characters on full $\GT$ is concluded.

label: thm:peripheral-finite-obstruction
status: Superseded by GC.030; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: There exist a finite group $G=\langle g_1,g_2\rangle$, a normal subgroup $N\operatorname{tr}ianglelefteq G$, and elements $a_1,a_2,a_3\in G$ with the following properties. Put $g_3=(g_1g_2)^{-1}$, $D=\gamma_{\infty}(N)$, and $h_i=a_ig_ia_i^{-1}$. Then \[ |G|=1440,\qquad |N|=480,\qquad |D|=120,\qquad G/D\cong A_4, \] and \[ h_iD=g_iD\quad(1\leq i\leq3),\qquad G=\langle h_1,h_2\rangle,\qquad 1\notin h_1^D h_2^D h_3^D. \] One may take $a_2=a_3=1$. In particular, the finite quotient datum is an identity automorphism with specified peripheral conjugators, but those conjugator cosets cannot be corrected by $D$.

label: prop:peripheral-full-quotient-excludes
status: Superseded by GC.031; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: Let $\Lambda=\widehat F_2=\langle x_1,x_2\rangle$, put $x_3=(x_1x_2)^{-1}$, and let $q:\Lambda\twoheadrightarrow G$ send $x_1,x_2$ to $g_1,g_2$. Set $U=q^{-1}(N)$, $R=\gamma_{\infty}(U)$, and $\bar\Lambda=\Lambda/R$, and write $\bar x_i$ for the image of $x_i$. There are no homomorphism $\alpha:\bar\Lambda\to\bar\Lambda$ and conjugators $\bar c_i$ such that \[ \alpha(\bar x_i)=\bar c_i\bar x_i\bar c_i^{-1} \] and the images of the $\bar c_i$ in $G/D$ are $a_1D,1,1$.

label: thm:all-cm-original-restriction
status: Superseded by AQ.294; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: The original quadratic restriction maps satisfy \[ \ker\bigl(X_2\to H^1(R_{\rm all},\mathbb F_2)^G\bigr) =\ker\bigl(X_2\to H^1(V_{\rm all},\mathbb F_2)^G\bigr) =\mathcal S. \tag{AC1}\label{eq:all-cm-original-kernel} \] There are canonical maps \[ B(V_{\rm all})_{\max2} \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }B(R_{\rm all})_{\max2} \twoheadrightarrow B_{\max2}. \tag{AC2}\label{eq:all-cm-relative-surjection} \] The last map is a surjection; an isomorphism is not asserted. Moreover, \[ R_{\rm all}/V_{\rm all} \simeq R_{\rm quad}/V_{\rm quad}, \] and this isomorphism preserves the image of the arithmetic intersections.

label: prop:163-finite-word-detector
status: Superseded by AQ.295; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: The elements \(X,Y\) generate \(\mathscr D\), so they define one finite quotient of \(\widehat F_2\), of order \(163\cdot4^{162}\). For every \(r\in R\), use the conjugator \(f_{r^n}\) of the group power \(r^n\), in the convention \[ \phi_f(x)=x,\qquad \phi_f(y)=f^{-1}yf,\qquad [x,y]=xyx^{-1}y^{-1}. \] Then \[ \prod_{j=0}^{26}f_{r^n}(X^{a_j},Y^{a_j}) =\bigl(2d^{-2}\Psi(h_{163}(r)),1\bigr) \quad\text{in }\mathscr D. \tag{F2}\label{eq:163-exact-word-value} \] In particular, \[ \prod_{j=0}^{26}f_{r^n}(X^{a_j},Y^{a_j})=1 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad h_{163}(r)\in A. \tag{F3}\label{eq:163-word-equivalence} \] The word value lies in \(2d^{-2}W\), a subgroup of order four.

label: prop:163-relative-cohomology
status: Superseded by AQ.296; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: There are natural identifications, relative to the displayed stable decomposition, \[ H^1(P,A;\mathbb F_2)=U, \] \[ H^2(P,A;\mathbb F_2) \simeq\operatorname{Quad}(E,\mathbb F_2) \oplus \operatorname{Bil}(E\times(L_{79}/2L_{79}),\mathbb F_2). \tag{R163.1}\label{eq:163-relative-forms} \] The latter space has dimension \(161\). Inversion acts trivially on it, and \[ H^2(P,A;\mathbb F_2)^{C_{162}} =\mathbb F_2\,\mathfrak q. \tag{R163.2}\label{eq:163-quaternion-line} \] Here \(\mathfrak q\) is the pullback of \(Q_8\to E\simeq\mathbb F_4\) along \(P\to E\), with its canonical splitting over \(A\). Its quadratic form is \(q(z)=z^3\). This class is fixed by every automorphism of the pair \((P,A)\).

label: lem:163-period-unit-square
status: Superseded by AQ.297; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: Let \(H_0=\langle8\rangle\subset(\mathbb Z/163)^\times\), and put \[ \theta_i=\sum_{a\in2^iH_0}\zeta_{163}^a,\qquad i=0,1,2. \] Then \[ \prod_{j=0}^{26} (\zeta_{163}^{8^j}+\zeta_{163}^{-8^j}) =-(5+\theta_1)^2. \tag{J163.2}\label{eq:163-period-square} \] The element \(5+\theta_1\) is a real unit. The two conjugate identities hold for the other two cosets.

label: thm:simultaneous-global-cm-normalization
status: Superseded by AQ.300; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: Let \(\Pi_{\rm global}\) be the set of primes \(p\geq5\) such that \(Q_p(1)\) is odd, the natural first-layer map \eqref{eq:uniform-natural-layer} is a finite isomorphism, and \(\mathscr K_p\) is injective. Define \[ R_{\rm global}=R_{\rm quad}\cap \bigcap_{p\in\Pi_{\rm global}}\ker h_p,\qquad V_{\rm global}=V_{\rm quad}\cap R_{\rm global}. \] Then the joint images of \(R_{\rm quad}\), \(V_{\rm quad}\), \(R_{\rm quad}\cap H\), and \(V_{\rm quad}\cap H\) are all \[ \mathcal P=\prod_{p\in\Pi_{\rm global}}P_p, \] including every finite sign subgroup. Consequently, \[ R_{\rm quad}/R_{\rm global}\simeq\mathcal P,\qquad V_{\rm quad}/V_{\rm global}\simeq\mathcal P,\qquad G=R_{\rm global}H, \tag{U9}\label{eq:uniform-global-factorization} \] and inclusion induces an isomorphism \[ R_{\rm global}/V_{\rm global} \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }R_{\rm quad}/V_{\rm quad} \tag{U10}\label{eq:uniform-proodd-identification} \] which preserves the image of the arithmetic intersections. In particular the quotient in \eqref{eq:uniform-proodd-identification} is pro-odd. The relative quotients satisfy \[ B(R_{\rm global})\simeq B,\qquad B(V_{\rm global})_{\max2}\simeq B_{\max2}. \tag{U11}\label{eq:uniform-relative-quotients} \] The original restrictions of \(X_2\) to both new groups have kernel exactly \(\mathcal S\), and image all continuous \(G\)-invariant quadratic characters which vanish on the corresponding arithmetic intersection. The older unit set \(\Pi\) and the primes \(29,113\) belong to \(\Pi_{\rm global}\), whereas \(163\) does not. No infinitude assertion about \(\Pi_{\rm global}\) is needed.

label: thm:uniform-arithmetic-cm-image
status: Superseded by AQ.301; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: Let \(R_\Lambda\) and \(V_\Lambda\) be obtained from \(R_{\rm quad}\) and \(V_{\rm quad}\) by imposing any collection of the scalar kernels \(h_q\) with \(q\ne p\). Under \eqref{eq:uniform-natural-layer}, their arithmetic images are \[ h_p(R_\Lambda\cap H)=h_p(V_\Lambda\cap H) =\{v\in P:\ell(v\bmod QP)=0\text{ for every } \ell\in\ker\mathscr K\}. \tag{U5}\label{eq:uniform-arithmetic-image} \] In particular, \[ [P:h_p(R_\Lambda\cap H)]=2^{\dim\ker\mathscr K},\qquad \dim_{\mathbb F_2}\bigl(h_p(R_\Lambda\cap H)/QP\bigr) =\dim\operatorname{im}\mathscr K. \] Every value in \eqref{eq:uniform-arithmetic-image} has a witness in \(V_{\rm quad}\cap H\) with all other prime scalar coordinates equal to \(1\).

label: thm:main-cyclotomic-cm-normalization
status: Superseded by AQ.292; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: With these definitions and the preceding hypotheses, the joint map \[ (\mathfrak h_p)_{p\in\Pi}:R_{\rm quad}\longrightarrow \prod_{p\in\Pi}\mathcal P_p \] is surjective already on \(V_{\rm quad}\cap H\). Put \[ \mathcal R_\Pi=R_{\rm quad}\cap\bigcap_{p\in\Pi}\ker\mathfrak h_p, \qquad \mathcal V_\Pi=V_{\rm quad}\cap\mathcal R_\Pi. \] These are closed normal subgroups, and \[ \begin{gathered} G=\mathcal R_\Pi H,\qquad R_{\rm quad}/\mathcal R_\Pi\simeq V_{\rm quad}/\mathcal V_\Pi\simeq\prod_{p\in\Pi}\mathcal P_p,\\ B\simeq\mathcal R_\Pi/ \overline{[G,\mathcal R_\Pi](\mathcal R_\Pi\cap H)},\\ B_{\max2}\simeq \left(\mathcal V_\Pi/ \overline{[G,\mathcal V_\Pi](\mathcal V_\Pi\cap H)}\right)_{\max2}. \end{gathered} \] The quotient identifications hold also on arithmetic intersections. Both original restriction kernels are exactly \(\mathcal S=s(Y_2)\), and both restricted images are every invariant quadratic character killing the arithmetic intersection, canonically \(\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cts}(B,\F_2)\). If \(r_p\) is the number of orbits of complex conjugation on the primes above two, then \[ \mathcal P_p\simeq\mathbf Z_2^{h_p}\times C_2^{r_p-1} \] noncanonically. No nonzero quadratic character of the product, pulled back to \(R_{\rm quad}\), extends to an original member of \(X_2\).

label: thm:main-genus-two-normalization
status: Preserved historical statement; consult current paper and LEDGER for replacement or scope correction
statement: With the preceding definitions and hypotheses, \[ \mathfrak h_5(R_{\rm quad})= \mathfrak h_5(R_{\rm quad}\cap H)= \mathfrak h_5(V_{\rm quad})= \mathfrak h_5(V_{\rm quad}\cap H)=P_5\simeq\mathbf Z_2^2. \] Define the closed normal subgroups \[ R_{{\rm quad},5}=R_{\rm quad}\cap\ker\mathfrak h_5, \qquad V_{{\rm quad},5}=V_{\rm quad}\cap\ker\mathfrak h_5. \] Then \[ \begin{gathered} G=R_{{\rm quad},5}H,\qquad R_{\rm quad}/R_{{\rm quad},5}\simeq V_{\rm quad}/V_{{\rm quad},5}\simeq\mathbf Z_2^2,\\ B\simeq R_{{\rm quad},5}/ \overline{[G,R_{{\rm quad},5}](R_{{\rm quad},5}\cap H)},\\ B_{\max2}\simeq \left(V_{{\rm quad},5}/ \overline{[G,V_{{\rm quad},5}](V_{{\rm quad},5}\cap H)}\right)_{\max2}. \end{gathered} \] Both quotient identifications hold also on the arithmetic intersections. Restriction of \(X_2\) to either new subgroup has exact kernel \(\mathcal S=s(Y_2)\); its image consists of every invariant quadratic character of that subgroup killing its arithmetic intersection. This image is canonically \(\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cts}(B,\F_2)\). No nonzero character of \(P_5\), pulled back to \(R_{\rm quad}\), extends to an original member of \(X_2\).

label: thm:genus-two-exact-image
status: Superseded by AQ.272; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: The four images are exactly \begin{equation}\label{eq:g2-four-images} \mathfrak h_5(R_{\rm quad})=\mathfrak h_5(R_{\rm quad}\cap H) =\mathfrak h_5(V_{\rm quad})=\mathfrak h_5(V_{\rm quad}\cap H) =P_5\simeq\mathbf Z_2^2. \end{equation} Put \[ R_{{\rm quad},5}=R_{\rm quad}\cap\ker \mathfrak h_5, \qquad V_{{\rm quad},5}=V_{\rm quad}\cap\ker \mathfrak h_5. \] These are closed normal subgroups of \(G\), and \[ G=R_{{\rm quad},5}H,\qquad R_{\rm quad}/R_{{\rm quad},5} \simeq V_{\rm quad}/V_{{\rm quad},5} \simeq\mathbf Z_2^2. \] The same quotient identifications hold on the arithmetic intersections. In particular both reductions have infinite index. They preserve the relative quotients: \[ B\simeq R_{{\rm quad},5}/ \overline{[G,R_{{\rm quad},5}](R_{{\rm quad},5}\cap H)}, \] \[ B_{\max2}\simeq \left(V_{{\rm quad},5}/ \overline{[G,V_{{\rm quad},5}](V_{{\rm quad},5}\cap H)} \right)_{\max2}. \] Restriction of the original \(X\) to either new subgroup still has exact kernel \(\mathcal S\). For either new subgroup \(L\), its image is exactly \begin{equation}\label{eq:g2-complete-restriction-image} \{\chi\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cts}(L,\mathbf F_2)^G: \chi|_{L\cap H}=0\}, \end{equation} canonically identified with \(\operatorname{Hom}_{\rm cts}(B,\mathbf F_2)\). Moreover, no nonzero character \(\varphi:P_5\to\mathbf F_2\), pulled back to \(R_{\rm quad}\) by \(\mathfrak h_5\), extends to a member of \(X\).

label: thm:main-simultaneous-quadratic
status: Superseded by AQ.254; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: The integral logarithm defines an invariant character \[ \tau=\frac{\log\mathfrak t_2}{4\delta}\pmod2\in H^1(M,\F_2)^G, \qquad \tau|_K=\kappa_{2,3}+\psi_3. \] Consequently \(\tau|_N+\psi_3\) lifts \(\kappa_{2,3}\) to \(X_2\). The joint map \[ (\mathfrak t_2,(\xi_{\ell,q})_{\mathcal I}):R_D \longrightarrow\mathcal U\times\prod_{\mathcal I}\F_2 \] is surjective already on \(R_D\cap H\), and also on \(V_D\cap H\). Define \[ R^*=R_D\cap\ker\mathfrak t_2 \cap\bigcap_{\mathcal I}\ker\xi_{\ell,q}, \qquad V^*=V_D\cap R^*. \] These subgroups are closed and normal in \(G\), and \[ \begin{gathered} R_D/R^*\simeq V_D/V^* \simeq\mathcal U\times\prod_{\mathcal I}\F_2,\qquad G=R^*H,\\ B\simeq R^*/\overline{[G,R^*](R^*\cap H)},\qquad B_{\max2}\simeq \left(V^*/\overline{[G,V^*](V^*\cap H)}\right)_{\max2}. \end{gathered} \] The two quotient descriptions also hold on arithmetic intersections. The kernel of the original \(X_2\) restriction to either \(R^*\) or \(V^*\) is exactly \[ \F_2\eta_3\oplus\bigoplus_{p\text{ odd}}\F_2\psi_p \oplus\F_2\tau\oplus\bigoplus_{\mathcal I}\F_2\xi_{\ell,q}. \] Arithmetic restriction is injective on this kernel.

label: thm:main-full-quadratic-target
status: Superseded by AQ.228; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: With \(A=G/N=H/(H\cap N)\), transgression is an isomorphism \[ \operatorname{tr}:Y_2\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \ker\bigl(H^2(A,\F_2)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Br}(\Q)[2]\bigr). \] There is a direct-sum decomposition \[ Y_2=\F_2\eta_3 \oplus\bigoplus_{p\text{ odd}}\F_2\psi_p \oplus\bigoplus_{p\text{ odd}}\F_2\kappa_{2,p} \oplus\bigoplus_{\substack{p<q\\p,q\text{ odd}}}\F_2\kappa_{p,q}, \] where \(\eta_3=m_3/8\bmod2\) is the cubic character and the additional basis characters are uniquely specified by \begin{align*} \operatorname{tr}(\kappa_{2,p}) &=\operatorname{Inf}_U^A \bigl(ac_p+\varepsilon_p(\delta_2+\delta_p)\bigr),\\ \operatorname{tr}(\kappa_{p,q}) &=\operatorname{Inf}_U^A \bigl(c_pc_q+\ell_p(q^*)\delta_p+\ell_q(p^*)\delta_q\bigr). \end{align*} All products are cup products, and every character is a finite sum. The character \(\kappa_{5,29}\) is realized by the central quadratic layer of \[ \Q\bigl(\sqrt5,\sqrt{29},\sqrt{7+2\sqrt5}\bigr) /\Q(\sqrt5,\sqrt{29}), \] restricted to \(G_{K_2}\). It is nonzero and independent of \(\eta_3\) and the \(\psi_p\).

label: thm:main-cubic-normalization
status: Preserved historical statement; consult current paper and LEDGER for replacement or scope correction
statement: For $g=(1,f)$ put $m_3(g)=[S^2T]f$ in the Magnus expansion $x=1+S$, $y=1+T$. Then \[ m_3(N)\subseteq8\Z_2,\qquad m_3(N_{\mathrm{rad}})=m_3(G_{L_{\mathrm{rad}}})=8\Z_2. \] Thus $\eta_3=m_3/8\pmod2$ belongs to $X_2$, and its restriction to $G_{L_{\mathrm{rad}}}$ is nonzero. It is linearly independent of the entire rational Kummer subspace. The joint map \[ N\longrightarrow \left(\prod_{q\text{ odd prime}}2\Zh\right)\times8\Z_2, \qquad n\longmapsto\bigl((\rho_q^I(n))_q,m_3(n)\bigr) \] is surjective already on $K$. Its kernel $N_{\mathrm{rad},3}=N_{\mathrm{rad}}\cap\ker m_3$ is a proper closed normal subgroup of $N_{\mathrm{rad}}$ and of $\GT$, and \[ \GT=N_{\mathrm{rad},3}\GQ,\qquad B\simeq N_{\mathrm{rad},3}/ \overline{[\GT,N_{\mathrm{rad},3}] (N_{\mathrm{rad},3}\cap\GQ)}. \] The kernel of restriction from $X_2$ to $H^1(N_{\mathrm{rad},3},\F_2)$ is precisely \[ \left(\bigoplus_{q\text{ odd prime}}\F_2\psi_q\right) \oplus\F_2\eta_3. \] On $N_{\mathrm{rad},3}$ put $m_5(g)=[S^4T]f$ and $K_{\mathrm{rad},3}=N_{\mathrm{rad},3}\cap\GQ$. Then \[ m_5(N_{\mathrm{rad},3})=m_5(K_{\mathrm{rad},3})=32\Z_2. \] Thus $N_{\mathrm{rad},3,5}=N_{\mathrm{rad},3}\cap\ker m_5$ is again proper and closed normal, with \[ \GT=N_{\mathrm{rad},3,5}\GQ,\qquad B\simeq N_{\mathrm{rad},3,5}/ \overline{[\GT,N_{\mathrm{rad},3,5}] (N_{\mathrm{rad},3,5}\cap\GQ)}. \] The divided character $\eta_5=m_5/32\pmod2$ on $N_{\mathrm{rad},3}$ does not extend to an invariant quadratic character of $N_{\mathrm{rad}}$ or of $N$. The kernel of restriction from $X_2$ to $H^1(N_{\mathrm{rad},3,5},\F_2)$ is still precisely the displayed rational Kummer and cubic span.

label: thm:main-weight-seven-alternative
status: Preserved historical statement; consult current paper and LEDGER for replacement or scope correction
statement: Put $D_3=N_{\mathrm{rad},3}$, $D_5=N_{\mathrm{rad},3,5}$, and $J_5=D_5\cap H$. Every $g\in D_5$ starts in Magnus degree seven, and $m_7(g)=[S^6T]f_g$ is an additive weight-seven coordinate with \[ m_7(D_5)=m_7(J_5)=128\Z_2. \] The proper closed normal subgroup $D_7=D_5\cap\ker m_7$ satisfies \[ \GT=D_7H,\qquad B\simeq D_7/\overline{[\GT,D_7](D_7\cap H)}. \] The invariant character $\eta_7=m_7/128\pmod2$ on $D_5$ has nonzero arithmetic restriction. It has no invariant extension to $N_{\mathrm{rad},3}$, $N_{\mathrm{rad}}$ or $N$. The kernel of restriction from $X_2$ to $H^1(D_7,\F_2)$ is still exactly the rational Kummer span together with $\F_2\eta_3$.

label: thm:main-weight-eight-normalization
status: Preserved historical statement; consult current paper and LEDGER for replacement or scope correction
statement: Every $g\in D_7$ has Magnus expansion starting in degree at least eight. Put \[ m_8(g)=[S^4TST^2]f_g,\qquad J_7=D_7\cap H. \] This is an additive coordinate of conjugation weight $\lambda_2^8$, and \[ m_8(D_7)=m_8(J_7)=\Z_2. \] Its kernel $D_8$ is proper, closed and normal in $\GT$, satisfies $\GT=D_8H$, and gives \[ B\simeq D_8/\overline{[\GT,D_8](D_8\cap H)}. \] Every element of $D_8$ starts in Magnus degree at least nine. The invariant quadratic character $\eta_8=m_8\pmod2$ on $D_7$ extends invariantly to $D_5$ by the same raw coefficient modulo two, but has no invariant extension to $D_3$, $N_{\mathrm{rad}}$ or $N$. More precisely, no nonzero combination of its extension and $\eta_7$ on $D_5$ extends invariantly to $D_3$, and \[ \ker\!\left(H^1(D_3,\F_2)^{\GT}\longrightarrow H^1(D_8,\F_2)\right) =\F_2\eta_5. \] The kernel of restriction from $X_2$ to $H^1(D_8,\F_2)$ remains exactly the rational Kummer span together with $\F_2\eta_3$.

label: prop:main-weight-nine-bounds
status: Preserved historical statement; consult current paper and LEDGER for replacement or scope correction
statement: Put $J_j=D_j\cap H$ for $j=7,8$, and $m_9(g)=[S^8T]f_g$ for $g\in D_7$. This is a continuous homomorphism of conjugation weight $\lambda_2^9$, and \[ m_9(D_7)=m_9(J_7)=m_9(D_8)=m_9(J_8)=512\Z_2. \] Its integral kernel $D_9=D_8\cap\ker m_9$ is proper, closed and normal in $\GT$, and \[ \GT=D_9H,\qquad B\simeq D_9/\overline{[\GT,D_9](D_9\cap H)}. \] Every $D_9$ word starts in degree at least ten. The joint map $(m_8,m_9):D_7\to\Z_2\times512\Z_2$ is surjective already on $J_7$ and has kernel $D_9$. The invariant character $\eta_9=m_9/512\pmod2$ on $D_7$ has nonzero arithmetic restriction; its restriction to $D_8$ has no invariant extension to $D_5$. The kernel of restriction from $X_2$ to $H^1(D_9,\F_2)$ remains exactly the rational Kummer span together with $\F_2\eta_3$.

label: thm:main-weight-ten-normalization
status: Preserved historical statement; consult current paper and LEDGER for replacement or scope correction
statement: On $D_9$, put $m_{10}(g)=[S^5TST^3]f_g$ and $J_9=D_9\cap H$. This is an additive coordinate of conjugation weight $\lambda_2^{10}$, with \[ m_{10}(D_9)=m_{10}(J_9)=\Z_2. \] Its kernel $D_{10}$ is proper, closed and normal, and \[ \GT=D_{10}H,\qquad B\simeq D_{10}/\overline{[\GT,D_{10}](D_{10}\cap H)}. \] Every element of $D_{10}$ starts in Magnus degree at least eleven. The invariant character $\eta_{10}=m_{10}\pmod2$ extends invariantly to $D_8$, but not to $D_7$ or any of $D_5,D_3,N_{\mathrm{rad}},N$. The kernel of restriction from $X_2$ to $H^1(D_{10},\F_2)$ is still exactly the rational Kummer span together with $\F_2\eta_3$.

label: prop:arithmetic-kummer-kernel-axes
status: Superseded by AQ.208; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: Let \(G=\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}\), let \(H\) be its arithmetic subgroup, and put \[ M=\ker\lambda,\qquad N=\ker(\lambda,\rho_2^I). \] \[ D=\bigcap_{q\ {\rm prime}}\ker(\rho_q^I|_M), \] \[ R_M=\{g\in M:f_g=1\text{ in the free pro-two group}\}. \] For every odd rational prime \(q\), there is an element \(k_q\in R_M\cap N\cap H\) whose only nonzero rational Kummer coordinate is \[ \rho_{q,2}^I(k_q)=-2. \] In particular the tuple of dyadic odd-prime coordinates on the closed arithmetic subgroup of \(R_M\cap N\) killing every odd-primary Kummer coordinate has image exactly \[ \prod_{q\ {\rm odd}}2\mathbf Z_2. \label{eq:arithmetic-kernel-axes-1} \] If \(G=DH\), and \(R_D=R_M\cap D\), the natural map \[ (R_M\cap N)/R_D\longrightarrow N/D \] is an isomorphism. If, in addition, \(M=R_M(M\cap H)\), then \[ D=R_D(D\cap H),\qquad G=R_DH. \]

label: thm:main-all-degree-dyadic
status: Superseded by AQ.200; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: For every $n\ge3$, the full and arithmetic leading images are \[ \operatorname{in}_n(F^nM) =\operatorname{in}_n(F^nM\cap H) =\mathfrak{grt}_1(\Q_2)_n \cap\operatorname{Lie}_{\Z_2}(S,T)_n. \] Arithmetic odd-degree elements freely generate this integral Lie algebra, and their reductions are Willwacher's characteristic-two generators. The full group $\GT$ and $H$ have the same image in $\operatorname{Aut}(\widehat F_2^{(2)})$. The subgroup $R_D$ is closed and normal, and \[ \GT=R_DH,\qquad B\simeq R_D/\overline{[\GT,R_D](R_D\cap H)}. \] Put $m_3(g)=[S^2T]f_g$ and $\eta_3=m_3/8\pmod2$ on $N$. Then $\eta_3\in X_2$, and \[ \ker\bigl(X_2\longrightarrow H^1(R_D,\F_2)\bigr) =\left(\bigoplus_{q\text{ odd prime}}\F_2\psi_q\right) \oplus\F_2\eta_3. \] Arithmetic restriction is injective on this kernel.

label: prop:arithmetic-kummer-kernel-axes
status: Superseded by AQ.190; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: Let \(G=\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}\), let \(H\) be its arithmetic subgroup, and put \[ M=\ker\lambda,\qquad N=\ker(\lambda,\rho_2^I),\qquad D=\bigcap_{q\ {\rm prime}}\ker(\rho_q^I|_M),\qquad R_M=\{g\in M:f_g=1\text{ in the free pro-two group}\}. \] For every odd rational prime \(q\), there is an element \(k_q\in R_M\cap N\cap H\) whose only nonzero rational Kummer coordinate is \[ \rho_{q,2}^I(k_q)=-2. \] In particular the tuple of dyadic odd-prime coordinates on the closed arithmetic subgroup of \(R_M\cap N\) killing every odd-primary Kummer coordinate has image exactly \[ \prod_{q\ {\rm odd}}2\mathbf Z_2. \label{eq:arithmetic-kernel-axes-1} \] If \(G=DH\), and \(R_D=R_M\cap D\), the natural map \[ (R_M\cap N)/R_D\longrightarrow N/D \] is an isomorphism. If, in addition, \(M=R_M(M\cap H)\), then \[ D=R_D(D\cap H),\qquad G=R_DH. \]

label: lem:level3-cubic-frame-principal
status: Superseded by AQ.179; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: For the same normalized element \(g\), let \(A_g\) be the normalized pure cubic conjugator, so that \[ \Phi_g(uv)=A_g(uv)A_g^{-1},\qquad A_g\in\widehat F(u^2,v^2)'. \] Then \(A_g\in\overline{\Gamma(3)}\). If also \(\rho_3^I(g)=0\), the normalized cubic identity gives \[ f_g(u^2,uv)\in\overline{\Gamma(3)}. \]

label: thm:main-uniform-dyadic-normalization
status: Superseded by AQ.181; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: Put $C_0=D=N_{\mathrm{rad}}$ and \[ C_r=D\cap\bigcap_{j=1}^r\ker c_{2j+1},\qquad C_\infty=\bigcap_{r\ge0}C_r. \] For every $r\ge1$, the coefficient $m_{2r+1}=[S^{2r}T]f$ is additive on $C_{r-1}$, has conjugation weight $\lambda_2^{2r+1}$, and satisfies \[ m_{2r+1}(C_{r-1})=m_{2r+1}(C_{r-1}\cap H) =2^{2r+1}\Z_2,\qquad \ker(m_{2r+1}|_{C_{r-1}})=C_r. \] All these subgroups are closed and normal, and \[ G=C_rH=C_\infty H,\qquad B\simeq C_\infty/ \overline{[G,C_\infty](C_\infty\cap H)}. \] The subgroup $C_\infty$ is exactly the kernel in $D$ of the dyadic beta multiplier. The kernel of restriction from $X_2$ to $H^1(C_\infty,\F_2)$ is the rational Kummer span together with $\F_2\eta_3$. Finally, $E=C_\infty\cap D_{10}$ has infinite index in $D_{10}$, and \[ G=EH,\qquad B\simeq E/\overline{[G,E](E\cap H)}. \] Its elements have no pro-$2$ Magnus term below degree eleven and have trivial dyadic beta multiplier. The kernel of restriction from $X_2$ to $H^1(E,\F_2)$ is again exactly the rational Kummer span together with $\F_2\eta_3$. The mixed coordinate $b_{11}=[S^6TST^3]f$ on $E$ is additive, has conjugation weight $\lambda_2^{11}$, and has full and arithmetic image $\Z_2$. Its kernel $E'$ is a proper closed normal subgroup whose words start in degree at least twelve, $G=E'H$, and \[ B\simeq E'/\overline{[G,E'](E'\cap H)}. \] The kernel of restriction from $X_2$ to $H^1(E',\F_2)$ is the same rational Kummer span together with $\F_2\eta_3$. More precisely, if $F^n$ denotes the subgroup whose pro-$2$ Magnus words start in degree $n$, then $E'=C_\infty\cap F^{12}$. More generally put $E_n=C_\infty\cap F^n$ for $n=12,13,14$. The two following leading layers have exact arithmetic images: \[ E_{12}/E_{13}\simeq\Z_2^2,\qquad E_{13}/E_{14}\simeq\Z_2^2. \] For each $n=12,13,14$, one has \[ G=E_nH,\qquad B\simeq E_n/\overline{[G,E_n](E_n\cap H)}. \] The kernel of restriction from $X_2$ to $E_n$ is still the rational Kummer span together with $\F_2\eta_3$.

label: lem:level3-principal-image
status: Superseded by AQ.169; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: Let \(P=\Gamma(3)\), the kernel of \(B\to\operatorname{PSL}_2(\mathbf F_3)\). Then \[ d_3(P)=\Gamma^0(9),\qquad \vartheta_3(P)=\Gamma_0(9). \] In particular \(\vartheta_3\) does not preserve \(P\). The intersection \(P\cap\Gamma_0(9)\) has index \(36\) in \(\mathcal M\); its modular curve has genus one and six cusps, of widths \(3,3,3,9,9,9\).

label: lem:weight-five-coefficients
status: Preserved historical statement; consult current paper and LEDGER for replacement or scope correction
statement: Suppose $f\in\gamma_5$ satisfies \[ f(y,x)f(x,y)=1,\qquad f(z,x)f(y,z)f(x,y)=1,\qquad z=(xy)^{-1}. \] Put \[ a=[S^4T]f,\quad c_5=[STSTS]f,\quad c_7=[STSTSTS]f,\quad c_9=[STSTSTSTS]f. \] Then \begin{equation}\label{eq:weight-five-three-coefficients} c_5=-2a,\qquad c_7\equiv5a\pmod{16},\qquad c_9\equiv2a\pmod4. \end{equation}

label: lem:weight-seven-matrix-filtration
status: Preserved historical statement; consult current paper and LEDGER for replacement or scope correction
statement: Let $Q$ be the closed subgroup of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbf Z_2)$ generated by $U^2,V^2$, where \[ U=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad V=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\-1&1\end{pmatrix}. \] Let $\mathcal B_r$ be the principal congruence group modulo $2^r$, and let $\mathcal A_r$ consist of determinant-one matrices whose diagonal entries are $1$ modulo $2^r$ and whose off-diagonal entries are zero modulo $2^{r+1}$. Then \[ \gamma_{2k}(Q)\subseteq\mathcal A_{3k-1},\qquad \gamma_{2k+1}(Q)\subseteq\mathcal B_{3k+1}\quad(k\ge1). \] In particular, $\gamma_7(Q)\subseteq\mathcal B_{10}$, $\gamma_9(Q)\subseteq\mathcal B_{13}$ and $\gamma_{10}(Q)\subseteq\mathcal A_{14}$.

label: prop:kn-linear-sign-model
status: Superseded by AQ.156; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: There is an $\mathbb F_{17}$-linear automorphism of the space (H) that commutes with the whole deck group $A$, preserves its alternating intersection form, and has determinant $-1$ on the ten-dimensional $\omega$-eigenspace over $\mathbb F_{17^2}$. Its quadratic norm-one determinant sign is therefore $-1$. This is a linear model, not a GT element or a solution of the pentagon or of (K).

label: prop:tame-harmonic-word-gate
status: Superseded by AQ.158; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: For every $g\in D$ the corrected harmonic frame satisfies \[ W_g=f_g(U^2,S)\qquad\text{in }\mathrm{SL}_2(\widehat{\mathbb Z}). \tag{1} \] Consequently its residue belongs to the cyclic group \[ \mathcal T_\ell =\{aI+bS_\ell:a,b\in\mathbb F_\ell,\ a^2+b^2=1\}, \qquad |\mathcal T_\ell|=\ell-\chi_{-4}(\ell). \] The simultaneous compatibility of the radical and CM actions on every rational quartic root is equivalent to the following family of finite word identities: \[ \boxed{\quad f_g(U_\ell^2,S_\ell)^{m_\ell}=I \qquad(g\in D,\ \ell\ge5\text{ prime}).\quad} \tag{2} \] For a fixed $g$, the same equivalence holds pointwise. This is a reformulation of the remaining tame quartic gate; it does not assert the identities in (2).

label: prop:two-relative-extensions
status: Superseded by AQ.146; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: Each of $\epsilon_h,\epsilon_c$ has a unique extension to a continuous homomorphism $G\to\mathbb F_2$ that is zero on $H$. Their sum is the established residual relative character $\chi_3$. The harmonic extension is proved to vanish in Section~\ref{sec:harmonic-dyadic-comparison}; the cubic extension then equals $\chi_3$, whose vanishing remains open.

label: cor:harmonic-defect-zero
status: Superseded by AQ.147; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: On $D=\ker\lambda\cap\bigcap_q\ker\rho_q^I$, the finite harmonic frame sign satisfies $w=\eta$. Thus the previously constructed relative character $\epsilon_h=w+\eta$ is zero on the whole of full GT, and the remaining exceptional character is $\chi_3=\epsilon_c=\tau+\eta$. No vanishing of $\epsilon_c$ is asserted.

label: thm:main-harmonic-dyadic
status: Superseded by AQ.151; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: For every $g=(1,f_g)\in\GT$ with $\rho_2(g)=0$, the pure harmonic frame satisfies \[ \beta_g(u^2,v^2)^{-1}=f_g(u^2,uvu) \quad\text{in }\widehat B_3. \] Consequently $w_3=\eta$ on $D$, the relative character $\epsilon_h$ is zero, and $\chi_3=\epsilon_c=\tau_3+\eta$. The vanishing of this remaining cubic comparison character is not determined.

label: thm:main-weight-ten-normalization
status: Superseded by AQ.142; original statement and proof locator preserved

label: prop:main-weight-nine-bounds
status: Superseded by AQ.130; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: Put $J_8=D_8\cap H$ and $m_9(g)=[S^8T]f_g$ for $g\in D_8$. This is a continuous homomorphism of conjugation weight $\lambda_2^9$, and \[ 512\Z_2\subseteq m_9(J_8)\subseteq m_9(D_8)\subseteq256\Z_2. \] Write $m_9(D_8)=2^e\Z_2$ and $m_9(J_8)=2^f\Z_2$; then $8\le e\le f\le9$. label: cor:cubic-radical-joint-image
status: Superseded by AQ.127; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: The map \[ N\longrightarrow \left(\prod_{q\text{ odd prime}}2\widehat{\mathbf Z}\right) \times8\mathbf Z_2, \qquad n\longmapsto((\rho_q^I(n))_q,m_3(n)) \] is surjective on $K=N\cap H$, with kernel $D_3$. Consequently the $G$-invariant continuous $\mathbf F_2$-characters of $N$ which vanish on $D_3$ form exactly \[ \left(\bigoplus_{q\text{ odd prime}}\mathbf F_2\psi_q\right) \oplus\mathbf F_2\eta_3. \] For an odd prime $p$, no nonzero $G$-invariant $\mathbf F_p$-character of $N$ vanishes on $D_3$.

label: thm:abelian-splitting
status: Superseded by AQ.117; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: There is a canonical isomorphism of profinite abelian groups \[ G^{\mathrm{ab}}\simeq U\times B \] under which the multiplier is the first projection. Moreover \[ D=N\cap\overline{[G,G]},\qquad B\simeq\bigl(G/\overline{\langle\!\langle H\rangle\!\rangle}\bigr)^{\mathrm{ab}}. \] For every prime $p$, put \[ X_p=H^1(N,\mathbb F_p)^G, \qquad r_p:X_p\longrightarrow H^1(K,\mathbb F_p). \] Restriction gives canonical identifications \begin{align*} \ker r_p&\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cts}}(B,\mathbb F_p),\\ H^1(G,\mathbb F_p)&\simeq \lambda^*H^1(U,\mathbb F_p)\oplus\ker r_p. \end{align*} Consequently $\ker r_p=0$ if and only if every continuous $\mathbb F_p$-character of $G$ factors through the multiplier. The multiplier identifies $G^{\mathrm{ab}}$ with $U$ if and only if $N\subset\overline{[G,G]}$, and this holds if and only if $\ker r_p=0$ for every prime~$p$.

label: thm:main-weight-seven-alternative
status: Superseded by AQ.089; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: Put $D_5=N_{\mathrm{rad},3,5}$ and $J_5=D_5\cap H$. Every $g\in D_5$ starts in Magnus degree seven, and $m_7(g)=[S^6T]f_g$ is an additive weight-seven coordinate. label: thm:weight-seven-bounds
status: Superseded by AQ.093; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: Every word belonging to $D_5$ has zero Magnus components below degree seven. The map $m_7:D_5\to\mathbf Z_2$ is a continuous homomorphism and \[ m_7(hgh^{-1})=\lambda_2(h)^7m_7(g) \qquad(h\in G,\ g\in D_5). \] Its arithmetic and full images satisfy \begin{equation}\label{eq:weight-seven-image-interval} 128\mathbf Z_2\subseteq m_7(J_5) \subseteq m_7(D_5)\subseteq64\mathbf Z_2. \end{equation} The leading degree-seven images are nonzero closed rank-one $\mathbf Z_2$-modules on the explicit primitive line described below. statement: Let $e,f$ be the exponents in Theorem~\ref{thm:weight-seven-bounds}, and put $D_7=D_5\cap\ker m_7$ and $J_7=D_7\cap H$. The subgroup $D_7$ is proper, closed and normal in $G$. label: thm:main-cubic-normalization
status: Superseded by AQ.069; original statement and proof locator preserved
statement: For $g=(1,f)$ put $m_3(g)=[S^2T]f$ in the Magnus expansion $x=1+S$, $y=1+T$. Then \[ m_3(N)\subseteq8\Z_2,\qquad m_3(N_{\mathrm{rad}})=m_3(G_{L_{\mathrm{rad}}})=8\Z_2. \] Thus $\eta_3=m_3/8\pmod2$ belongs to $X_2$, and its restriction to $G_{L_{\mathrm{rad}}}$ is nonzero.
